text: By the end of this section you should know:

locator: Driving along › Summary · item 1
text: How to steer and use your vehicle’s signalling system and hand signals

locator: Driving along › Summary · item 2
text: The importance of maintaining space and how to measure following distance

locator: Driving along › Summary · item 3
text: Where to position your vehicle on the road and to obey speed limits and police

locator: Driving efficiently › Intro · ¶1
text: Vehicles powered by gasoline and diesel give off air pollutants and gases such as oxides of carbon, nitrogen and sulphur, hydrocarbons and soot.

locator: Driving efficiently › Intro · ¶1
text: These pollutants affect the quality of the air we breathe, our health, crop yields and even the global climate.

locator: Driving efficiently › Intro · ¶2
text: Hydrocarbons and oxides of nitrogen react in sunlight to form ground-level ozone, better known as smog.

locator: Driving efficiently › Intro · ¶2
text: Smog is a major health hazard responsible for respiratory ailments and other illnesses.

locator: Driving efficiently › Intro · ¶2
text: Oxides of sulphur and nitrogen combine with water vapour to form acid rain, which damages our lakes, forests and crops.

locator: Driving efficiently › Intro · ¶3
text: Global warming is the result of too much carbon dioxide and other gases trapping heat in our atmosphere.

locator: Driving efficiently › Intro · ¶3
text: Global warming could cause average temperatures to rise, causing droughts, crop failures, lower water levels and more frequent and severe storms.

locator: Driving efficiently › Intro · ¶4
text: A car gives off less carbon dioxide than a larger vehicle, such as an airplane, truck, bus or train, does.

locator: Driving efficiently › Intro · ¶4
text: However, because so many people own cars and drive them so often, cars are responsible for nearly half the carbon dioxide produced by all forms of transportation.

locator: Driving efficiently › Intro · ¶4
text: Vehicles that carry large numbers of passengers, such as buses, produce less carbon dioxide per passenger than cars.

locator: Driving efficiently › Intro · ¶5
text: As a driver, you can help to protect the environment from the harmful effects of driving by following these suggestions.

locator: Driving efficiently › Intro · ¶5
text: Many of them can also save you money.

locator: Driving efficiently › Intro · ¶5
text: For further information visit the Fleetsmart website.

locator: Driving efficiently › Before you drive · item 1
text: Plan ahead.

locator: Driving efficiently › Before you drive · item 1
text: Combine several errands into one trip.

locator: Driving efficiently › Before you drive · item 2
text: Avoid driving during rush hours.

locator: Driving efficiently › Before you drive · item 2
text: Driving in off-peak times takes less time, uses less fuel and releases fewer emissions.

locator: Driving efficiently › Before you drive · item 3
text: Pay attention to smog alerts.

locator: Driving efficiently › Before you drive · item 3
text: It is especially important to follow these suggestions on days when smog is bad.

locator: Driving efficiently › Before you drive · item 4
text: For short trips, consider walking or cycling.

locator: Driving efficiently › Before you drive · item 5
text: For longer trips, public transit is an environmentally friendly alternative to driving alone.

locator: Driving efficiently › Before you drive · item 6
text: Carpool whenever possible.

locator: Driving efficiently › Before you drive · item 6
text: If you want to meet at a central location, there are free carpool lots in many parts of the province.

locator: Driving efficiently › While driving · item 1
text: Avoid starting your vehicle unnecessarily.

locator: Driving efficiently › While driving · item 1
text: A large burst of pollutants is emitted when a cold engine is started.

locator: Driving efficiently › While driving · item 2
text: Turn off your vehicle if parked more than 10 seconds.

locator: Driving efficiently › While driving · item 2
text: Even in cold weather, vehicle engines warm up within 30 seconds.

locator: Driving efficiently › While driving · item 3
text: Obey the speed limits.

locator: Driving efficiently › While driving · item 3
text: Driving at high speed uses more fuel and increases your chances of a serious collision.

locator: Driving efficiently › While driving · item 4
text: On the freeway, use your vehicle’s overdrive gear and cruise control for better fuel efficiency.

locator: Driving efficiently › While driving · item 5
text: Remove unnecessary weight from your vehicle, such as heavy baggage, wet snow and winter sand or salt.

locator: Driving efficiently › While driving · item 6
text: Maintain your vehicle’s aerodynamics.

locator: Driving efficiently › While driving · item 6
text: Remove roof racks and compartments when not in use.

locator: Driving efficiently › While driving · item 6
text: At high speeds, use your vents instead of opening the windows.

locator: Driving efficiently › While driving · item 7
text: Use your vehicle’s air conditioning wisely.

locator: Driving efficiently › While driving · item 7
text: Use your windows and vents in city and stop-and-go traffic.

locator: Driving efficiently › While driving · item 7
text: At high speeds, using your air conditioning is usually more fuel efficient than opening your windows and reducing the vehicle’s aerodynamics.

locator: Driving efficiently › While driving · item 8
text: Don't “top-off” the tank when refueling.

locator: Driving efficiently › While driving · item 8
text: Spilled fuel releases harmful vapours.

locator: Driving efficiently › At the garage · item 1
text: Regular maintenance will keep your vehicle running at maximum efficien­cy, reducing the fuel you need to buy and the pollutants your vehicle emits.

locator: Driving efficiently › At the garage · item 2
text: Keep your vehicle’s engine well tuned.

locator: Driving efficiently › At the garage · item 2
text: Worn spark plugs, dragging brakes, low transmission fluid or a transmission not going into high gear can increase fuel consumption substantially.

locator: Driving efficiently › At the garage · item 3
text: Follow the recommended maintenance schedule in your vehicle owner’s manual to maximize fuel efficiency.

locator: Driving efficiently › At the garage · item 4
text: Have any fluid leaks checked by a specialist to avoid engine damage and harming the environment.

locator: Driving efficiently › At the garage · item 5
text: Keep your tires properly inflated to reduce your fuel bill, emissions and tire wear.

locator: Driving efficiently › At the garage · item 6
text: Have your vehicle’s alignment checked regularly to reduce uneven tire wear and fuel consumption.

locator: Driving efficiently › At the garage · ¶1
text: (For more information on driving efficiently, see the section on maintaining your vehicle ).

locator: Driving efficiently › At the garage · ¶2
text: Drivers are reminded that many collisions occur when the driving environment is less than optimal.

locator: Driving efficiently › At the garage · ¶2
text: Whether driving at night, during times of reduced visibility or when road conditions are wet and slippery, drivers are encouraged to use the appropriate safe-driving tips provided in this handbook.

locator: Driving efficiently › 10 ways you can help make Ontario’s roads the safest in North America · item 1
text: Don't drink and drive.

locator: Driving efficiently › 10 ways you can help make Ontario’s roads the safest in North America · item 1
text: Don't drive when you're taking medication that will affect your driving.

locator: Driving efficiently › 10 ways you can help make Ontario’s roads the safest in North America · item 2
text: Always wear your seatbelt and make sure passengers are using the appropriate child car seat,booster seat or seatbelt.

locator: Driving efficiently › 10 ways you can help make Ontario’s roads the safest in North America · item 3
text: Obey the speed limits.

locator: Driving efficiently › 10 ways you can help make Ontario’s roads the safest in North America · item 3
text: Slow down when road and weather conditions are poor.

locator: Driving efficiently › 10 ways you can help make Ontario’s roads the safest in North America · item 4
text: Don't take risks: don't cut people off in traffic, make sudden lane changes or run yellow lights.

locator: Driving efficiently › 10 ways you can help make Ontario’s roads the safest in North America · item 5
text: Don't drive when you're tired, upset or sick.

locator: Driving efficiently › 10 ways you can help make Ontario’s roads the safest in North America · item 6
text: If you're in doubt, let the other driver go first - yield the right-of-way.

locator: Driving efficiently › 10 ways you can help make Ontario’s roads the safest in North America · item 7
text: Keep at least a two-second space between your vehicle and the one ahead.

locator: Driving efficiently › 10 ways you can help make Ontario’s roads the safest in North America · item 7
text: To check your distance: start counting when the vehicle ahead passes a fixed object, stop counting when your vehicle reaches the same spot.

locator: Driving efficiently › 10 ways you can help make Ontario’s roads the safest in North America · item 8
text: Cut the distractions: don't overcrowd the vehicle or play loud music.

locator: Driving efficiently › 10 ways you can help make Ontario’s roads the safest in North America · item 9
text: Always check your blind spot: look in your mirror and over your shoulder before you change lanes.

locator: Driving efficiently › 10 ways you can help make Ontario’s roads the safest in North America · item 10
text: Check traffic in all directions, including any sidewalks and paths/trails, before entering an intersection.

text: By the end of this section, you should know:

locator: Driving efficiently › Summary · item 1
text: How passenger vehicles affect the environment

locator: Driving efficiently › Summary · item 2
text: Ways to reduce the amount you drive

locator: Driving efficiently › Summary · item 3
text: Ways to conserve fuel and reduce emissions when you drive

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Intro · ¶1
text: At night and in weather conditions such as rain, snow or fog, you cannot see as far ahead, even with headlights.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Intro · ¶1
text: Slow down when driving at night, especially on unlit roads and whenever weather conditions reduce your visibility.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Overdriving your headlights · ¶1
text: You are overdriving your headlights when you go so fast that your stopping distance is farther than you can see with your headlights.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Overdriving your headlights · ¶1
text: This is a dangerous thing to do, because you may not give yourself enough room to make a safe stop.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Overdriving your headlights · ¶1
text: Reflective road signs can mislead you as well, making you believe you can see farther than you really can.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Overdriving your headlights · ¶1
text: This may cause you to over-drive your headlights if you are not careful (Diagram 2-58).

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Glare · ¶1
text: Glare is dazzling light that makes it hard for you to see and be aware what others around you are doing.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Glare · ¶1
text: It can be a problem on both sunny and overcast days, depending on the angle of the sun’s rays and your surroundings.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Glare · ¶1
text: Glare can also be a problem at night when you face bright headlights or see them reflected in your rear view mirror.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Glare · ¶2
text: When meeting oncoming vehicles with bright headlights at night, look up and beyond and slightly to the right of the oncoming lights.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Glare · ¶2
text: In daytime glare, use your sun visor or keep a pair of good quality sunglasses in your vehicle.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Glare · ¶2
text: When you enter a tunnel on a bright day, slow down to let your eyes adjust to the reduced light.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Glare · ¶2
text: Remove your sunglasses and turn on your headlights.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Glare · ¶3
text: Cut down glare at night by following the rules of the road for vehicle lights.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Glare · ¶3
text: Use your low-beam headlights within 150 metres of an oncoming vehicle or when following a vehicle within 60 metres.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Glare · ¶3
text: On country roads, switch to low beams when you come to a curve or hilltop so you can see oncoming headlights and won't blind oncoming drivers.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Glare · ¶3
text: If you can't see any headlights, switch back to high beams.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog · ¶1
text: Fog is a thin layer of cloud resting on the ground.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog · ¶1
text: Fog can reduce visibility for drivers, resulting in difficult driving conditions.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog · ¶2
text: The best thing to do is to avoid driving in fog.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog · ¶2
text: Check weather forecasts and if there is a fog warning, delay your trip until it clears.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog · ¶2
text: If that is not possible or you get caught driving in fog, there are a number of safe driving tips you should follow.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog · ¶2
text: If visibility is decreasing rapidly, move off the road and into a safe parking area to wait for the fog to lift.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog · ¶1
text: Before you drive - and during your trip - check weather forecasts.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog · ¶1
text: If there is a fog warning, delay your trip until it clears.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog · ¶1
text: If you are caught driving in fog, follow these safe-driving tips:

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › DO: · item 1
text: Slow down gradually and drive at a speed that suits the conditions.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › DO: · item 2
text: Make sure the full lighting system of your vehicle is turned on.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › DO: · item 3
text: Use your low-beam headlights.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › DO: · item 3
text: High beams reflect off the moisture droplets in the fog, making it harder to see.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › DO: · item 4
text: If you have fog lights on your vehicle, use them, in addition to your low beams.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › DO: · item 5
text: Be patient.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › DO: · item 5
text: Avoid passing, changing lanes and crossing traffic.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › DO: · item 6
text: Use pavement markings to help guide you.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › DO: · item 6
text: Use the right edge of the road as a guide, rather than the centre line.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › DO: · item 7
text: Increase your following distance.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › DO: · item 7
text: You will need extra distance to brake safely.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › DO: · item 8
text: Look and listen for any hazards that may be ahead.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › DO: · item 9
text: Reduce the distractions in your vehicle.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › DO: · item 9
text: For example, turn off the cell phone.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › DO: · item 9
text: Your full attention is required.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › DO: · item 10
text: Watch for any electronically operated warning signs.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › DO: · item 11
text: Keep looking as far ahead as possible.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › DO: · item 12
text: Keep your windows and mirrors clean.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › DO: · item 12
text: Use your defroster and wipers to maximize your vision.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › DO: · item 13
text: If the fog is too dense to continue, pull completely off the road and try to position your vehicle in a safe parking area.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › DO: · item 13
text: Turn on your emergency flashers, in addition to keeping on your low-beam headlights.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › Don’t: · item 1
text: Don't stop on the travelled portion of the road.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › Don’t: · item 1
text: You could become the first link in a chain-reaction collision.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › Don’t: · item 2
text: Don't speed up suddenly, even if the fog seems to be clearing.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › Don’t: · item 2
text: You could find yourself suddenly back in fog.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › Don’t: · item 3
text: Don't speed up to pass a vehicle moving slowly or to get away from a vehicle that is following too closely.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › REMEMBER: · item 1
text: Watch your speed.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › REMEMBER: · item 1
text: You may be going faster than you think.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › REMEMBER: · item 1
text: If so, reduce speed gradually.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › REMEMBER: · item 2
text: Leave a safe braking distance between you and the vehicle ahead.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › REMEMBER: · item 3
text: Remain calm and patient.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › REMEMBER: · item 3
text: Don't pass other vehicles or speed up suddenly.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › REMEMBER: · item 4
text: Don't stop on the road.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › REMEMBER: · item 4
text: If visibility is decreasing rapidly, pull off the road into a safe parking area and wait for the fog to lift.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Fog › Tips for driving safely in fog › REMEMBER: · item 5
text: Use your low-beam lights.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Rain · ¶1
text: Rain makes road surfaces slippery, especially as the first drops fall.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Rain · ¶1
text: With more rain, tires make less contact with the road.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Rain · ¶1
text: If there is too much water or if you are going too fast, your tires may ride on top of the water, like water skis.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Rain · ¶1
text: This is called hydroplaning.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Rain · ¶1
text: When this happens, control becomes very difficult.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Rain · ¶1
text: Make sure you have good tires with deep tread, and slow down when the road is wet.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Rain · ¶2
text: Rain also reduces visibility.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Rain · ¶2
text: Drive slowly enough to be able to stop within the distance you can see.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Rain · ¶2
text: Make sure your windshield wipers are in good condition.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Rain · ¶2
text: If your wiper blades do not clean the windshield without streaking, replace them.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Rain · ¶3
text: In rain, try to drive on clear sections of road.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Rain · ¶3
text: Look ahead and plan your movements.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Rain · ¶3
text: Smooth steering, braking and accelerating will reduce the chance of skids Leave more space between you and the vehicle ahead in case you have to stop.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Rain · ¶3
text: This will also help you to avoid spray from the vehicle ahead that can make it even harder to see.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Rain · ¶4
text: Avoid driving in puddles.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Rain · ¶4
text: A puddle can hide a large pothole that could damage your vehicle or its suspension, or flatten a tire.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Rain · ¶4
text: The spray of water could obstruct the vision of adjacent motorists and result in a collision, cause harm to nearby pedestrians or drown your engine, causing it to stall.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Rain · ¶4
text: Water can also make your brakes less effective.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Flooded roads · ¶1
text: Avoid driving on flooded roads, water may prevent your brakes from working.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Flooded roads · ¶1
text: If you must drive through a flooded stretch of road, test your brakes afterward to dry them out.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Flooded roads · ¶1
text: Test your brakes when it is safe to do so by stopping quickly and firmly at 50 km/h. Make sure the vehicle stops in a straight line, without pulling to one side.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Flooded roads · ¶1
text: The brake pedal should feel firm and secure, not spongy, that’s a sign of trouble.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Flooded roads · ¶1
text: If you still feel a pulling to one side or a spongy brake pedal even after the brakes are dry, you should take the vehicle in for repair immediately.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids · ¶1
text: A skid may happen when one or more tires lose their grip with the road’s surface.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids · ¶1
text: Skids most often happen on a slippery surface, such as a road that is wet, icy or covered with snow, gravel or some other loose material.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids · ¶1
text: Most skids result from driving too fast for road conditions.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids · ¶1
text: Hard braking and overly aggressive turning or accelerating can cause your vehicle to skid and possibly go out of control.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids · ¶2
text: To avoid a skid on a slippery road, drive at a reduced speed and operate the vehicle’s controls in a smooth and constrained manner.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids · ¶2
text: Increasing tire forces, such as by braking or accelerating while steering may push tires even closer to a skid condition.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids · ¶2
text: It’s essential that the vehicle’s speed be maintained at a safe level and that turns be made gently.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids · ¶3
text: If your vehicle begins to skid, try not to panic - it is possible to maintain control of your vehicle, even in a skid.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids · ¶3
text: Ease off on the accelerator or brake and on a very slippery surface slip the transmission into neutral if you can.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids · ¶3
text: Continue to steer in the direction you wish to go.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids · ¶3
text: Be careful not to oversteer.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids · ¶3
text: Once you regain control, you can brake as needed, but very gently and smoothly.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids › Anti-lock braking systems (ABS) · ¶1
text: If your vehicle is equipped with anti-lock brakes, practise emergency braking to understand how your vehicle will react.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids › Anti-lock braking systems (ABS) · ¶1
text: It is a good idea to practise doing this under controlled conditions with a qualified driving instructor.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids › Anti-lock braking systems (ABS) · ¶2
text: ABS is designed to sense the speed of the wheels on a vehicle during braking.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids › Anti-lock braking systems (ABS) · ¶2
text: An abnormal drop in wheel speed, which indicates potential wheel lock, causes the brake force to be reduced to that wheel.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids › Anti-lock braking systems (ABS) · ¶2
text: This is how ABS prevents tire skid and the accompanying loss of steering control.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids › Anti-lock braking systems (ABS) · ¶2
text: This improves vehicle safety during heavy brake use or when braking with poor traction.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids › Anti-lock braking systems (ABS) · ¶3
text: Although anti-lock braking systems help to prevent wheel lock, you should not expect the stopping distance for your vehicle to be shortened.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids › Anti-lock braking systems (ABS) · ¶4
text: Drivers unfamiliar with anti-lock braking may be surprised by the pulsations that they may feel in the brake pedal when they brake hard.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids › Anti-lock braking systems (ABS) · ¶4
text: Make sure you know what to expect so you will not be distracted by the pulsation or tempted to release the pedal during emergency braking manoeuvres.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids › Threshold braking · ¶1
text: Threshold braking should bring you to a reasonably quick controlled stop in your own lane, even in slippery conditions.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids › Threshold braking · ¶1
text: This technique is generally practised in a vehicle that is not equipped with ABS .

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids › Threshold braking · ¶1
text: Brake as hard as you can until a wheel begins to lock up, then release pressure on the pedal slightly to release the wheel.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids › Threshold braking · ¶1
text: Press down on the brake pedal, applying as much braking force as possible without inducing a skid.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids › Threshold braking · ¶1
text: If you feel any of the wheels begin to lock up, release the brake pressure slightly and re-apply.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids › Threshold braking · ¶1
text: Don't pump the brakes.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids › Threshold braking · ¶1
text: Continue braking this way until you have slowed the vehicle to the desired speed.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids › Threshold braking · ¶2
text: Vehicles equipped with ABS should provide controlled braking on slippery surfaces automatically.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Skids › Threshold braking · ¶2
text: Press the brake pedal hard and allow the system to control wheel lock-up.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Snow · ¶1
text: Snow may be hard-packed and slippery as ice; rutted, full of hard tracks and gullies; or smooth and soft.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Snow · ¶1
text: Look ahead and anticipate what you must do based on the conditions.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Snow · ¶1
text: Slow down on rutted, snowy roads.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Snow · ¶1
text: Avoid sudden steering, braking or accelerating that could cause a skid.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Snow · ¶1
text: Do not use cruise control during times of snow and other inclement weather.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Whiteouts · ¶1
text: Blowing snow may create whiteouts where snow completely blocks your view of the road.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Whiteouts · ¶1
text: When blowing snow is forecast, drive only if necessary and with extreme caution.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Whiteouts › Tips for driving in blowing snow and whiteout conditions · ¶1
text: Before you drive - and during your trip - check weather forecasts and road reports.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Whiteouts › Tips for driving in blowing snow and whiteout conditions · ¶1
text: If there is a weather warning, or reports of poor visibility and driving conditions, delay your trip until conditions improve, if possible.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Whiteouts › Tips for driving in blowing snow and whiteout conditions · ¶1
text: If you get caught driving in blowing snow or a whiteout, follow these safe driving tips:

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Whiteouts › Tips for driving in blowing snow and whiteout conditions › DO: · item 1
text: Slow down gradually and drive at a speed that suits the conditions.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Whiteouts › Tips for driving in blowing snow and whiteout conditions › DO: · item 2
text: Make sure the full lighting system of your vehicle is turned on.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Whiteouts › Tips for driving in blowing snow and whiteout conditions › DO: · item 3
text: Use your low-beam headlights.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Whiteouts › Tips for driving in blowing snow and whiteout conditions › DO: · item 3
text: High beams reflect off the ice particles in the snow, making it harder to see.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Whiteouts › Tips for driving in blowing snow and whiteout conditions › DO: · item 9

text: Don't attempt to pass a vehicle moving slowly or speed up to get away from a vehicle that is following too closely.

text: Watch your speed.

text: You may be going faster than you think.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Whiteouts › Tips for driving in blowing snow and whiteout conditions › REMEMBER: · item 1
text: If so, reduce speed gradually.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Whiteouts › Tips for driving in blowing snow and whiteout conditions › REMEMBER: · item 2
text: Leave a safe braking distance between you and the vehicle ahead.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Whiteouts › Tips for driving in blowing snow and whiteout conditions › REMEMBER: · item 3

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Whiteouts › Tips for driving in blowing snow and whiteout conditions › REMEMBER: · item 5

text: Open a window slightly for ventilation.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Whiteouts › Tips for driving in blowing snow and whiteout conditions › REMEMBER: · item 5

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Whiteouts › Tips for driving in blowing snow and whiteout conditions › REMEMBER: · item 5
text: Use your emergency flashers.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Whiteouts › Tips for driving in blowing snow and whiteout conditions › REMEMBER: · item 6
text: Be prepared and carry a winter driving survival kit that includes items such as warm clothing, non-perishable energy foods, flashlight, shovel and blanket.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Whiteouts › Tips for driving in blowing snow and whiteout conditions › REMEMBER: · item 7
text: It is important to look ahead and watch for clues that indicate you need to slow down and anticipate slippery road conditions.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Ice · ¶1
text: As temperatures drop below freezing, wet roads become icy.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Ice · ¶1
text: Sections of road in shaded areas or on bridges and overpasses freeze first.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Ice · ¶1
text: It is important to look ahead, slow down and anticipate ice.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Ice · ¶1
text: If the road ahead looks like black and shiny asphalt, be suspicious.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Ice · ¶1
text: It may be covered by a thin layer of ice known as black ice.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Ice · ¶1
text: Generally, asphalt in the winter should look gray-white in colour.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Ice · ¶1
text: If you think there may be black ice ahead, slow down and be careful.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Snow plows · ¶1
text: Snow-removal vehicles on public roadways are equipped with flashing blue lights that can be seen from 150 metres.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Snow plows · ¶2
text: Flashing blue lights warn you of wide and slow-moving vehicles: some snow plows have a wing that extends as far as three metres to the right of the vehicle.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Snow plows · ¶2
text: On freeways, several snow plows may be staggered across the road, clearing all lanes at the same time by passing a ridge of snow from plow to plow.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Snow plows · ¶2
text: Do not try to pass between them.

locator: Driving at night and in bad weather › Snow plows · ¶2
text: This is extremely dangerous because there is not enough room to pass safely, and the ridge of wet snow can throw your vehicle out of control.

locator: Driving through intersections › Intro · ¶1
text: Be alert as you come to intersections and look carefully for pedestrians, cyclists, other motor vehicles, yield signs, stop signs and traffic lights.

locator: Driving through intersections › Intro · ¶1
text: Be sure to scan any sidewalks and paths/trails as well as the roadways.

locator: Driving through intersections › Intro · ¶1
text: Bear in mind that children are often unaware of traffic laws and also that cycling on the sidewalk may be permitted by local bylaw.

locator: Driving through intersections › Intro · ¶2
text: There are two main types of intersections: controlled and uncontrolled.

locator: Driving through intersections › Controlled intersections · ¶1
text: Controlled intersections have traffic lights, yield signs or stop signs to control traffic (Diagram 2-19).

locator: Driving through intersections › Controlled intersections · ¶2
text: At a controlled intersection where you face a green light, drive carefully through the intersection at a steady speed.

locator: Driving through intersections › Controlled intersections · ¶2
text: If the light has been green for a while, be prepared to stop when it turns yellow.

locator: Driving through intersections › Controlled intersections · ¶2
text: However, if you are already so close that you cannot stop safely, drive through the intersection with caution.

locator: Driving through intersections › Controlled intersections · ¶2
text: Where you face a red light, come to a complete stop and wait until the light turns green.

locator: Driving through intersections › Controlled intersections · ¶3
text: When you approach an intersection on a main road, and the intersection is blocked with traffic, stop before entering the intersection and wait until the traffic ahead moves on.

locator: Driving through intersections › Controlled intersections · ¶3
text: This does not apply if you are turning left or right.

locator: Driving through intersections › Controlled intersections · ¶4
text: At a controlled intersection where you face a yield sign, slow down or stop if necessary and wait until the way is clear before driving through the intersection.

locator: Driving through intersections › Controlled intersections · ¶5
text: At a controlled intersection where you face a stop sign, come to a complete stop.

locator: Driving through intersections › Controlled intersections · ¶5
text: Drive through the intersection only when the way is clear (Diagram 2-19).

locator: Driving through intersections › Uncontrolled intersections · ¶1
text: Uncontrolled intersections have no signs or traffic lights.

locator: Driving through intersections › Uncontrolled intersections · ¶1
text: They are usually found in areas where there is not much traffic.

locator: Driving through intersections › Uncontrolled intersections · ¶1
text: Be extra careful around these intersections.

locator: Driving through intersections › Uncontrolled intersections · ¶1
text: If two vehicles come to an uncontrolled intersection from different roads at the same time, the driver on the left must let the driver on the right go first.

locator: Driving through intersections › Uncontrolled intersections · ¶1
text: This is called yielding the right-of-way.

locator: Driving through intersections › Yielding the right-of-way · ¶1
text: There are times when you must yield the right-of-way.

locator: Driving through intersections › Yielding the right-of-way · ¶1
text: This means you must let another driver go first.

locator: Driving through intersections › Yielding the right-of-way · ¶1
text: Here are some rules about when you must yield the right-of-way.

locator: Driving through intersections › Yielding the right-of-way · ¶2
text: At an intersection without signs or lights, you must yield the right-of-way to a vehicle approaching the intersection before you, and if you arrive at the same time, the vehicle approaching from the right has the right-of-way (Diagram 2-18).

locator: Driving through intersections › Yielding the right-of-way · ¶3
text: At an intersection with stop signs at all corners, you must yield the right-of-way to the first vehicle to come to a complete stop.

locator: Driving through intersections › Yielding the right-of-way · ¶3
text: If two vehicles stop at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right (Diagram 2-19).

locator: Driving through intersections › Yielding the right-of-way · ¶4
text: At any intersection where you want to turn left or right, you must yield the right-of-way.

locator: Driving through intersections › Yielding the right-of-way · ¶4
text: If you are turning left, you must wait for approaching traffic to pass or turn and for pedestrians in or approaching your path to cross.

locator: Driving through intersections › Yielding the right-of-way · ¶4
text: If you are turning right, you must wait for pedestrians to cross if they are in or approaching your path (Diagram 2-20).

locator: Driving through intersections › Yielding the right-of-way · ¶4
text: You should also check your blind spot for cyclists approaching from behind, particularly in a bike lane to your right, on a sidewalk or a trail.

locator: Driving through intersections › Yielding the right-of-way · ¶4
text: A yield sign means you must slow down or stop if necessary and yield the right-of-way to traffic in the intersection or on the intersecting road.

locator: Driving through intersections › Yielding the right-of-way · ¶5
text: When entering a road from a private road or driveway, you must yield to vehicles on the road and pedestrians on the sidewalk (Diagram 2-21).

locator: Driving through intersections › Yielding the right-of-way · ¶6
text: You must yield the right-of-way and wait for pedestrians to completely cross the road at pedestrian crossovers (Diagram 2-22) and school crossings with crossing guards.

locator: Driving through intersections › Yielding the right-of-way · ¶7
text: Remember, signalling does not give you the right-of-way.

locator: Driving through intersections › Yielding the right-of-way · ¶7
text: You must make sure the way is clear.

locator: Freeway driving › Intro · ¶1
text: A freeway - also called an expressway - is a high-speed, multi-lane road.

locator: Freeway driving › Intro · ¶1
text: On a freeway, traffic going in each direction is separated and ramps let vehicles enter and exit.

locator: Freeway driving › Intro · ¶1
text: Vehicle speed is higher on a freeway than on other roads, so driving can be more demanding and difficult.

locator: Freeway driving › Intro · ¶1
text: However, because there are no intersections, bicycles or pedestrians, freeway driving can be safer for experienced drivers.

locator: Freeway driving › Intro · ¶2
text: Lanes called High Occupancy Vehicle ( HOV ) lanes are to be used for:

locator: Freeway driving › Intro · item 1
text: vehicles carrying at least two people

locator: Freeway driving › Intro · item 2
text: buses

locator: Freeway driving › Intro · item 3
text: licensed taxis

locator: Freeway driving › Intro · item 4
text: green‑plate vehicles

locator: Freeway driving › Intro · item 5
text: airport limousines

locator: Freeway driving › Intro · item 6
text: motorcycles

locator: Freeway driving › Intro · item 7
text: High-Occupancy Toll ( HOT ) permit holders (where permitted)

locator: Freeway driving › Intro · item 8
text: emergency vehicles

locator: Freeway driving › Intro · ¶3
text: You will need to learn how to recognize markings and signs for these lanes, and the rules for using them.

locator: Freeway driving › Intro · ¶4
text: New drivers need to learn how to drive with other vehicles around them at low speeds before trying freeway driving.

locator: Freeway driving › Intro · ¶4
text: Class G1 drivers may only drive on freeways with a licensed driving instructor.

locator: Freeway driving › Entering a freeway · ¶1
text: There are usually two parts to a freeway entrance: an entrance ramp and an acceleration lane.

locator: Freeway driving › Entering a freeway · ¶2
text: As you move along the freeway entrance ramp, look ahead and check your mirrors and blind spots to assess the traffic to see where you will move into the nearest freeway lane.

locator: Freeway driving › Entering a freeway · ¶3
text: As you leave the ramp you enter the acceleration lane.

locator: Freeway driving › Entering a freeway · ¶3
text: In the acceleration lane, drivers increase their speed to the speed of traffic on the freeway before they merge with it.

locator: Freeway driving › Entering a freeway · ¶3
text: Signal and increase your speed to merge smoothly with traffic.

locator: Freeway driving › Entering a freeway · ¶3
text: Freeway drivers should move over, if it is safe to do so, leaving room for merging vehicles.

locator: Freeway driving › Entering a freeway · ¶4
text: A few entrance ramps join the freeway on the left.

locator: Freeway driving › Entering a freeway · ¶4
text: This means you enter the fastest lane of traffic first.

locator: Freeway driving › Entering a freeway · ¶4
text: Use the acceleration lane to match your speed to the traffic, increasing your speed more quickly.

locator: Freeway driving › Driving along a freeway · ¶1
text: Once on the freeway, a safe driver travels at a steady speed, looking forward and anticipating what’s going to happen on the road ahead.

locator: Freeway driving › Driving along a freeway · ¶1
text: Traffic should keep to the right, using the left lanes for passing.

locator: Freeway driving › Driving along a freeway · ¶2
text: As in city driving, your eyes should be constantly moving, scanning the road ahead, to each side and behind.

locator: Freeway driving › Driving along a freeway · ¶2
text: Look ahead to where you are going to be in the next 15 to 20 seconds, or as far ahead as you can see, when you travel at faster speeds.

locator: Freeway driving › Driving along a freeway · ¶2
text: Remember to keep scanning and check your mirrors frequently.

locator: Freeway driving › Driving along a freeway · ¶3
text: Stay clear of large vehicles.

locator: Freeway driving › Driving along a freeway · ¶3
text: Because of their size, they block your view more than other vehicles.

locator: Freeway driving › Driving along a freeway · ¶3
text: Leave space around your vehicle.

locator: Freeway driving › Driving along a freeway · ¶3
text: This will let you see clearly in every direction and will give you time and space to react.

locator: Freeway driving › Driving along a freeway · ¶3
text: Learn more about following distances.

locator: Freeway driving › Driving along a freeway · ¶4
text: Be careful not to cut off any vehicle, large or small, when making a lane change or joining the flow of traffic.

locator: Freeway driving › Driving along a freeway · ¶4
text: It is dangerous and illegal for a slower moving vehicle to cut in front of a faster moving vehicle.

locator: Freeway driving › Driving along a freeway · ¶5
text: Use the far left lane of a multi-lane freeway to pass traffic moving slower than the speed limit, but don't stay there.

locator: Freeway driving › Driving along a freeway · ¶5
text: Drive in the right-hand lane when possible.

locator: Freeway driving › Driving along a freeway · ¶5
text: On many freeways with three or more lanes in each direction, large trucks cannot travel in the far left lane and must use the lane to the right for passing.

locator: Freeway driving › Driving along a freeway · ¶5
text: Get into the habit of driving in the right lane, leaving the other lanes clear for passing.

locator: Freeway driving › Leaving a freeway · ¶1
text: There are usually three parts to a freeway exit: a deceleration lane for slowing down that leads drivers out of the main flow of traffic, an exit ramp and an intersection with a stop sign, yield sign or traffic light.

locator: Freeway driving › Leaving a freeway · ¶1
text: When leaving the freeway, signal that you want to move into the decelera­tion lane, but do not slow down.

locator: Freeway driving › Leaving a freeway · ¶1
text: When you are in the lane, reduce your speed gradually to the speed shown for the exit ramp.

locator: Freeway driving › Leaving a freeway · ¶1
text: Check your speedometer to make sure you are going slowly enough.

locator: Freeway driving › Leaving a freeway · ¶1
text: You may not realize how fast you are going because you are used to the high speed of the freeway.

locator: Freeway driving › Leaving a freeway · ¶1
text: Losing your ability to judge your speed accurately is sometimes called speed adaptation or velocitization.

locator: Freeway driving › Leaving a freeway · ¶1
text: It is a special danger when leaving a freeway.

locator: Freeway driving › Leaving a freeway · ¶1
text: Be prepared to stop at the end of the exit ramp.

locator: Freeway driving › Leaving a freeway · ¶2
text: Signs telling you that there are freeway exits ahead are far enough in advance for you to make any lane changes safely.

locator: Freeway driving › Leaving a freeway · ¶2
text: If you miss an exit, do not stop or reverse on the freeway.

locator: Freeway driving › Leaving a freeway · ¶2
text: Take the next exit.

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · ¶1
text: A High-Occupancy Vehicle ( HOV ) lane is a specially designed lane that is designated for use by certain types of vehicles with a specified number of occupants.

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · ¶1
text: It can offer travel-time savings to those who choose to carpool or take transit.

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · ¶1
text: HOV lanes can move a greater number of people than a general traffic lane, and encourage carpooling and transit use by providing travel-time savings and a more reliable trip time.

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · ¶1
text: HOV lanes are open 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · ¶2
text: HOV lanes benefit all drivers, not only those who carpool, in the following ways:

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · item 1
text: Improves highway infrastructure by moving more people in fewer cars

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · item 2
text: Reduces the number of vehicles on the road

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · item 3
text: Reduces overall emissions and improves air quality

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · ¶3
text: HOV lanes on provincial highways are reserved for:

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · item 4
text: vehicles carrying at least two people

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · item 5
text: buses

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · item 6
text: licensed taxis

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · item 7
text: green‑plate vehicles

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · item 8
text: airport limousines

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · item 9
text: motorcycles

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · item 10
text: High-Occupancy Toll (HOT) permit holders (where permitted)

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · item 11
text: emergency vehicles

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · ¶4
text: Large trucks are not permitted on the HOV lanes, regardless of the number of occupants.

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · item 12
text: The HOV lane is separated from the other general traffic lanes by a striped buffer zone.

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · item 12
text: It is illegal and unsafe to cross the striped buffer pavement markings.

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · item 13
text: Certain vehicles are exempt from the HOV lane rules.

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · item 13
text: Buses can use an HOV lane at any time, regardless of the number of occupants.

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · item 13
text: Emergency vehicles such as police, fire and ambulance are also exempt from the restrictions.

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · item 14
text: If you use the HOV lanes improperly, you can be stopped and ticketed by a police officer.

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · item 14
text: You will be required to re-enter the general lanes at the next entry/exit zone.

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · item 15
text: Commercial motor vehicles must have two or more people in the vehicle and be less than 6.5 metres in total length to be in the HOV lane.

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · item 15
text: Single-occupant taxis and airport limousines are permitted in the HOV lane.

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · item 15
text: Vehicles with the “Green” licence plate are permitted in the HOV lane with any number of occupants.

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · item 15
text: Green plates are available for eligible plug-in hybrid electric vehicles and full-battery electric vehicles.

locator: Freeway driving › High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) Lane · item 15
text: Please consult the Ministry of Transportation website for more details.
