locator: The Level Two Road Test › Intro · ¶1
text: Statistics show that new drivers of all ages are far more likely than experienced drivers to be involved in serious or fatal collisions.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Intro · ¶2
text: To help new drivers develop better, safer driving habits, Ontario introduced graduated licensing in 1994 for all drivers applying for their first car or motorcycle licence.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Intro · ¶2
text: Graduated licensing lets you gain driving skills and experience gradually, in lower-risk environments.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Intro · ¶2
text: The two-step licensing system takes at least 20 months to complete and includes two road tests.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Intro · ¶2
text: Passing the Level Two (G2) road test gives you full Class G driving privileges.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Intro · ¶3
text: While the Level One road test deals with basic driving skills, the Level Two deals with advanced knowledge and skills that are generally gained with driving experience.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Intro · ¶3
text: When you take the test, the examiner will give you directions.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Intro · ¶3
text: As you complete the driving tasks, the examiner will watch to make sure you successfully perform the actions associated with them.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Intro · ¶4
text: The G2 road test includes a component of expressway driving.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Intro · ¶4
text: In order to reschedule, you will have to pay the 50 per cent of the road-test fee lost through the out-of-order.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Intro · ¶4
text: Make sure you obtain the required highway driving experience before rescheduling your test.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Intro · ¶4
text: To proceed, you must complete and sign a “Declaration of Highway Driving Experience” to ensure that you have sufficient expressway driving experience to complete this component.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Intro · ¶4
text: On the form, you will indicates how many times in the three months before the road test you have driven on a freeway and/or a highway with a speed limit of at least 80 km/h .

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Intro · ¶4
text: You are required to indicate what was the average length of these trips (for example, under 5 kilometres, between 5 and 15 kilometres, over 15 kilometres).

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Intro · ¶4
text: Freeways include: 400, 401, 402, 403, 404, 405, 406, 407, 409, 410, 416, 417, 420, 427, Queen Elizabeth Way, Don Valley Parkway, Gardiner Expressway, E.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Intro · ¶4
text: C.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Intro · ¶4
text: Row Expressway and the Conestoga Parkway.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Intro · ¶4
text: If you do not have sufficient highway driving experience, the examiner must declare the road test “out-of-order” and cancel it.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Intro · ¶4
text: You will lose 50 per cent of your prepaid road-test fee.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Intro · ¶5
text: To help you prepare, this chapter tells you the various tasks and actions that you will be expected to perform in your Level Two road test.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Intro · ¶5
text: This is only a guide.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Intro · ¶5
text: For more information on the driving tasks, you should review chapters 2 and 3.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Intro · ¶6
text: Until further notice, the G road test will not include these elements that are already covered in the G2 road test: parallel parking roadside stops 3-point turn driving in residential neighbourhoods The test will still include all of the fundamental elements such as: driving on major roads and expressways including merging on and off, maintaining appropriate speed and space, signalling and more turns, curves and lane changes intersections driving in business areas Learn more about what’s included in the G road test .

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › The approach · ¶1
text: This driving task begins when the examiner tells you to make a left or right turn, and ends at the point just before you enter the intersection.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › The approach · ¶1
text: Make sure you take the following actions:

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › The approach › Traffic check · ¶1
text: Before slowing down, look all around you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › The approach › Traffic check · ¶1
text: Use your rearview and side mirrors to check traffic behind you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › The approach › Traffic check · ¶1
text: If you change lanes, remember to check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › The approach › Lane · ¶1
text: Move into the far left or far right lane as soon as the way is clear.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › The approach › Signal · ¶1
text: Turn on your signal before slowing down for the turn, unless there are vehicles waiting to enter the road from side roads or driveways between you and the intersection.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › The approach › Signal · ¶1
text: Wait until you have passed these entrances so that drivers will not think you are turning before the intersection.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › The approach › Speed · ¶1
text: Steadily reduce speed as you approach the turn.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › The approach › Speed · ¶1
text: In a vehicle with manual transmission, you may downshift into a lower gear as you slow down.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › The approach › Speed · ¶1
text: Do not coast with your foot on the clutch pedal.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › The approach › Space · ¶1
text: While slowing down, keep at least a two to three-second distance behind the vehicle in front of you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › If stopped · ¶1
text: You will need to do this driving task if you cannot complete your turn without stopping, either because the way is not clear or you face a stop sign or red traffic light.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › If stopped · ¶1
text: Remember to follow these actions:

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › If stopped › Stop · ¶1
text: Come to a complete stop.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › If stopped › Stop · ¶1
text: Do not let your vehicle roll forward or backward.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › If stopped › Stop · ¶1
text: When traffic conditions allow, move forward to check that the way is clear or to start the turn.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › If stopped › Stop · ¶1
text: If you have to stop after you have passed the stop line, do not back up.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › If stopped › Space · ¶1
text: When stopped behind another vehicle at an intersection, leave enough space to pull out and pass without having to back up.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › If stopped › Space · ¶1
text: Leaving this space protects you in three ways: it lets you pull around the vehicle in front if it stalls; it helps prevent you from being pushed into the vehicle ahead if you are hit from behind; and it reduces the risk of collision if the vehicle ahead rolls backward or backs up.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › If stopped › Stop line · ¶1
text: If you are the first vehicle approaching an intersection with a red light or stop sign, stop behind the stop line if it is marked on the pavement.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › If stopped › Stop line · ¶1
text: If there is no stop line, stop at the crosswalk, marked or not.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › If stopped › Stop line · ¶1
text: If there is no crosswalk, stop at the edge of the sidewalk.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › If stopped › Stop line · ¶1
text: If there is no sidewalk, stop at the edge of the intersection.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › If stopped › Wheels · ¶1
text: When waiting to make a left turn, keep your front wheels straight.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › If stopped › Wheels · ¶1
text: With your wheels turned left, your vehicle could be pushed into oncoming traffic.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › If stopped › Wheels · ¶1
text: When waiting to turn right, keep the wheels straight if there is a risk of being pushed into pedestrians crossing the intersection.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › If stopped › Wheels · ¶1
text: At a large intersection with curved sidewalks where you are turning right, angle your vehicle to follow the curb so that no other vehi­cle can fit between you and the curb.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Making the turn · ¶1
text: The driving task involves your actions as you make the turn.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Making the turn · ¶1
text: Remember to do the following:

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Making the turn › Traffic check · ¶1
text: If you are stopped, waiting for a green light or for the way to be clear, keep checking traffic all around you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Making the turn › Traffic check · ¶1
text: Just before entering the intersection, look left, ahead and right to check that the way is clear.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Making the turn › Traffic check · ¶1
text: If there is any doubt about the right-of-way, try to make eye contact with nearby drivers or pedestrians.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Making the turn › Traffic check · ¶1
text: If it is possible for another vehicle to overtake you while you are turning, check your blind spot before starting to turn.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Making the turn › Traffic check · ¶1
text: You have not properly checked traffic if another vehicle or pedestrian has the right-of-way and must take action to avoid your vehicle.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Making the turn › Both hands · ¶1
text: Use both hands to turn the steering wheel throughout the turn.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Making the turn › Both hands · ¶1
text: You are most at risk from other traffic when turning.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Making the turn › Both hands · ¶1
text: Using both hands on the wheel gives you maximum steering control when you need it most.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Making the turn › Both hands · ¶1
text: An exception to this is if you have a disability that prevents you from using both hands.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Making the turn › Gears · ¶1
text: In a vehicle with manual transmission, do not shift gears during the turn.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Making the turn › Gears · ¶1
text: If you need to, you may shift gears immediately after the vehicle is moving but before it is well into the turn.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Making the turn › Gears · ¶1
text: You may also shift gears in an intersection wider than four lanes if not doing so would slow down other traffic.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Making the turn › Gears · ¶1
text: Generally, not changing gears gives you more control over your vehicle when turning.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Making the turn › Speed · ¶1
text: Move ahead within four to five seconds after it is safe to start.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Making the turn › Speed · ¶1
text: Make the turn at a steady speed, increasing speed as you complete the turn.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Making the turn › Speed · ¶1
text: Drive slowly enough to keep full control of your vehicle without slowing down other traffic.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Making the turn › Wide/short · ¶1
text: Turn into the corresponding lane on the intersecting road without going over any lane markings or curbs.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Completing the turn · ¶1
text: This driving task completes the turn.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Completing the turn · ¶1
text: It begins when you enter the intersecting road and ends when you return to normal traffic speed.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Completing the turn · ¶1
text: Take the following actions:

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Completing the turn › Lane · ¶1
text: End your turn in the lane that corresponds to the lane you turned from.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Completing the turn › Lane · ¶1
text: If you are turning left onto a multi-lane road, return to normal traffic speed and move into the curb lane when it is safe to do so.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Completing the turn › Lane · ¶1
text: If you are turning right onto a road where the right lane is blocked with parked vehicles or cannot be used for other reasons, move directly to the next available lane.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Completing the turn › Traffic check · ¶1
text: As you return to normal traffic speed, check your mirrors to become aware of the traffic situation on the new road.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Completing the turn › Speed · ¶1
text: Return to normal traffic speed by accelerating smoothly to blend with the traffic around you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Completing the turn › Speed · ¶1
text: In light traffic, accelerate moderately.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Completing the turn › Speed · ¶1
text: In heavier traffic, you may have to accelerate more quickly.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Left and right turns › Completing the turn › Speed · ¶1
text: In a vehicle with manual transmission, shift gears as you increase speed.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › The approach · ¶1
text: This driving task is done at inter­sections where you must come to a stop.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › The approach · ¶1
text: It begins at the point where you can see the intersection and ends just before you enter the intersection.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › The approach · ¶1
text: Be sure to follow these actions:

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › The approach › Traffic check · ¶1
text: Before slowing down, look all around you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › The approach › Traffic check · ¶1
text: Use your mirrors to check traffic behind you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › The approach › Speed · ¶1
text: Steadily reduce speed as you approach the intersection.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › The approach › Speed · ¶1
text: In a vehicle with manual transmission, you may downshift into a lower gear as you slow down.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › The approach › Speed · ¶1
text: Do not coast with your foot on the clutch pedal.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › The approach › Space · ¶1
text: While slowing down, keep at least a two to three-second distance behind the vehicle in front of you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › The stop · ¶1
text: This driving task includes the actions you take while stopped and waiting to move through the intersection.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › The stop · ¶1
text: Remember these points:

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › The stop › Stop · ¶1
text: Come to a complete stop.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › The stop › Stop · ¶1
text: Do not let your vehicle roll forward or backward.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › The stop › Stop · ¶1
text: When traffic conditions allow, move forward to check that the way is clear or start across the intersection.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › The stop › Stop · ¶1
text: If you have to stop after you have passed the stop line, do not back up.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › The stop › Space · ¶1
text: When stopped behind another vehicle at the intersection, leave enough space to pull out and pass without having to back up.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › The stop › Space · ¶1
text: Leaving this space protects you in three ways: it lets you pull around the vehicle in front if it stalls; it helps prevent you from being pushed into the ahead if you are hit from behind; and it reduces the risk of collision if the vehicle ahead rolls backward or backs up.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › The stop › Stop line · ¶1
text: If you are the first vehicle approaching an intersection with a red light or stop sign, stop behind the stop line if it is marked on the pavement.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › The stop › Stop line · ¶1
text: If there is no stop line, stop at the crosswalk, marked or not.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › The stop › Stop line · ¶1
text: If there is no crosswalk, stop at the edge of the sidewalk.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › The stop › Stop line · ¶1
text: If there is no sidewalk, stop at the edge of the intersection.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › Driving through · ¶1
text: This task includes the actions you take as you drive through the intersection and return to normal traffic speed.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › Driving through · ¶1
text: Make sure to follow these actions:

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › Driving through › Traffic check · ¶1
text: If you are stopped, waiting for a green light or for the way to be clear, keep checking traffic all around you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › Driving through › Traffic check · ¶1
text: Just before entering the intersection, look left, ahead and right to check that the way is clear.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › Driving through › Traffic check · ¶1
text: If there is any doubt about the right-of-way, try to make eye contact with nearby driv­ers or pedestrians.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › Driving through › Traffic check · ¶1
text: You have not properly checked traffic if another vehicle or pedestrian has the right-­of-way and must take action to avoid your vehicle.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › Driving through › Both hands · ¶1
text: Keep both hands on the steering wheel as you drive through the intersection.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › Driving through › Both hands · ¶1
text: You are most at risk from other traffic when you are crossing the intersection.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › Driving through › Both hands · ¶1
text: Using both hands on the wheel gives you maximum steering control when you need it most.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › Driving through › Both hands · ¶1
text: An exception to this is if you have a disability that prevents you from using both hands.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › Driving through › Gears · ¶1
text: In a vehicle with manual transmission, do not shift gears crossing the intersection.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › Driving through › Gears · ¶1
text: If you need to, you may shift gears immediately after the vehicle is moving but before it is well into the intersection.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › Driving through › Gears · ¶1
text: You may also shift gears in an intersection wider than four lanes if not doing so would slow down other traffic.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › Driving through › Gears · ¶1
text: Generally, not changing gears gives you more control over your vehicle.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › Driving through › Traffic check · ¶2
text: As you return to normal traffic speed, check your mirrors to become aware of the traffic situation after you have gone through the intersection.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › Driving through › Speed · ¶1
text: Move ahead within four to five seconds after it is safe to start.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › Driving through › Speed · ¶1
text: Return to normal traffic speed by accelerating smoothly to blend with the traffic around you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › Driving through › Speed · ¶1
text: In light traffic, accelerate moderately.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › Driving through › Speed · ¶1
text: In heavier traffic, you may have to accelerate more quickly.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Stop intersection › Driving through › Speed · ¶1
text: In a vehicle with manual transmission, shift gears as you increase speed.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Through intersection › The approach · ¶1
text: This driving task is done at inter­sections where you may not need to stop.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Through intersection › The approach · ¶1
text: It begins at the point where you can see the intersection and ends just before the entrance to the intersection.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Through intersection › The approach · ¶1
text: Remember to do the following:

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Through intersection › The approach › Traffic check · ¶1
text: As you approach the intersection, look left and right for traffic on the intersecting road.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Through intersection › The approach › Traffic check · ¶1
text: If you have to slow down for the intersection, check your mirrors for traffic behind you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Through intersection › The approach › Speed · ¶1
text: Keep at the same speed as you go through the intersection unless there is a chance traffic may cross the intersection in front of you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Through intersection › The approach › Speed · ¶1
text: If so, slow down or hold your foot over the brake, ready to slow down or stop.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Through intersection › The approach › Speed · ¶1
text: Watch for pedestrians about to cross the intersection and vehicles edging into the intersection or approaching at higher speeds.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Through intersection › The approach › Space · ¶1
text: Keep at least a two- to three-second distance behind the vehicle in front of you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Through intersection › Driving through · ¶1
text: This driving task includes your actions from the time you enter the intersection until you have crossed it and are returning to normal traffic speed.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Through intersection › Driving through · ¶1
text: Remember these points:

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Through intersection › Driving through › Lane · ¶1
text: Do not go over lane markings or change lanes in the intersection.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Through intersection › Driving through › Lane · ¶1
text: If your lane is blocked by a vehicle turning left or a vehicle edging into the intersection from the right, slow down or stop instead of pulling out to go around the vehicle.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Through intersection › Driving through › Both hands · ¶1
text: Keep both hands on the steering wheel as you drive through the intersection.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Through intersection › Driving through › Both hands · ¶1
text: You are most at risk from other traffic when you are crossing the intersection.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Through intersection › Driving through › Both hands · ¶1
text: Using both hands on the wheel givesyou maximum steering control when you need it most.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Through intersection › Driving through › Both hands · ¶1
text: An exception to this is if you have a disability that prevents you from using both hands.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Through intersection › Driving through › Gears · ¶1
text: In a vehicle with manual transmission, do not shift gears while crossing the intersection.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Through intersection › Driving through › Gears · ¶1
text: If you need to, you may shift gears immediately after the is moving but before it is well into the intersection.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Through intersection › Driving through › Gears · ¶1
text: You may also shift gears in an intersection wider than four lanes if not doing so would slow down other traffic.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Through intersection › Driving through › Gears · ¶1
text: Generally, not changing gears gives you more control over your vehicle.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Through intersection › Driving through › Traffic check · ¶1
text: If you slowed down for the intersection, check your mirrors again before returning to normal traffic speed.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Entering · ¶1
text: This driving task begins on the entrance ramp to a freeway and ends when you have reached the speed of the traffic on the freeway.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Entering · ¶1
text: Remember to do the following:

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Entering › Traffic check · ¶1
text: While on the ramp, as soon as you can see freeway traffic approaching from behind, check your mirrors and blind spot for a space to merge safely.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Entering › Traffic check · ¶1
text: At the same time, watch any vehicles in front of you on the ramp and keep back a safe distance.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Entering › Traffic check · ¶1
text: Continue to divide your attention between watching in front, checking your mirrors and looking over your shoulder to check your blind spot until you can merge safely with traffic.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Entering › Signal · ¶1
text: If you have not done so already, turn on your signal as soon as traffic on the freeway is able to see your vehicle on the ramp.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Entering › Space · ¶1
text: While on the ramp and merging with freeway traffic, keep at least a two- to three-second distance behind the vehicle in front of you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Entering › Space · ¶1
text: Time your merge so you do not move in beside another vehicle or into the blind spot of another vehicle.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Entering › Space · ¶1
text: If traffic is heavy or moving at such a high speed that it is difficult to keep an ideal following distance, adjust your speed to get the best spacing possible.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Entering › Space · ¶1
text: While on the ramp and in the acceleration lane, keep inside the lane markings.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Entering › Speed · ¶1
text: On the curve of the entrance ramp, keep your speed slow enough so that objects and people inside your vehicle are not pushed from the force created by turning the curve.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Entering › Speed · ¶1
text: While in the acceleration lane, increase your speed to match that of freeway traffic.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Entering › Speed · ¶1
text: While merging, control your speed to blend smoothly with freeway traffic.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Entering › Merge · ¶1
text: Merge with freeway traffic in a smooth, gradual movement to the centre of the nearest freeway lane.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Entering › Cancel signal · ¶1
text: Turn off your signal as soon as you have merged with freeway traffic.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Driving along · ¶1
text: This driving task checks your actions driving along the freeway (but not merging, changing lanes or exiting).

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Driving along · ¶1
text: Be sure to remember the following points:

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Driving along › Traffic check · ¶1
text: While driving along, keep checking traffic all around you and look in your mirrors every five to 10 seconds.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Driving along › Speed · ¶1
text: Avoid exceeding the speed limit or driving unreasonably slowly.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Driving along › Speed · ¶1
text: Whenever possible, drive at a steady speed.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Driving along › Speed · ¶1
text: Look ahead to where you are going to be in the next 12 to 15 seconds for dangerous situations or obstacles that you can avoid by changing your speed.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Driving along › Space · ¶1
text: Always keep at least a two- to three-second distance behind the vehicle in front of you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Driving along › Space · ¶1
text: If another vehicle follows too closely behind you, give yourself even more room in front or change lanes.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Driving along › Space · ¶1
text: Try to keep a space on both sides of your vehicle, and try not to drive in the blind spots of other vehicles.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Driving along › Space · ¶1
text: Avoid driving behind large vehicles.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Driving along › Space · ¶1
text: Because of their size, they block your view of traffic more than other vehicles.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Exiting · ¶1
text: This driving task begins when you are driving in the far right lane of the freeway and can see the exit you want to take.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Exiting · ¶1
text: It ends when you reach the end of the exit ramp.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Exiting · ¶1
text: Remember to do the following:

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Exiting › Traffic check · ¶1
text: Before moving into the exit lane, look left and right and check your mirrors.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Exiting › Traffic check · ¶1
text: If there is a lane of traffic on your right, such as an acceleration lane from an entrance ramp or a paved shoulder, remember also to check your right blind spot.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Exiting › Signal · ¶1
text: Turn on your signal before you reach the exit lane.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Exiting › Exit lane · ¶1
text: Enter the exit lane at the beginning of the lane with a smooth, gradual movement.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Exiting › Exit lane · ¶1
text: Stay inside the lane markings.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Exiting › Exit lane · ¶1
text: If there are two or more exit lanes, do not cross solid lines on the pavement to change lanes.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Exiting › Speed · ¶1
text: Do not slow down before you are completely in the exit lane.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Exiting › Speed · ¶1
text: Once you are in the lane, slow gradually without causing traffic to pile up behind you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Exiting › Speed · ¶1
text: On the curve of the exit ramp, keep your speed slow enough so that objects and people inside your vehicle are not pushed from the force created by turning the curve.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Exiting › Speed · ¶1
text: In a vehicle with manual transmission, downshift as you reduce speed.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Exiting › Space · ¶1
text: Keep at least a two- to three-second distance behind the vehicle in front of you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Freeway › Exiting › Cancel signal · ¶1
text: Turn off your signal once you are on the exit ramp.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Lane change · ¶1
text: This driving task begins as you look for a space to change lanes and ends when you have completed the lane change.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Lane change · ¶1
text: Remember to follow these actions:

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Lane change › Traffic check · ¶1
text: While waiting to change lanes safely, look all around you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Lane change › Traffic check · ¶1
text: Divide your attention between watching in front, watching the mirrors and checking your blind spot.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Lane change › Traffic check · ¶1
text: If there is another lane beside the one you are moving into, check traffic in that lane to avoid colliding with a vehicle moving into the lane at the same time as you do.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Lane change › Signal · ¶1
text: Turn on your signal when there is enough space for you to change lanes.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Lane change › Signal · ¶1
text: After signalling, check your blind spot one more time before starting to move into the other lane.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Lane change › Signal · ¶1
text: Your signal should be on soon enough to give traffic behind you time to react to the signal.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Lane change › Signal · ¶1
text: If traffic in the lane you are moving into is heavy, you may turn on your signal before there is enough space to change lanes.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Lane change › Signal · ¶1
text: This will let traffic behind you know that you are looking for a space to change lanes.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Lane change › Space · ¶1
text: Keep at least a two- to three-second distance behind the vehicle in front of you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Lane change › Space · ¶1
text: If there is another lane beside the one you are moving into, be careful not to move in beside another vehicle or into the blind spot of another vehicle.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Lane change › Speed · ¶1
text: Adjust your speed to match the speed of traffic in the new lane.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Lane change › Change · ¶1
text: Change lanes with a smooth, gradual movement into the centre of the new lane.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Lane change › Both hands · ¶1
text: Keep both hands on the steering wheel as you change lanes.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Lane change › Both hands · ¶1
text: Using both hands on the wheel gives you maximum steering control.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Lane change › Both hands · ¶1
text: An exception to this is if you have a disability that prevents you from using both hands.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Lane change › Cancel signal · ¶1
text: Turn off your signal as soon as you have changed lanes.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › The approach · ¶1
text: This driving task begins when the examiner tells you to stop and ends once you have come to a stop.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › The approach · ¶1
text: Make sure you take these actions:

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › The approach › Traffic check · ¶1
text: Before slowing down, check your mirrors and scan to see if it is legal (look for signs) to make the roadside stop.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › The approach › Traffic check · ¶1
text: Then scan the road for traffic approaching from the front and rear of your of your vehicle.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › The approach › Traffic check · ¶1
text: A 150-metre gap in both directions provides enough space to perform the move safely.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › The approach › Traffic check · ¶1
text: If there is a chance of traffic or pedestrians overtaking you on the right, check your right blind spot just before pulling over.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › The approach › Signal · ¶1
text: Turn on your signal before slowing down unless there are vehicles waiting to enter the road from side roads or driveways between you and the point where you intend to stop.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › The approach › Signal · ¶1
text: Wait until you have passed these entrances so that drivers will not think you are turning before the stopping point.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › The approach › Speed · ¶1
text: Steadily reduce speed as you approach the stop.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › The approach › Speed · ¶1
text: In a vehicle with manual transmission, you may downshift into a lower gear as you slow down.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › The approach › Speed · ¶1
text: Do not coast with your foot on the clutch pedal.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › The approach › Position · ¶1
text: Stop parallel to the curb and not more than about 30 centimetres away from it.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › The approach › Position · ¶1
text: If there is no curb,stop as far as possible off the travelled part of the road.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › The approach › Position · ¶1
text: Do not stop where you will block an entrance or other traffic.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › The stop · ¶1
text: This driving task includes the actions you take after stopping.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › The stop · ¶1
text: Remember to do the following:

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › The stop › Signal · ¶1
text: Turn off your signal and turn on your hazard lights.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › The stop › Park · ¶1
text: If your vehicle has an automatic transmission, put the gear selector in park and set the parking brake.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › The stop › Park · ¶1
text: If your has a manual transmission, set the parking brake and shift into neutral if not turning off the engine, or shift into low or reverse if turning off the engine.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › The stop › Park · ¶1
text: When parking on a hill, set your wheels against the curb, in the appropriate direction to keep your vehicle from rolling.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › Resume · ¶1
text: This driving task begins when the examiner tells you to move back onto the road and ends when you have returned to normal traffic speed.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › Resume · ¶1
text: Take the following actions:

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › Resume › Start · ¶1
text: Turn on the engine.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › Resume › Start · ¶1
text: Release the parking brake and select the correct gear to move back onto the road.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › Resume › Signal · ¶1
text: Turn off your hazard lights and turn on your left turn signal.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › Resume › Traffic check · ¶1
text: Just before pulling away from the stop, check your mirrors and your left blind spot.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › Resume › Speed · ¶1
text: Return to normal traffic speed by accelerating smoothly to blend with the traffic around you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › Resume › Speed · ¶1
text: In light traffic, accelerate moderately.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › Resume › Speed · ¶1
text: In heavier traffic, you may have to accelerate more quickly.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › Resume › Speed · ¶1
text: In a vehicle with manual transmission, shift gears as you increase speed.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Roadside stop › Resume › Cancel signal · ¶1
text: Turn off your signal as soon as you are back on the road.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Curve · ¶1
text: This driving task begins when the curve comes into sight and ends when you have gone completely around it.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Curve · ¶1
text: Follow these actions:

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Curve › Speed · ¶1
text: As you approach the curve, try to determine the safe speed for it.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Curve › Speed · ¶1
text: To do this, look for clues such as a sign that shows the safe speed, the shape of the curve and the type of road you are driving on.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Curve › Speed · ¶1
text: Slow down to the safe speed for the curve by the time you are 30 metres into it.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Curve › Speed · ¶1
text: In a blind curve where you cannot see all the way around it, drive more slowly in case oncoming traffic wanders into your lane or the curve is tighter than you expected.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Curve › Speed · ¶1
text: Slow down before the start of the curve to avoid braking in it .

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Curve › Speed · ¶1
text: While in the curve, keep your speed steady and slow enough so that objects and people inside your vehicle are not pushed from the force created by turning on the curve.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Curve › Speed · ¶1
text: Near the end of the curve, begin accelerating to return to normal speed.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Curve › Speed · ¶1
text: In a vehicle with manual transmission, do not shift gears in the curve.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Curve › Speed · ¶1
text: Not changing gears gives you more control over your vehicle and reduces the risk of your wheels locking while downshifting.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Curve › Lane · ¶1
text: As you enter the curve, look across or as far around it as possible.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Curve › Lane · ¶1
text: This helps you stay in a smooth line and centred in the lane throughout the curve.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Curve › Lane · ¶1
text: If you look only at the road directly in front of you, you are likely to wander back and forth across the lane, forcing you to constantly correct your steering.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Business section · ¶1
text: This driving task is done on straight sections of road where a number of businesses are located.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Business section · ¶1
text: Be sure to do the following actions:

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Business section › Traffic check · ¶1
text: In a business area, there are many places other than intersections where vehicles or pedestrians are likely to enter the road.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Business section › Traffic check · ¶1
text: These include entrances to businesses, institutions and construction sites, as well as pedestrian and railway crossings.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Business section › Traffic check · ¶1
text: At all these locations, look left and right to check for vehicles or pedestrians about to enter the road.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Business section › Mirror check · ¶1
text: While driving along, check your mirrors every five to 10 seconds.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Business section › Mirror check · ¶1
text: Check your mirrors more often in heavy traffic or where vehicles are moving at different speeds.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Business section › Lane · ¶1
text: Drive in the safest lane for through traffic.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Business section › Lane · ¶1
text: This is usually the curb lane.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Business section › Lane · ¶1
text: However, if the curb lane is blocked by traffic or there are many curbside hazards, the centre lane may be a safer choice.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Business section › Lane · ¶1
text: Keep to the centre of the lane and within the lane markings.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Business section › Lane · ¶1
text: Look ahead to where you will be in the next 12 to 15 seconds for dangerous situations or obstacles that you can avoid by changing lanes.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Business section › Speed · ¶1
text: Avoid exceeding the speed limit or driving unreasonably slowly.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Business section › Speed · ¶1
text: Whenever possible, drive at a steady speed.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Business section › Speed · ¶1
text: Look ahead to where you will be in the next 12 to 15 seconds for dangerous situations or obstacles that you can avoid by changing your speed.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Business section › Space · ¶1
text: Keep at least a two- to three-second distance behind the vehicle in front of you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Business section › Space · ¶1
text: Increase the distance if another vehicle follows too closely behind you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Business section › Space · ¶1
text: On a multi-lane road, try to keep a space on both sides of your vehicle, and try not to drive in the blind spots of other vehicles.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Business section › Space · ¶1
text: In slow traffic, avoid driving behind large vehicles that block your view of traffic ahead of you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Business section › Space · ¶1
text: When you stop behind another vehicle, leave enough space to see its rear wheels or to pull around it without having to back up.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Residential section · ¶1
text: This driving task is done on straight sections of residential or rural road.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Residential section · ¶1
text: Remember these points:

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Residential section › Traffic check · ¶1
text: On a residential road, watch out for entrances to schools, pedestrian crossings, driveways, sidewalks and any other locations where there might be traffic hazards.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Residential section › Traffic check · ¶1
text: On a rural road, watch for entrances to residences, farms, businesses and industrial sites.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Residential section › Traffic check · ¶1
text: At all these locations, look left and right to check for vehicles or pedestrians about to enter the road.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Residential section › Mirror check · ¶1
text: While driving along, check your mirrors every five to 10 seconds.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Residential section › Mirror check · ¶1
text: Check your mirrors more often in heavy traffic or where vehicles are moving at different speeds.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Residential section › Lane · ¶1
text: Keep to the centre of the lane.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Residential section › Lane · ¶1
text: If there are no lane markings, keep to the centre of the travelled part of the road, away from parked vehicles or pedestrians.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Residential section › Lane · ¶1
text: Where you cannot see far ahead on the road because of a curve or a hill, move right to avoid colliding with an oncoming vehicle that is over the centre line.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Residential section › Lane · ¶1
text: Look ahead to where you will be in the next 12 to 15 seconds for dangerous situations or obstacles that you can avoid by changing lanes.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Residential section › Speed · ¶1
text: Avoid exceeding the speed limit or driving unreasonably slowly.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Residential section › Speed · ¶1
text: Whenever possible, drive at a steady speed.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Residential section › Speed · ¶1
text: Look ahead to where you will be in the next 12 to 15 seconds for dangerous situations or obstacles that you can avoid by changing your speed.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Residential section › Space · ¶1
text: Keep at least a two- to three-second distance behind the vehicle in front of you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Residential section › Space · ¶1
text: Increase the distance if another vehicle follows too closely behind you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Residential section › Space · ¶1
text: In slow traffic, avoid driving behind large vehicles that block your view of traffic ahead.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Residential section › Space · ¶1
text: When you stop behind another vehicle, leave enough space to see its rear wheels or to pull around it without having to back up.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › The approach · ¶1
text: This driving task begins when the examiner tells you to park and ends when you have come to a stop, ready to back into the parking space.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › The approach · ¶1
text: Remember these points:

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › The approach › Traffic check · ¶1
text: Before slowing down, check your mirror for traffic behind you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › The approach › Traffic check · ¶1
text: Before pulling into position to back up, check your blind spot.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › The approach › Signal · ¶1
text: Turn on your signal before slowing down unless there are vehicles waiting to enter the road from side roads or driveways between you and your stopping point.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › The approach › Signal · ¶1
text: Wait until you have passed these entrances so that drivers will not think you are turning before your parallel parking position.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › The approach › Speed · ¶1
text: Steadily reduce speed.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › The approach › Speed · ¶1
text: In a vehicle with manual transmission, you may downshift into a lower gear as you slow down.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › The approach › Speed · ¶1
text: Do not coast with your foot on the clutch pedal.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › The approach › Stop · ¶1
text: Stop beside, or parallel to, the parked vehicle (real or imagi­nary) in front of the empty parking space.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › The approach › Stop · ¶1
text: Leave at least 60 centimetres between your vehicle and the parked vehicle.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › The approach › Stop · ¶1
text: Stop when your vehicle is completely in front of the empty parking space.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › Park · ¶1
text: This driving task includes the actions you take to park in a parallel parking space.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › Park · ¶1
text: Remember to do the following:

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › Park › Traffic check · ¶1
text: Before backing up, look all around the vehicle and check your mirrors and both blind spots.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › Park › Traffic check · ¶1
text: Do not start reversing until the way is clear or traffic has stopped to let you park.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › Park › Back up · ¶1
text: Begin reversing into the space, turning the steering wheel toward the curb.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › Park › Back up · ¶1
text: When your vehicle is about halfway into the space, steer to bring your vehicle in line with the curb.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › Park › Back up · ¶1
text: Once you are in the parking space, move forward or backward to fit within the pavement markings or to allow room for the vehicle in front or behind you to pull out.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › Park › Back up · ¶1
text: Do not hit the curb or touch another vehicle while entering your parking space.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › Park › Back up · ¶1
text: Where there is no curb, park off the travelled part of the road.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › Park › Park · ¶1
text: If your vehicle has automatic transmission, put the gear selector in park and set the parking brake.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › Park › Park · ¶1
text: If your vehicle has manual transmission, set the parking brake and shift into neutral if not turning off the engine, or shift into low or reverse if turning off the engine.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › Park › Park · ¶1
text: When parking on a hill, turn your wheels in the appropriate direction to keep your vehicle from rolling.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › Resume · ¶1
text: This driving task begins when the examiner tells you to move from the parking space and ends when you have returned to normal traffic speed.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › Resume · ¶1
text: Remember these points:

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › Resume › Start · ¶1
text: Turn on the engine.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › Resume › Start · ¶1
text: Release the parking brake and select the correct gear to move back onto the road.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › Resume › Signal · ¶1
text: Turn on your signal.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › Resume › Traffic check · ¶1
text: Just before pulling out of the parking spot, check your mirrors and your blind spot.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › Resume › Speed · ¶1
text: Return to normal traffic speed by accelerating smoothly to blend with the traffic around you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › Resume › Speed · ¶1
text: In light traffic, accelerate moderately.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › Resume › Speed · ¶1
text: In heavier traffic, you may have to accelerate more quickly.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › Resume › Speed · ¶1
text: In a vehicle with manual transmission, shift gears as you increase speed.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Parallel park › Resume › Cancel signal · ¶1
text: Turn off your signal after you leave the parking space.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › The approach · ¶1
text: This driving task begins when the examiner tells you to stop and turn your vehicle around.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › The approach · ¶1
text: It ends when you have almost stopped, ready to start the turn.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › The approach · ¶1
text: Be sure to do the following:

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › The approach › Traffic check · ¶1
text: Before slowing down, check traffic in front and behind you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › The approach › Traffic check · ¶1
text: If necessary, check your blind spot before pulling over to the right side of the road to stop.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › The approach › Signal · ¶1
text: Turn on your signal before slowing down unless there are vehicles waiting to enter the road from sideroads or driveways between you and your stopping point.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › The approach › Signal · ¶1
text: Wait until you have passed these entrances so that driv­ers will not think you are turning.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › The approach › Speed · ¶1
text: Steadily reduce speed.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › The approach › Speed · ¶1
text: In a vehicle with manual transmission, you may downshift into a lower gear as you slow down.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › The approach › Speed · ¶1
text: Do not coast with your foot on the clutch pedal.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › The approach › Position · ¶1
text: Stop so you are parallel to the curb and not more than 30 centimetres away.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › The approach › Position · ¶1
text: Where there is no curb, stop as far as possible off the travelled part of the road.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › The approach › Position · ¶1
text: Do not stop where you will block an entrance or other traffic.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › Turn around · ¶1
text: This driving task includes the actions you take to turn around and ends when you are ready to drive away in the opposite direction.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › Turn around · ¶1
text: Remember these points:

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › Turn around › Traffic check · ¶1
text: Check your mirrors and your blind spot just before starting the turn.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › Turn around › Traffic check · ¶1
text: Wait until the way is clear or traffic has stopped to let you turn.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › Turn around › Traffic check · ¶1
text: Each time you stop while turning, check traffic in both directions.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › Turn around › Signal · ¶1
text: Turn on your left signal before starting to turn.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › Turn around › Turn around · ¶1
text: With the steering wheel turned sharply left, move slowly and smoothly across the road.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › Turn around › Turn around · ¶1
text: When you have reached the far left side of the road, stop and put your vehicle in reverse.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › Turn around › Turn around · ¶1
text: With the steering wheel turned sharply right, reverse so the vehicle is facing in the new direction.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › Turn around › Turn around · ¶1
text: Stop and shift into forward gear to move ahead.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › Turn around › Turn around · ¶1
text: Use the whole road to make your turn, reversing only once.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › Turn around › Turn around · ¶1
text: Do not reverse over the edge or shoulder of the road or into the curb.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › Resume · ¶1
text: This driving task begins when you are turned around, ready to move ahead and ends when you have returned to normal traffic speed.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › Resume · ¶1
text: Make sure you take these actions:

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › Resume › Traffic check · ¶1
text: Check your mirrors before increasing speed.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › Resume › Speed · ¶1
text: Return to normal traffic speed by accelerating smoothly to blend with the traffic around you.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › Resume › Speed · ¶1
text: In light traffic, accelerate moderately.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › Resume › Speed · ¶1
text: In heavier traffic, you may have to accelerate more quickly.

locator: The Level Two Road Test › Three-point turn › Resume › Speed · ¶1
text: In a vehicle with manual transmission, shift gears as you increase speed.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Intro · ¶1
text: It is illegal to drive a vehicle in dangerous condition.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Intro · ¶1
text: But maintaining your vehicle also makes sense from an economic point of view: it can mean better gas mileage and a better price when you sell it.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Intro · ¶1
text: Maintaining your vehicle also helps to protect the environment.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Intro · ¶2
text: A police officer or Ministry of Transportation inspector can examine your vehicle, its equipment and any trailer attached to it, at any time.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Intro · ¶2
text: If the vehicle is found to be unsafe, it may be taken off the road until the problem is fixed.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Intro · ¶3
text: The following driver habits and regular maintenance will help keep your vehicle fit and safe.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Driver Habits · ¶1
text: Driver habits are the things that you can do whenever you drive a vehicle.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Driver Habits · ¶1
text: If you identify any concerns or deficiencies, further investigation or actions, including inspection and repair by a qualified mechanic, should be considered.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Driver Habits · ¶1
text: The vehicle’s owner manual often has detailed information on what to look for when inspecting your vehicle and how to address minor problems.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Driver Habits › When approaching your vehicle look for signs of: · item 1
text: Fresh damage

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Driver Habits › When approaching your vehicle look for signs of: · item 2
text: Fluid leaks underneath

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Driver Habits › When approaching your vehicle look for signs of: · item 3
text: Under-inflated or flat tires

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Driver Habits › When approaching your vehicle look for signs of: · item 4
text: Ajar doors, hood, trunk and fuel door/cap

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Driver Habits › When approaching your vehicle look for signs of: · item 5
text: Unsecured loads

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Driver Habits › When approaching your vehicle look for signs of: · item 6
text: Check for ice, snow, or dirt that may interfere with vehicle lighting, steering, driver visibility, or become a hazard to other motorists should it come free from your vehicle

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Driver Habits › From the driver’s seat and before driving, look for: · item 1
text: Unobstructed visibility around entire vehicle

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Driver Habits › From the driver’s seat and before driving, look for: · item 2
text: Burned-out or dim headlamps

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Driver Habits › From the driver’s seat and before driving, look for: · item 3
text: Illuminated dashboard warning lights during engine start, then going out

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Driver Habits › From the driver’s seat and before driving, look for: · item 4
text: Loose objects in the vehicle

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Driver Habits › While driving, be alert for: · item 1
text: Unusual engine or exhaust noises

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Driver Habits › While driving, be alert for: · item 2
text: Squeaking or grinding noises when applying the brakes

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Driver Habits › While driving, be alert for: · item 3
text: Dashboard warning lights coming on

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Driver Habits › When planning an extended trip, perform more detailed checks, including: · item 1
text: Windshield wipers and washer-fluid level

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Driver Habits › When planning an extended trip, perform more detailed checks, including: · item 2
text: Tire pressures, condition and wear

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Driver Habits › When planning an extended trip, perform more detailed checks, including: · item 3
text: All lights work

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Driver Habits › When planning an extended trip, perform more detailed checks, including: · item 4
text: Under the hood when the engine is cold; oil and coolant levels, obvious defects with belts, hoses, and possible leaks.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Driver Habits › When planning an extended trip, perform more detailed checks, including: · item 4
text: Using the vehicle owner’s manual for more information on what to look for

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Driver Habits › When planning an extended trip, perform more detailed checks, including: · item 5
text: Having your vehicle thoroughly inspected by a qualified mechanic

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Regular Maintenance · ¶1
text: In order to keep your vehicle running smoothly, vehicle manufacturers often establish a schedule for regular maintenance.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Regular Maintenance · ¶1
text: Scheduling of this work is normally based upon accumulated vehicle mileage or time intervals (whichever comes first).

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Regular Maintenance · ¶1
text: Further details may be found in the vehicle’s owner’s manual.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Regular Maintenance · ¶1
text: Regular maintenance may include oil and filter change, other fluid checks and changes, air and fuel filter replacement, tire rotation and brake inspection.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Regular Maintenance · ¶1
text: Periodically, more intensive mechanical servicing such as engine adjustments and timing-belt replacement may be required.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Winter maintenance · ¶1
text: A well-maintained vehicle will usually start in all weather conditions.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Winter maintenance · ¶2
text: Carry emergency supplies.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Winter maintenance · ¶2
text: These should include:

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Winter maintenance · item 1
text: a shovel

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Winter maintenance · item 2
text: booster cables

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Winter maintenance · item 3
text: emergency flares or warning lights

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Winter maintenance · item 4
text: a blanket

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Winter maintenance · item 5
text: a chain for towing.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Winter maintenance · ¶3
text: Always carry extra windshield washer fluid in the winter and refill the container when necessary.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Winter maintenance · ¶4
text: Faulty exhaust systems are especially dangerous in the winter when drivers are more likely to drive with windows and vents closed.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Winter maintenance · ¶4
text: Have your exhaust checked if it sounds noisy or rattles.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Tires · ¶1
text: The type of tires you have and the way they are made are critical for good traction, mileage and safety.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Tires · ¶1
text: Keep these points in mind when you buy or replace tires, and check your vehicle owner’s manual or the tire manufacturer’s guide for recommendations.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Tires · ¶2
text: Tires must meet standards described in the Canadian Motor Vehicle Safety Act .

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Tires · ¶2
text: Tires deteriorate with age, even when not in use.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Tires · ¶2
text: Aged tires have reduced traction, are more prone to cracking and may fail unexpectedly while in use.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Tires · ¶2
text: Tires should not be older than 10 years.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Tires · item 1
text: Replace tires when the tread is less than 1.5 millimetres deep or when tread-wear indicators touch the road.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Tires · item 1
text: Vehicles that weigh more than 4,500 kilograms must replace their front tires when tread is less than three millimetres deep.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Tires · item 2
text: Replace tires that have bumps, bulges, knots, exposed cords or tread and sidewall cuts deep enough to expose cords.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Tires · item 3
text: Any tire on a vehicle must not be smaller than the vehicle manufacturer’s specified minimum size.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Tires · item 3
text: And it must not be so large that it touches the vehicle or affects its safe operation.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Tires · item 4
text: You should use similar tires on all four wheels of your vehicle.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Tires · item 5
text: To provide the best traction during the winter season, it is recommended that your vehicle be equipped with four winter or all-weather tires with the same tread pattern.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Tires · item 6
text: If you live in northern Ontario, you can legally use studded tires on your vehicle.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Tires · item 7
text: Scrap tires are a serious environmental concern.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Tires · item 7
text: Proper maintenance will extend the life of a tire and delay its disposal.

locator: Maintaining your vehicle › Tires · item 7
text: Some tips for longer wear: maintain the right air pressure; inspect tires for wear; rotate tires regularly and practice good driving habits.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Intro · ¶1
text: This handbook is only a guide.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Intro · ¶1
text: For official purposes, please refer to the Highway Traffic Act , the Motorized Snow Vehicles Act and the Off-road Vehicles Act of Ontario .

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Intro · ¶2
text: If you're taking beginner driver education, make sure it’s from a ministry-approved school .

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Intro · ¶3
text: For more information about driver licensing, visit the website .
