locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Intro · ¶6
text: Driving is a privilege - not a right

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Introduction · ¶1
text: Off-road vehicles and snowmobiles are popular forms of recreation for many people in Ontario.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Introduction · ¶1
text: They are also necessary for transportation in remote areas and in emergencies.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Introduction · ¶1
text: But these vehicles are not toys.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Introduction · ¶1
text: If you intend to use them, you must know how they work, how to drive them safely in different situations and how Ontario laws apply to them.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Introduction · ¶2
text: It is important to remember that off-road vehicles are intended for off-road use.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Introduction · ¶2
text: Dirt bikes cannot be driven on public roads, although snowmobiles can be in some areas.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Introduction · ¶2
text: Off-road vehicles are allowed to travel directly across some highways.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Introduction · ¶2
text: However only single-rider, all-terrain vehicles can be driven on the shoulder of some provincial highways and municipal roads where bylaws permit.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Introduction · ¶3
text: This section of the handbook contains information about Ontario’s laws and safe driving tips for snowmobiles and off-road vehicles.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Introduction · ¶3
text: As you read, remember it is a guide only.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Introduction · ¶3
text: For official purposes, please refer to the Highway Traffic Act , the Motorized Snow Vehicles Act , the Off-road Vehicles Act , the Trespass to Property Act and the Occupiers' Liability Act of Ontario .

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Introduction · ¶3
text: The applicable legislation can be accessed online through Ontario’s e-Laws website .

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Introduction · ¶4
text: Note: Alcohol presents a major risk to your safety and the safety of others whether you are driving a car, motorcycle, snowmobile or off-road vehicle.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Introduction · ¶4
text: Drinking affects your ability to operate your vehicle and increases your chances of having a collision.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile · ¶1
text: This chapter tells you what you need to know to drive a motorized snow vehicle in Ontario.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile · ¶1
text: This includes age requirements, registration, where you can and cannot drive, safety tips, traffic signs and signals and the Snowmobiler’s Code of Ethics.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › What you need to drive a snowmobile in Ontario · ¶1
text: You can drive a snowmobile if you have a valid Ontario driver’s licence (any class).

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › What you need to drive a snowmobile in Ontario · ¶1
text: If you do not have a driver’s licence and you are 12 years of age or older, a valid motorized snow-vehicle operator’s licence (MSVOL) will allow you to drive on trails established and maintained by a recreational organization for the use of snowmobiles.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › What you need to drive a snowmobile in Ontario · ¶1
text: However, you must be 16 years of age or older and have a driver’s licence or a motorized snow-vehicle operator’s licence (not both) to drive a snowmobile along or across a public road where snowmobiles are allowed.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › What you need to drive a snowmobile in Ontario · ¶2
text: An MSVOL is issued by the Ontario Federation of Snowmobile Clubs in co-operation with the Ministry of Transportation.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › What you need to drive a snowmobile in Ontario · ¶2
text: You must successfully pass a snowmobile driver-training course to get a licence.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › What you need to drive a snowmobile in Ontario · ¶2
text: (For more information on how to get a motorized snow-vehicle operator’s licence .

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › What you need to drive a snowmobile in Ontario · ¶3
text: If you are a visitor to Ontario and wish to drive a snowmobile while you are here, you must have a valid licence that allows you to drive a snowmobile in your home province, state or country.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › What you need to drive a snowmobile in Ontario · ¶4
text: You must carry your driver’s licence or snow-vehicle operator’s licence when you are driving your snowmobile anywhere other than on your own property.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › What you need to drive a snowmobile in Ontario · ¶4
text: You must show it when asked by a police or conservation officer.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › What you need to drive a snowmobile in Ontario · ¶5
text: If your driver’s licence or snow-vehicle operator’s licence has been suspended, you may not drive any type of vehicle on or off any roads or in any public place.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Registering and insuring your snowmobile · ¶1
text: Before driving a snowmobile, it must be registered with the Ministry of Transportation through a ServiceOntario centre.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Registering and insuring your snowmobile · ¶1
text: This applies to new or used snowmobiles that have never been registered, and snowmobiles previously registered in another jurisdiction.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Registering and insuring your snowmobile · ¶1
text: If you buy a new snowmobile, it must be registered within six days of sale.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Registering and insuring your snowmobile · ¶1
text: You can download and complete a registration form before visiting a ServiceOntario centre.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Registering and insuring your snowmobile · ¶2
text: If you buy a new snowmobile, your dealer will register it with the Ministry of Transportation within six days of the sale.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Registering and insuring your snowmobile · ¶2
text: If you buy a used snowmobile that has been previously registered, you will simply need the signed snow-vehicle permit and the bill of sale to transfer the registration into your name.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Registering and insuring your snowmobile · ¶3
text: You must pay a fee to register your snowmobile.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Registering and insuring your snowmobile · ¶3
text: This is a one-time fee to be paid by the owner of the snowmobile.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Registering and insuring your snowmobile · ¶3
text: After registering, you will be given a permit and a registration number decal to display on your snowmobile.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Registering and insuring your snowmobile · ¶4
text: Attach the decal to each side of your snowmobile’s cowling or engine cover.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Registering and insuring your snowmobile · ¶4
text: It should be placed so that the start of the registration number is between 10 and 15 centimetres from the rear of the cowling.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Registering and insuring your snowmobile · ¶4
text: If the decal cannot be placed on the cowling because of the design of the vehicle, place the decal on each side of the tunnel, near the light reflector.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Registering and insuring your snowmobile · ¶5
text: Unless you are driving your registered snowmobile on your own property or you are a resident of northern Ontario that is exempt, you must have a validation sticker on your registration decal.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Registering and insuring your snowmobile · ¶5
text: You must carry your driver’s licence or MSVOL and evidence of your vehicle’s registration at all times and show it to a police or conservation officer when asked.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Registering and insuring your snowmobile · ¶6
text: Snowmobiles are only permitted on public highways when directly crossing.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Registering and insuring your snowmobile · ¶6
text: In specific circumstances, snowmobiles can operate on the non-serviced portion of some highways.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Registering and insuring your snowmobile · ¶6
text: Local municipalities also have authority to pass bylaws governing the use of snowmobiles on highways under their jurisdiction.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Registering and insuring your snowmobile · ¶7
text: There is an annual renewal fee for the sticker.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Registering and insuring your snowmobile · ¶7
text: Place the sticker in the upper right corner of the decal.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Registering and insuring your snowmobile · ¶8
text: You must also have liability insurance to drive your snowmobile off your own property.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Registering and insuring your snowmobile · ¶8
text: Carry the insurance card given to you by the insurance company for the snowmobile, and show it when a police or conservation officer asks for it.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Registering and insuring your snowmobile · ¶8
text: If someone else uses your snowmobile with your consent, you are both responsible for any penalties, damages or injuries that may occur.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Registering and insuring your snowmobile · ¶9
text: There are separate requirements and rules regarding the operation of trail grooming equipment.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Registering and insuring your snowmobile · ¶9
text: Make sure you know what is required before operating grooming equipment.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Wear a helmet · ¶1
text: You must wear a helmet whenever you drive or ride on a snowmobile or any kind of toboggan or sled towed by a snowmobile.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Wear a helmet · ¶1
text: Although you do not require a helmet when you operate a snowmobile on your own land, it is recommended that you wear one for safety reasons.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Wear a helmet · ¶1
text: The helmet must meet the standards approved for motorcycle helmets, or motor-assisted bicycle helmets, and must be fastened properly under the chin.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Protect your eyes and face · ¶1
text: Always wear a face shield or goggles.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Protect your eyes and face · ¶1
text: A face shield can help prevent windburn, frostbite, sunblindness and watering eyes from the wind.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Protect your eyes and face · ¶1
text: A face shield can also protect your eyes from branches and twigs when driving through wooded areas.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Protect your eyes and face · ¶1
text: Select lightly tinted and shatterproof shields or goggles to match conditions.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Protect your eyes and face · ¶1
text: For example, choose clear plastic for dull, cloudy days and deep yellow for late afternoon when flat light can hide depressions in the snow.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Protect your eyes and face · ¶1
text: Avoid dark-tinted shields or goggles, which can restrict your vision.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Make sure your snowmobile is in good condition · ¶1
text: Before every trip, check your snowmobile to make sure it is in good working order.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Make sure your snowmobile is in good condition · ¶1
text: Your life may depend upon it.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Make sure your snowmobile is in good condition · ¶1
text: Do the following:

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Make sure your snowmobile is in good condition · item 1
text: Check the steering mechanism.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Make sure your snowmobile is in good condition · item 1
text: Turn the handlebars back and forth to make sure the turning is smooth and unrestricted.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Make sure your snowmobile is in good condition · item 2
text: Check the condition and tension of the motor drive belt.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Make sure your snowmobile is in good condition · item 2
text: Change it if necessary or if you are in doubt about its reliability.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Make sure your snowmobile is in good condition · item 3
text: Check the emergency switch, headlights and tail lights.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Make sure your snowmobile is in good condition · item 4
text: Check the battery solution level.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Make sure your snowmobile is in good condition · item 5
text: Check the throttle and brake levers.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Make sure your snowmobile is in good condition · item 5
text: Make sure they move freely.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Make sure your snowmobile is in good condition · item 6
text: Check the spark plugs and the tank’s fuel level.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Make sure your snowmobile is in good condition · item 6
text: Do not use matches or a lighter when doing this, and never add fuel when the motor is running.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Make sure your snowmobile is in good condition · ¶2
text: When towing a toboggan, sled or any other kind of vehicle behind a snowmobile, be sure to use a rigid tow bar and a safety chain.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Make sure your snowmobile is in good condition · ¶2
text: For safety, towed vehicles must have reflective material on the front sides, rear sides and rear to make them more visible.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Make sure your snowmobile is in good condition · ¶2
text: Towing is generally not allowed on public roads except to cross the road at a 90-degree angle.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Make sure your snowmobile is in good condition · ¶2
text: This does not apply to a snowmobile being used to free a stuck vehicle, for any emergency rescue or for trail maintenance.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Make sure your snowmobile is in good condition · ¶3
text: Before you drive anywhere, read the owner’s manual carefully and keep it in your snowmobile at all times.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Be well prepared for every trip · ¶1
text: Carefully preparing for every trip is an important part of safe snow­mobiling.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Be well prepared for every trip · ¶1
text: Check local weather forecasts and local ice conditions before heading out, as they can change in a matter of hours.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Be well prepared for every trip · ¶1
text: Avoid travelling on unmarked frozen lakes and rivers.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Be well prepared for every trip · ¶1
text: Make sure you tell someone where you will be travelling and when you expect to be back.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Be well prepared for every trip · ¶1
text: Use the buddy system; do not drive your snowmobile alone and always ride within your abilities and according to conditions.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Be well prepared for every trip · ¶2
text: Take along a first-aid kit, a vehicle repair kit, an extra ignition key, a drive belt, spark plugs and a rope.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Be well prepared for every trip · ¶2
text: On long trips, include a map and a compass (or a GPS unit and know how to use it), flashlight, hunting knife, hatchet, extra fuel, matches in a waterproof box and high-energy food such as granola bars.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › I. Getting ready to drive a snowmobile › Be well prepared for every trip · ¶2
text: If you travel over frozen lakes and rivers, wear a buoyant snowmobile suit and carry ice picks to improve the chances of survival if you break through the ice.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Where you can and cannot drive · ¶1
text: You may drive your registered snowmobile on your own property, on the private trails of organizations to which you belong, on private property when you have the owner’s permission or in permitted public parks and conservation areas.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Where you can and cannot drive · ¶2
text: Snowmobiles are only permitted on public highways when directly crossing.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Where you can and cannot drive · ¶2
text: In specific circumstances, snowmobiles can operate on the non-serviced portion of some highways.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Where you can and cannot drive · ¶2
text: Local municipalities also have the authority to pass bylaws governing the use of snowmobiles on highways under their authority.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Where you can and cannot drive · ¶3
text: You may not drive a snow­mobile on certain high-speed roads, freeways, the Queen Elizabeth Way, the Ottawa Queensway and the Kitchener-Waterloo Expressway.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Where you can and cannot drive · ¶3
text: This includes the area around these roads, from fence line to fence line.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Where you can and cannot drive · ¶3
text: You may not drive on the serviced section of a road (from shoulder to shoulder) except to cross.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Where you can and cannot drive · ¶3
text: When crossing, you must slow down, stop and then proceed at a 90-degree angle.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Where you can and cannot drive · ¶3
text: When riding in a group, do not motion the driver behind you to cross.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Where you can and cannot drive · ¶3
text: Let each rider assess oncoming traffic and decide for themselves when it is safe to cross.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Where you can and cannot drive · ¶3
text: If visibility is restricted at the crossing, you may then wave to the driver behind you that the way is clear.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Where you can and cannot drive · ¶4
text: Except where prohibited, you may drive your snowmobile along public roads, keeping as far away from the road as possible in the section between the shoulder and the fence line.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Where you can and cannot drive · ¶4
text: Local municipalities may pass bylaws that regulate or prohibit snowmobiles anywhere within their boundaries, on or off public roads.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Where you can and cannot drive · ¶4
text: Make sure you are aware of the bylaws in the municipality where you intend to snowmobile.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Where you can and cannot drive · ¶5
text: You may not drive a snow­mobile on railway tracks unless you have permission from the railway track authority.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Public trails · ¶1
text: Ontario’s public trails are established and maintained by many snowmobile clubs.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Public trails · ¶1
text: They are patrolled by Ontario Provincial Police, municipal police, conservation officers and Snowmobile Trail Officer Patrol officers.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Public trails · ¶1
text: Some clubs require snowmobiles to have and display a trail permit to drive on their trails.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Public trails · ¶1
text: Some other clubs allow their trails to be used without a trail permit.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Public trails · ¶1
text: Trails may have signs stating that a trail permit is required.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Public trails · ¶1
text: If you are unsure, check with the local snowmobile club to find out if you need a trail permit.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Public trails · ¶2
text: For trails operated by the Ontario Federation of Snowmobile Clubs, you must have and display a trail permit.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Public trails · ¶2
text: This includes trails on private property, municipal property and land owned by the government.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Public trails · ¶2
text: Some snowmobile-trail user groups are exempt from the permit requirement.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Public trails · ¶2
text: Those who are eligible for exemption and the documents required as proof are included in the trail-permits section of the regulations of the Motorized Snow Vehicles Act .

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Public trails · ¶2
text: Snowmobilers who are exempt must carry the appropriate documents and show them when requested to do so.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Public trails · ¶3
text: For information about trails and trail permits, contact your local snowmobile club or the Ontario Federation of Snowmobile Clubs, 501 Welham Road, Unit 9, Barrie, ON L4N 8Z6.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Public trails · ¶3
text: Phone 705-739-7669; fax 705-739-5005; or e-mail at info@ofsc.on.ca .

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Public trails · ¶3
text: You can visit the OFSC website .

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not trespass · ¶1
text: You are trespassing if you drive your snowmobile on private property without permission from the owner.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not trespass · ¶1
text: The owner is not required to have a “No Trespassing” sign posted.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not trespass · ¶1
text: If you are driving your snowmobile on private property, you must stop and identify yourself when asked by the police, the owner of the property or a representative of the owner.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not trespass · ¶1
text: If you are told to leave the property, you must do so immediately.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not trespass · ¶2
text: You may be fined if you are convicted of trespassing.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not trespass · ¶2
text: In addition, you may be ordered to pay damages.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not trespass · ¶2
text: Under certain circumstances, you may also be required to pay for the cost of prosecuting.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not trespass · ¶2
text: Charges will be laid against the driver of the snow­mobile.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not trespass · ¶2
text: If the driver is not known, the owner may be charged if the snowmobile was used with the owner’s permission.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not trespass · ¶3
text: A copy of the Trespass to Property Act is available through Publications Ontario.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not trespass · ¶3
Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not trespass · ¶3
text: It is available over the Internet at ServiceOntario Publications and Ontario’s e-Laws website .

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not trespass · ¶4
text: It is an offence under the Railway Safety Act to trespass on railway tracks.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Obey the speed limits · ¶1
text: You must not drive a snowmobile faster than 20 km/h in any public park or exhibition ground, or on any road where the speed limit for other vehi­cles is 50 km/h or less.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Obey the speed limits · ¶1
text: You must not drive faster than 50 km/h on snowmobile trails or on any road where the speed limit for other vehicles is more than 50 km/h .

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Obey the speed limits · ¶1
text: Always leave extra space between you and the snowmobile in front to give yourself more time to react to unexpected hazards and stop safely.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Obey the speed limits · ¶1
text: Lower your speed at night and don't outrun your headlights.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Obey the speed limits · ¶1
text: Reduced nighttime visibility makes hazards more difficult to spot and estimating distance is much harder.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Obey the speed limits · ¶1
text: Always wear clothing with reflective markings to remain visible at night.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Obey the speed limits · ¶2
text: Municipalities may set other speed limits for snowmobiles on public roads, trails and parks within their boundaries.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Obey the speed limits · ¶2
text: Check municipal bylaws.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Stop for police · ¶1
text: You must come to a safe stop when requested by a police officer to do so.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Stop for police · ¶1
text: If you do not stop, you may have to pay a fine or go to jail, or both.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Stop for police · ¶1
text: If you are convicted of failing to stop for a police officer and the court believes you wilfully avoided police during pursuit - that you tried to escape the police - your licence will be suspended for a minimum of five years.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Stop for police · ¶1
text: Your licence can be suspended for up to 10 years if anyone is killed or injured as a result of avoiding police.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Report collisions to the police · ¶1
text: You must report to the police immediately any collision that results in injury to any person or damage to property apparently exceeding $400.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶1
text: Alcohol is a major factor in snowmobile fatalities.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶1
text: Consuming any amount of alcohol before you ride affects your ability to make good decisions.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶1
text: Alcohol also increases fatigue, slows reaction time and increases your risk of hypothermia.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶2
text: It is against the law to drive a snowmobile when you are impaired by alcohol or drugs.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶3
text: Drinking and driving is a deadly combination.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶3
text: All drivers, especially inexperienced drivers, must be able to concentrate on driving.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶4
text: Consuming any amount of alcohol before you ride affects your ability to make good decisions.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶4
text: Even one drink can reduce your ability to concentrate and react to things that happen suddenly when you are driving.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶4
text: With more alcohol in your blood, you could have trouble judging distances and your vision may become blurred.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶4
text: Factors like tiredness, your mood, and how long ago you ate and how much, can make a difference in how alcohol affects your driving ability.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶5
text: The police can stop any driver to determine if alcohol or drug testing is required.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶5
text: They may also do roadside spot checks.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶5
text: When stopped by the police, you may be told to blow into a machine that tests your breath for alcohol, a roadside screening device, or perform physical co-ordination tests.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶5
text: If you fail or refuse to provide a breath sample or to perform the physical co-ordination tests, you will be charged under the Criminal Code.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶6
text: If the reading on the machine shows you have been drinking, you may be taken to a police station for a breathalyzer test.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶6
text: The breathalyzer uses your breath to measure the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶7
text: If you cannot give a breath sample or it is impractical to obtain a sample of breath, the police officer can require you to provide a blood sample instead.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶8
text: If the police believe that a driver is impaired because of the consumption of a drug or a combination of alcohol and a drug, they can also require a driver to submit to an evaluation and then require a driver to provide blood, oral fluid or urine samples.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶8
text: If you fail or refuse to comply with any of these demands, you will be charged under the Criminal Code.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶9
text: Driving impaired or with more than 80 milligrams of alcohol in 100 millilitres of blood (.08) is an offence under the Criminal Code.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶9
text: Even if your blood-alcohol concentration is less than .08, you can still be charged with impaired driving under the Criminal Code.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶10
text: You will receive an immediate 90-day administrative driver’s licence suspension if your blood-alcohol concentration (BAC) is more than .08 or if you fail or refuse to provide a breath or bodily fluid sample, perform a physical co-ordination test or submit to an evaluation.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶11
text: If you register in the “warn range” of .05 to .08 on a roadside screening device, you will receive an immediate driver’s licence suspension.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶11
text: For a first occurrence, you will be suspended for three days.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶11
text: For a second occurrence in a five-year period, you will be immediately suspended for seven days and you must undergo a remedial alcohol-education program.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶11
text: For a third or subsequent time in a five-year period, you will be immediately suspended for 30 days, and you must undergo a remedial alcohol-treatment program and have an ignition interlock condition placed on your licence for six months.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶11
text: If you choose not to install an ignition interlock device, you must not drive until the condition is removed from your licence.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶12
text: If you are 21 years old and under and hold a full-class driver’s licence, you must not drive if you have been drinking alcohol.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶12
text: Your blood-alcohol level must be zero.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶12
text: If you are caught driving with alcohol in your blood, you will receive an immediate driver’s licence suspension at the roadside for 24 hours and, if convicted, you will face a fine and a 30-day licence suspension.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶13
text: Drivers of all ages in either Level One or Level Two of Ontario’s graduated licensing system must also have a blood-alcohol level of zero when driving.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶13
text: New drivers caught drinking and driving will receive an immediate driver’s licence suspension at the roadside for 24 hours and, if convicted, will face a fine and will receive a suspension period as per the Novice Driver Escalating Sanctions scheme.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶13
text: For the first occurrence, you will be suspended for 30 days.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶13
text: For the second occurrence, in a five-year period, you will be suspended for 90 days.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶13
text: For the third occurrence in a five-year period, the novice portion of your driver’s licence will be cancelled, and you must reapply for a G1 licence.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Do not drink and drive · ¶14
text: Novice drivers will also be charged under the Criminal Code if their BAC exceeds .08 and will be issued a warn-range suspension if they register between .05 and .08.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Drugs · ¶1
text: Any drug that changes your mood or the way you see and feel about the world around you will affect the way you drive.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Drugs · ¶1
text: Criminal Code and HTA sanctions apply to drivers impaired by alcohol or a drug.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Drugs · ¶2
text: In circumstances involving possible impairment by drugs or a combination of alcohol and a drug, police can require a driver to perform physical co-ordination tests and to submit to an evaluation, and then require a driver to provide blood, oral fluid or urine samples.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Drugs · ¶2
text: If you fail or refuse to comply with any of these demands, you will be charged under the Criminal Code.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Drugs · ¶2
text: You will also receive an immediate 90-day administrative driver’s licence suspension.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Drugs · ¶2
text: Illegal drugs such as marijuana and cocaine are not the only problem.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Drugs · ¶2
text: Some drugs that your doctor may prescribe for you and some over-the-counter drugs can also impair your driving.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Drugs · ¶3
text: Here are some points you should remember:

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Drugs · item 1
text: If you use prescription medicines or get allergy shots, ask your doctor about side effects such as dizziness, blurred vision, nausea or drowsiness that could affect your driving.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Drugs · item 2
text: Read the information on the package of any over-the-counter medicine you take.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Drugs · item 2
text: Any stimulant, diet pill, tranquillizer or sedative may affect your driving.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Drugs · item 2
text: Even allergy and cold remedies may have ingredients that could affect your driving.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Drugs · item 3
text: Drugs and any amount of alcohol together can have dangerous effects, even several days after you have taken the drug.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Drugs · item 3
text: Do not take a chance - ask your doctor or pharmacist.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Practice safe snowmobiling · ¶1
text: Driving a snowmobile requires the same attention and alertness that driving any other kind of vehicle does.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Practice safe snowmobiling · ¶1
text: You must have complete control of your reflexes.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Practice safe snowmobiling · ¶1
text: If you are a beginner, practise until you can handle the basic driving skills.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Practice safe snowmobiling · ¶2
text: Learn how to control your balance on turns by using your weight to control your movements and leaning in the direction you want to turn.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Practice safe snowmobiling · ¶2
text: Position your body on the snowmobile in a way that will give you the most comfort and control for the conditions in which you are driving.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Practice safe snowmobiling · ¶2
text: On level ground, sit or kneel with both knees on the seat.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Practice safe snowmobiling · ¶2
text: On uneven or bumpy ground, stand on the running boards with your knees slightly bent.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Practice safe snowmobiling · ¶3
text: Always take the time to plan your route before you ride and make sure others in your group know the route as well.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Practice safe snowmobiling · ¶3
text: If you must stop on the trail, always select a location where you will be visible and pull over to the right as far as possible.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Practice safe snowmobiling · ¶3
text: If you are riding in a group, you should park the snowmobiles in single file and leave the vehicles running so you are visible at night.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Practice safe snowmobiling · ¶4
text: On hard-packed snow or ice, reduce your speed, because stops and turns are harder to make and you will require greater distance to complete them.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Practice safe snowmobiling · ¶4
text: When your snowmobile is trapped in deep snow, remember to turn off the motor before you try to get it out of the snow.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Practice safe snowmobiling · ¶5
text: Every time you travel on ice, you are risking your safety and that of your passenger.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Practice safe snowmobiling · ¶5
text: Watch out for pressure cracks that are much more difficult to spot at night.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Practice safe snowmobiling · ¶5
text: If you are in an unfamiliar area, ask local authorities or residents about the ice conditions, inlets, outlets, springs, fast-moving current or other hazards.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Practice safe snowmobiling · ¶5
text: Listen to local radio broadcast warnings by the Ontario Provincial Police about ice conditions.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Practice safe snowmobiling · ¶5
text: If you must drive over frozen lakes or rivers, you should consider using a buoyant snowmobile suit.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Practice safe snowmobiling · ¶5
text: It might save your life.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Practice safe snowmobiling · ¶6
text: Whenever you are driving, always watch for trails and highway, signs and obey them.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Practice safe snowmobiling · ¶6
text: Always remain on the right-hand side of the trail when riding and exercise caution on hills and curves.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Practice safe snowmobiling · ¶6
text: You should always be prepared for the unexpected.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Practice safe snowmobiling · ¶6
text: Exercise caution at road and rail crossings.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Practice safe snowmobiling · ¶6
text: Trucks and trains often kick up large clouds of snow that greatly reduce visibility.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › II. Safe and responsible snowmobiling › Practice safe snowmobiling · ¶6
text: Carry a cell phone with you when riding.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Hand signals · ¶1
text: Signals tell others what you want to do, giving them a chance to slow down, stop or prepare to turn.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Hand signals · ¶1
text: Use hand signals to signal before stopping, slowing down suddenly or turning.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Hand signals · ¶1
text: Give the correct signal well before the action and make sure others can see it.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Hand signals · ¶1
text: These illustrations show nationally recognized hand and arm signals.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Hand signals · ¶2
text: Left turn

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Hand signals · ¶3
text: Extend your left arm straight out and point in the direction of the turn.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Hand signals · ¶4
text: Right turn

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Hand signals · ¶5
text: Raise your left arm to shoulder height with elbow bent.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Hand signals · ¶6
text: Stop

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Hand signals · ¶7
text: Extend your right arm straight up over your head with the palm of the hand flat.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Hand signals · ¶8
text: Slowing

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Hand signals · ¶9
text: Extend your left arm out and down the side of your body.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Hand signals · ¶9
text: Flap your arm up and down to signal caution.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Hand signals · ¶10
text: Oncoming snowmobiles

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Hand signals · ¶11
text: Raise your left arm to shoulder height with your elbow bent and motion left to right over your head, pointing to the right side of the trail.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Hand signals · ¶12
text: Snowmobiles following

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Hand signals · ¶13
text: Raise left arm to shoulder height with your elbow bent.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Hand signals · ¶13
text: Motion front to back over your shoulder with your thumb, like a hitchhiker.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Hand signals · ¶14
text: Last snowmobile in line

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Hand signals · ¶15
text: With elbow bent, raise your left forearm to shoulder height and clench your fist.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Trail signs · ¶1
text: Trail signs give you important information about what to do in certain situations.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Trail signs · ¶1
text: Here are some common trail signs and what they mean.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Trail signs · ¶1
text: Because trail signs are not official traffic signs, they may vary in shape and colour.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Trail signs · ¶1
text: Watch for signs such as these and obey them.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Trail signs · ¶2
text: Stop

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Trail signs · ¶3
text: A stop sign is eight-sided and has a red background with white letters.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Trail signs · ¶3
text: Come to a complete stop.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Trail signs · ¶4
text: Stop ahead

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Trail signs · ¶5
text: Be prepared to stop for a stop sign up ahead.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Trail signs · ¶6
text: Snowmobiling permitted

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Trail signs · ¶7
text: A sign with a green circle means you may do the activity shown inside the ring.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Trail signs · ¶7
text: You may drive a snowmobile in the area where this sign is displayed.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Trail signs · ¶8
text: Snowmobiling restricted

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Trail signs · ¶9
text: A sign with a red circle with a line through it means the activity shown inside the ring is not allowed.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Trail signs · ¶9
text: Do not drive a snow­mobile in the area where this sign is displayed.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Direction signs · ¶1
text: These signs give you information about the direction in which you should travel on the trail.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Direction signs · ¶1
text: Do as the sign tells you.

text: If you are driving your snowmobile along or across any public roads, you need to be aware of traffic signs and what they mean.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Wind-chill factor · ¶1
text: It is important to consider the wind-chill factor when planning outdoor winter activities.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Wind-chill factor · ¶2
text: Wind-chill factor is the combined effect of wind and low temperature, which makes it feel much colder on a windy day in winter than is the actual temperature.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Wind-chill factor · ¶2
text: This is caused by the faster cooling effect of the wind.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Wind-chill factor · ¶2
text: For example, if the actual temperature is -10°C and the wind speed is 40 km/h , the temperature feels like -31°C.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Wind-chill factor · ¶3
text: You need to be aware of the wind-chill factor so that you can dress appropriately.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Wind-chill factor · ¶3
text: Outer layers that are waterproof and multiple under-layers of clothing provide added protection, and allow you to take clothing off if temperatures increase.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Wind-chill factor · ¶3
text: Also, make sure that young passengers are properly dressed and that their hands and faces are well protected.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Wind-chill factor · ¶3
text: Wearing a balaclava will reduce the risk of exposure.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Wind-chill factor · ¶3
text: Prolonged exposure to cold wind-chill temperatures can lead to hypothermia.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Wind-chill factor · ¶4
text: The chart below can help you calculate wind chill so you will be aware of potentially dangerous conditions.

text: Approximate Thresholds:

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Wind-chill calculation chart · ¶2
text: Wind-chill at or below -25°C: risk of frostbite in prolonged exposure.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Wind-chill calculation chart · ¶3
text: Wind-chill at or below -35°C: frostbite possible in 10 minutes; warm skin, suddenly exposed.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Wind-chill calculation chart · ¶3
text: (Shorter time if skin is cool at the start.)

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Wind-chill calculation chart · ¶4
text: Wind-chill at or below -60°C: frostbite possible in less than two minutes; warm skin, suddenly exposed.

text: (Shorter time if skin is cool at the start.)

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Take a snowmobile driver-training course · ¶1
text: If you are between 12 and 15 years of age, or if you are 16 and older and do not have a valid Ontario driver’s licence, you must successfully pass a snowmobile driver-training course to get your operator’s licence.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Take a snowmobile driver-training course · ¶1
text: A snowmobile driver-training course can also be a valuable refresher for licensed and experienced snowmobilers.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Take a snowmobile driver-training course · ¶2
text: The course takes about six hours and is usually held over three days.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Take a snowmobile driver-training course · ¶2
text: It covers safe driving practices, snowmobile laws, knowledge of the snowmobile, maintenance, driving positions, survival, first aid, night driving, trail signs, clothing and storage.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Take a snowmobile driver-training course · ¶2
text: It also teaches safe and courteous driving habits and skills to help you avoid collisions and property damage.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Take a snowmobile driver-training course · ¶3
text: The training course is offered by the Ontario Federation of Snowmobile Clubs (OFSC) in co-operation with the Ministry of Transportation and is offered by club instructors trained by the OFSC .

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Take a snowmobile driver-training course · ¶3
text: For the location of the nearest OFSC member club offering the course and the cost, contact the OFSC Driver Training Office at 501 Welham Road, Unit 9, Barrie, ON , L4N 8Z6.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Take a snowmobile driver-training course · ¶3
Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › Take a snowmobile driver-training course · ¶3
text: You can visit the OFSC website .

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › The snowmobiler’s code of ethics · ¶1
text: Follow this code of ethics, and you will do your part to make snowmobiling a respectable, fun and safe winter recreation.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › The snowmobiler’s code of ethics · item 1
text: I will be a good sportsperson and conservationist.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › The snowmobiler’s code of ethics · item 1
text: I recognize that people judge all snowmobilers by my actions.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › The snowmobiler’s code of ethics · item 1
text: I will use my influence with other snowmobilers to promote responsible conduct.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › The snowmobiler’s code of ethics · item 2
text: I will not litter trails or camping areas.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › The snowmobiler’s code of ethics · item 2
text: I will not pollute lakes or streams.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › The snowmobiler’s code of ethics · item 2
text: I will carry out what I carried in.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › The snowmobiler’s code of ethics · item 3
text: I will not damage living trees, shrubs or other natural features.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › The snowmobiler’s code of ethics · item 4
text: I will respect other people’s property and rights.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › The snowmobiler’s code of ethics · item 5
text: I will lend a helping hand when I see someone in distress.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › The snowmobiler’s code of ethics · item 6
text: I will make myself and my snowmobile available to assist in search-and-rescue operations.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › The snowmobiler’s code of ethics · item 7
text: I will not interfere with or harass hikers, skiers, snowshoers, people who are ice fishing or participating in other winter sports.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › The snowmobiler’s code of ethics · item 7
text: I will respect their rights to enjoy recreation facilities.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › The snowmobiler’s code of ethics · item 8
text: I will know and obey all federal, provincial and local rules regulating the operation of snowmobiles in areas where I use my snowmobile.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › The snowmobiler’s code of ethics · item 9
text: I will not harass wildlife.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › The snowmobiler’s code of ethics · item 9
text: I will avoid areas posted for the protection of wildlife.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving a snowmobile › III. Snowmobile signals and signs › The snowmobiler’s code of ethics · item 10
text: I will not drive where snowmobiles are prohibited.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle · ¶1
text: Off-road vehicles (sometimes called ORVs) are any two- or three-wheeled motorized vehicles, as well as specific vehicles with four or more wheels as prescribed by regulation, intended for recreational use.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle · ¶1
text: Examples of off-road vehicles include all-terrain vehicles (ATVs), two-up ATV s, side-by-side ATV s, utility terrain vehicles (UTVs), amphibious ATV s, off-road motorcycles and dune buggies.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle · ¶2
text: Note: Electric and motorized scooters (commonly known as go-peds) and pocket bikes (which are miniature motorcycles about two feet in height and with a speed of 70-80 km/h ) are not off-road vehicles and, as such, cannot be registered as off-road vehicles.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle · ¶2
text: These vehicles also do not comply with motorcycle standards and cannot be registered as motorcycles.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › What you need to drive an off-road vehicle in Ontario · ¶1
text: You must be 12 years of age or older to drive an off-road vehicle, except on land occupied by the vehicle owner or under the close supervision of an adult.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › What you need to drive an off-road vehicle in Ontario · ¶1
text: Direct and close supervision by an adult is recommended.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › What you need to drive an off-road vehicle in Ontario · ¶2
text: While off-road vehicles are generally not allowed on public roads, there are some exceptions.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › What you need to drive an off-road vehicle in Ontario · ¶2
text: (See the section " Where you can and cannot drive.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › What you need to drive an off-road vehicle in Ontario · ¶2
Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Registering and insuring your off-road vehicle · ¶1
text: Off-road vehicles must be registered with the Ministry of Transportation at a ServiceOntario centre.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Registering and insuring your off-road vehicle · ¶1
text: This applies to both new and used vehicles.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Registering and insuring your off-road vehicle · ¶1
text: You must be 16 years or older to register an off-road vehicle, and you must be able to prove you own the vehicle.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Registering and insuring your off-road vehicle · ¶2
text: If you buy a new off-road vehicle, you must get a certificate of sale from the dealer.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Registering and insuring your off-road vehicle · ¶3
text: If you buy or transfer ownership of a used off-road vehicle, you must present the signed vehicle portion of the vehicle permit from the previous owner.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Registering and insuring your off-road vehicle · ¶4
text: You must pay a fee to register your off-road vehicle.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Registering and insuring your off-road vehicle · ¶4
text: After regi­stering, you will be given a vehicle permit and licence plate.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Registering and insuring your off-road vehicle · ¶4
text: You should carry the vehicle permit at all times unless you are operating the vehicle on land occupied by the owner of the vehicle.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Registering and insuring your off-road vehicle · ¶5
text: If you have a two- or three-wheeled vehicle, attach the licence plate to the front of the vehicle in plain view.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Registering and insuring your off-road vehicle · ¶5
text: If you have a vehicle with four or more wheels, attach the licence plate to the rear of the vehicle.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Registering and insuring your off-road vehicle · ¶6
text: You must register your vehicle within six days of becoming the owner.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Registering and insuring your off-road vehicle · ¶6
text: If you change your address, you must notify the Ministry of Transportation within six days of the change.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Registering and insuring your off-road vehicle · ¶6
text: You may do this in person at a ServiceOntario centre, by mail to the Ministry of Transportation, P.O.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Registering and insuring your off-road vehicle · ¶6
text: Box 9200, Kingston, ON K7L 5K4, or on the ServiceOntario website .

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Registering and insuring your off-road vehicle · ¶7
text: If you are driving your off-road vehicle anywhere other than on the vehicle owner’s property, you must also have vehicle liability insurance.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Registering and insuring your off-road vehicle · ¶7
text: You must carry the insurance card with you and show it if requested by a police officer.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Registering and insuring your off-road vehicle · ¶7
text: If someone else uses your off-road vehicle with your consent, you are both responsible for any penalties, damages or injuries that may occur.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Registering and insuring your off-road vehicle · ¶8
text: The following vehicles do not need to be registered as off-road vehicles: road-building machines, farm vehicles, golf carts and motorized wheelchairs.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Registering and insuring your off-road vehicle · ¶8
text: In addition, off-road vehicles participating in a rally or competition sponsored by a motorcycle association with more than 25 members do not need to be registered for the event.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Wear a helmet · ¶1
text: You must wear a motorcycle helmet, as required by the Highway Traffic Act , whenever you drive or ride on an off-road vehicle or on any vehicle towed by an off-road vehicle.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Wear a helmet · ¶1
text: The only exception is when you operate the vehicle on the property of the vehicle owner.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Wear a helmet · ¶1
text: The helmet must meet the standards approved for motorcycle helmets, or motor-assisted vehicle helmets, and must be fastened properly under the chin.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Protect your face and body · ¶1
text: Always wear a face shield or goggles.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Protect your face and body · ¶1
text: A face shield can help prevent windburn, sunblindness and watering eyes from the wind.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Protect your face and body · ¶1
text: It can also protect your eyes from branches and twigs when driving through wooded areas.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Protect your face and body · ¶1
text: Wear pants that cover your legs, a long-sleeved shirt or jacket to protect your arms and gloves.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Protect your face and body · ¶1
text: Boots should be high enough to cover your ankles.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Protect your face and body · ¶1
text: To make yourself more visible to others while driving, wear brightly coloured clothing.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Make sure your vehicle is in good condition · ¶1
text: Before every trip, check your vehicle to make sure it is in good working order.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Make sure your vehicle is in good condition · ¶1
text: Your life may depend upon it.

locator: Off-road Vehicles & Snowmobiles › Driving an Off-road vehicle › I. Getting ready to drive an off-road vehicle › Make sure your vehicle is in good condition · ¶1
