locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › Auto insurance – it’s the law! · ¶1
text: Ontario has compulsory automobile insurance.

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › Auto insurance – it’s the law! · ¶1
text: This means every vehicle registered in the province must be insured.

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › Auto insurance – it’s the law! · ¶2
text: You must show proof that you have insurance coverage before you can register a vehicle or renew your registration.

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › Auto insurance – it’s the law! · ¶2
text: The Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario ( FSRA ), regulates insurance in Ontario.

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › Auto insurance – it’s the law! · ¶2
text: Visit FSRA 's website for more information on auto insurance.

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › Registration · ¶1
text: Vehicle registration includes licence plates and a vehicle permit.

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › Registration · ¶2
text: Licence plates in Ontario are based on a plate-to-owner system.

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › Registration · ¶2
text: This means that vehicle licence plates move with the vehicle owner, not the vehicle.

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › Registration · ¶2
text: When you sell or change vehicles, you must remove your plates.

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › Registration · ¶3
text: If you do not intend to use them on another vehicle, you may return your plates to a ServiceOntario centre.

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › Registration · ¶4
text: Learn more about buying, selling and registering a vehicle.

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › New residents · ¶1
text: New Ontario residents have 30 days to register their vehicles.

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › New residents · ¶1
text: To get a permit and Ontario licence plates, go to a ServiceOntario centre.

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › New residents · ¶1
text: You must bring along:

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › New residents · item 1
text: A safety standards certificate

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › New residents · item 2
text: Proof of insurance

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › New residents · item 3
text: Vehicle Import Forms, if you have brought the vehicle in from another country

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › New residents · item 4
text: The vehicle permit, or ownership, from where you used to live

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › Protect yourself from auto insurance fraud · ¶1
text: By being vigilant, Ontario drivers can help put a stop to fraudsters who abuse the automobile insurance system.

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › Protect yourself from auto insurance fraud · ¶1
text: Keep this in mind to protect yourself from auto insurance fraud.

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › Protect yourself from auto insurance fraud › When Buying Auto Insurance: · item 1
text: Use a licensed insurance company, agent or broker.

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › Protect yourself from auto insurance fraud › When Buying Auto Insurance: · item 1
text: The Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario (FSRA), an agency of the Ministry of Finance, regulates insurance in Ontario.

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › Protect yourself from auto insurance fraud › When Buying Auto Insurance: · item 1
text: Visit FSRA’s website, to check whether an insurance company or agent is licensed.

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › Protect yourself from auto insurance fraud › When Buying Auto Insurance: · item 1
text: The Registered Insurance Brokers of Ontario (RIBO) is the self-regulatory body for insurance brokers in Ontario.

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › Protect yourself from auto insurance fraud › When Buying Auto Insurance: · item 1
text: Visit RIBO’s website, to check whether an insurance broker is licensed.

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › Protect yourself from auto insurance fraud › After an Auto Collision: · item 1
text: Collect as much information as possible.

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › Protect yourself from auto insurance fraud › After an Auto Collision: · item 1
text: Take photos of the collision scene.

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › Protect yourself from auto insurance fraud › After an Auto Collision: · item 1
text: Get the names, addresses, phone numbers, licence plate and driver’s licence numbers, and insurance information from all those involved in the collision, including passengers in the other vehicle(s).

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › Protect yourself from auto insurance fraud › After an Auto Collision: · item 2
text: Be suspicious of referrals.

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › Protect yourself from auto insurance fraud › After an Auto Collision: · item 2
text: Be wary if you are pressured or offered money by a tow truck operator to go to a particular body shop, lawyer, paralegal or health-care provider.

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › Protect yourself from auto insurance fraud › After an Auto Collision: · item 2
text: Contact your insurance company for information on towing and where to take your vehicle to be repaired.

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › Protect yourself from auto insurance fraud › After an Auto Collision: · item 3
text: Refuse to sign blank forms in advance of receiving any services or health-care treatment related to your collision.

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › Protect yourself from auto insurance fraud › After an Auto Collision: · item 4
text: Demand detailed repair and medical bills for any goods and services related to your collision, and review them carefully.

locator: Vehicle insurance and registration › Protect yourself from auto insurance fraud › After an Auto Collision: · ¶1
text: Visit the Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario (FSRA) website for information on how to avoid, detect and report auto insur­ance fraud.

locator: s. 1 (1), "median strip"
heading: Definitions
text: “median strip” means the portion of a highway so constructed as to separate traffic travelling in one direction from traffic travelling in the opposite direction by a physical barrier or a raised or depressed paved or unpaved separation area that is not intended to allow crossing vehicular movement;

heading: Passing moving vehicles within 30 metres of pedestrian crossover
text: (3) When a vehicle is approaching a pedestrian crossover and is within 30 metres of it, the driver of any other vehicle approaching from the rear shall not allow the front extremity of his or her vehicle to pass beyond the front extremity of the other vehicle.

heading: Signal for left or right turn
text: 142 (1) The driver or operator of a vehicle upon a highway before turning to the left or right at any intersection or into a private road or driveway or from one lane for traffic to another lane for traffic or to leave the roadway shall first see that the movement can be made in safety, and if the operation of any other vehicle may be affected by the movement shall give a signal plainly visible to the driver or operator of the other vehicle of the intention to make the movement.

heading: Requirement to yield to bus from bus bay
text: 142.1 (1) Every driver of a vehicle in the lane of traffic adjacent to a bus bay shall yield the right of way to the driver of a bus who has indicated his or her intention, as prescribed, to re-enter that lane from the bus bay.

heading: Slow vehicles to travel on right side
text: 147 (1) Any vehicle travelling upon a roadway at less than the normal speed of traffic at that time and place shall, where practicable, be driven in the right-hand lane then available for traffic or as close as practicable to the right hand curb or edge of the roadway.

heading: Offence
text: (3) Every person who, while driving a motor vehicle, contravenes this section is guilty of an offence and on conviction is liable to a fine of not less than $150 and not more than $1,000.

heading: Vehicles or equestrians overtaken

heading: Bicycles overtaken
text: (6.1) Every person in charge of a motor vehicle on a highway who is overtaking a person travelling on a bicycle shall, as nearly as may be practicable, leave a distance of not less than one metre between the bicycle and the motor vehicle and shall maintain that distance until safely past the bicycle.

heading: Bicycles overtaken

heading: Passing vehicle going in same direction
text: (8) No person in charge of a vehicle shall pass or attempt to pass another vehicle going in the same direction on a highway unless the roadway, (a) in front of and to the left of the vehicle to be passed is safely free from approaching traffic; and (b) to the left of the vehicle passing or attempting to pass is safely free from overtaking traffic.

heading: No overtaking a snow plow
text: 148.1 (1) On a highway on which the speed limit is 80 kilometres per hour or more and which is divided into clearly marked lanes for traffic, no person shall, while travelling in a direction that has two or more such lanes, overtake a snow plow that is travelling in echelon with another plow or plows unless the lane of travel that is used by the overtaking vehicle to overtake the snow plow is entirely clear of any part of the snow plow, including any part of an attachment or the plow blade.

heading: Driving to left of centre prohibited under certain conditions
text: 149 (1) No vehicle shall be driven or operated to the left of the centre of a roadway designed for one or more lanes of traffic in each direction, (a) when approaching the crest of a grade or upon a curve in the roadway or within 30 metres of a bridge, viaduct or tunnel where the driver’s view is obstructed within that distance so as to create a potential hazard in the event another vehicle might approach from the opposite direction; or (b) when approaching within 30 metres of a level railway crossing.

heading: Exception
text: (2) Subsection (1) does not apply, (a) on a highway divided into clearly marked lanes where there are more such lanes for traffic in one direction than in the other direction; (b) to a road service vehicle where precautions are taken to eliminate the hazard; or (c) on a highway while it is designated for the use of one-way traffic.

heading: Passing to right of vehicle
text: 150 (1) The driver of a motor vehicle may overtake and pass to the right of another vehicle only where the movement can be made in safety and, (a) the vehicle overtaken is making or about to make a left turn or its driver has signalled his or her intention to make a left turn; (b) is made on a highway with unobstructed pavement of sufficient width for two or more lines of vehicles in each direction; or (c) is made on a highway designated for the use of one-way traffic only.

heading: Driving off roadway prohibited
text: (2) No driver of a motor vehicle shall overtake and pass another vehicle by driving off the roadway.

heading: Non-application of subs. (2)
text: (3) Subsection (2) does not apply to, (a) a motor vehicle overtaking and passing to the right of another vehicle where the shoulder to the right of the roadway is paved and the vehicle overtaken is making or about to make a left turn or its driver has signalled his or her intention to make a left turn;

heading: Where highway divided into lanes
text: (a) a vehicle shall not be driven from one lane to another lane or to the shoulder or from the shoulder to a lane unless the driver first ascertains that it can be done safely;

heading: Where highway divided into lanes
text: (b) in the case of a highway that is divided into three lanes, a vehicle shall not be driven in the centre lane except when overtaking and passing another vehicle where the roadway is clearly visible and the centre lane is clear of traffic within a reasonable safe distance, or in preparation for a left turn, or where the centre lane is at the time designated for the use of traffic moving in the direction in which the vehicle is proceeding and official signs are erected to indicate the designation;

heading: Where highway divided into lanes
text: (c) any lane may be designated for slowly moving traffic, traffic moving in a particular direction or classes or types of vehicles and, despite section 141, where a lane is so designated and official signs indicating the designation are erected, every driver shall obey the instructions on the official signs.

heading: Headway of motor vehicles, generally
text: 158 (1) The driver of a motor vehicle or street car shall not follow another vehicle or street car more closely than is reasonable and prudent having due regard for the speed of the vehicle and the traffic on and the conditions of the highway.

heading: Stop on approach of vehicle with flashing lights or bell or siren sounding
text: 159 (1) The driver of a vehicle, upon the approach of an emergency vehicle mentioned in clause (a) of the definition of that term, with its bell or siren sounding or with its lamp producing intermittent flashes of red light or red and blue light, or upon the approach of a public utility emergency vehicle with its bell or siren sounding or its lamp producing intermittent flashes of red light, shall immediately bring such vehicle to a standstill, (a) as near as is practicable to the right-hand curb or edge of the roadway and parallel therewith and clear of any intersection; or (b) when on a roadway having more than two lanes for traffic and designated for the use of one-way traffic, as near as is practicable to the nearest curb or edge of the roadway and parallel therewith and clear of any intersection.

heading: Standing street car, etc.
text: 166 (1) Where a person in charge of a vehicle or on horseback or leading a horse on a highway overtakes a street car or a car of an electric railway, operated in or near the centre of the roadway, which is stationary for the purpose of taking on or discharging passengers, he or she shall not pass the car or approach nearer than 2 metres measured back from the nearest door of the car that the person is approaching and through which passengers may get on or off until the passengers have got on or got safely to the side of the street, as the case may be, but this subsection does not apply where a safety zone has been set aside and designated by a by-law passed under section 9, 10 or 11 of the Municipal Act, 2001 or under section 7 or 8 of the City of Toronto Act, 2006.

heading: Prohibition as to passing street cars on left-hand side
text: (2) No person in charge of a vehicle or on horseback or leading a horse, overtaking a street car or the car of an electric railway, operated in or near the centre of the roadway, which is stationary or in motion, shall pass on the left side of the car, having reference to the direction in which the car is travelling, but this subsection does not apply to a fire department vehicle while proceeding to a fire or answering a fire alarm call or where the street car or car of an electric railway is being operated on a highway designated for the use of one-way traffic.

heading: Racing, stunts, etc., prohibited

heading: Duty of drivers when school bus stopped
text: (11.1) Every driver or street car operator, when meeting on a highway, other than a highway with a median strip, a stopped school bus that has its stop arm actuated, shall stop before reaching the bus and shall not proceed until the bus moves or the stop arm is no longer actuated.

heading: Duty of drivers when school bus stopped
text: (12) Every driver or street car operator on a highway, when approaching from the rear a stopped school bus that has its overhead red signal-lights flashing, shall stop and shall not proceed until the bus moves or the overhead red signal-lights have stopped flashing.

heading: Duty of drivers when school bus stopped
text: (12.1) Every driver or street car operator on a highway, when approaching from the rear a stopped school bus that has its stop arm actuated, shall stop and shall not proceed until the bus moves or the stop arm is no longer actuated.

heading: Duty of drivers when school bus stopped
text: (12.2) Every driver or street car operator on a highway, when approaching from the rear a stopped school bus that has its overhead red signal-lights flashing, or that has its stop arm actuated, shall stop at least 20 metres before reaching the bus.

heading: School bus driver, signals
text: (6) Subject to subsection (9), every school bus driver, (a) who is about to stop on a highway for the purpose of receiving or discharging children or receiving or discharging adults who have developmental disabilities, shall actuate the overhead signal-lights on the bus; (b) as soon as the bus is stopped for a purpose set out in clause (a), shall actuate the school bus stop arm; and (c) while the bus is stopped for a purpose set out in clause (a) on a highway, shall continue to operate the overhead signal-lights and stop arm until the passengers have been received or discharged and until all passengers having to cross the highway have completed the crossing.

heading: Vehicle owner may be convicted
text: 207 (1) Subject to subsection (2), the owner of a vehicle may be charged with and convicted of an offence under this Act or the regulations or any municipal by-law regulating traffic for which the driver of the vehicle is subject to be charged unless, at the time of the offence, the vehicle was in the possession of some person other than the owner without the owner’s consent and on conviction the owner is liable to the penalty prescribed for the offence.

heading: Limitation
text: (7) An owner of a motor vehicle convicted of an offence under subsection 175 (19), (19.1), (20) or (20.1) is not liable to imprisonment, a probation order under subsection 72 (1) of the Provincial Offences Act or a driver’s licence suspension as a result of that conviction or as a result of default in payment of a fine resulting from that conviction.

heading: General penalty
text: 214 (1) Every person who contravenes this Act or any regulation is guilty of an offence and on conviction, where a penalty for the contravention is not otherwise provided for herein, is liable to a fine of not less than $60 and not more than $1,000.

heading: Unnecessary noise
text: (4) A person having the control or charge of a motor vehicle shall not sound any bell, horn or other signalling device so as to make an unreasonable noise, and a driver of any motor vehicle shall not permit any unreasonable amount of smoke to escape from the motor vehicle, nor shall the driver at any time cause the motor vehicle to make any unnecessary noise, but this subsection does not apply to a motor vehicle of a municipal fire department while proceeding to a fire or answering a fire alarm call.

heading: Alarm bell to be sounded
text: (5) Every motor vehicle, motor assisted bicycle and bicycle shall be equipped with an alarm bell, gong or horn, which shall be kept in good working order and sounded whenever it is reasonably necessary to notify pedestrians or others of its approach.

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › F · ¶4
text: flashing signal – traffic signal alerting drivers to dangerous conditions or tells them to stop

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › F · ¶5
text: focus vision (fovial) – the part of the vision field which allows the driver to read signs and make distinctions between vehicles and objects often measured as visual acuity

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › F · ¶6
text: following interval – the time recommended to follow another vehicle in the intended path of travel. Select an object near the road surface. When the vehicle ahead passes that object, start counting one thousand-one, one thousand-two, etc., until the front of your car reaches the same object. For speeds under 30 mph, the minimum time with good road conditions is 2 seconds. For speeds above 30 mph, maintain 4 seconds (more for adverse conditions) of following time. Developing a four-second following interval is the best practice for a beginning or less experienced driver

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › F · ¶7
text: force of impact – the force with which one moving object hits another object; this varies according to speed, weight, and distance between impact and stop, and is based on forces of inertia and momentum

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › F · ¶8
text: friction – the force creating heat which helps the tire maintain traction on the road, unless too much heat is generated which may cause traction loss due to melting of tire rubber on the road

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › G · ¶1
text: gap – time or distance interval between vehicles on road

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › G · ¶2
text: glare recovery time – the time your eyes need to regain clear vision after being affected by bright lights

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › G · ¶3
text: glare resistance – the ability to continue seeing when looking at bright lights

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › G · ¶4
text: graduated driver license program – requires young drivers to progress through a series of licensing stages with various restrictions such as accompanying drivers, times permitted to drive, and allowable passengers

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › G · ¶5
text: guide sign – a sign providing directions, distances, services, points of interest, or other information

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › H · ¶1
text: hallucinogen – mind-altering drug that tends to distort a person’s perception of direction, distance, and time

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › H · ¶2
text: hazard flasher – a device that flashes front turn signal lights and taillights to warn others the vehicle is a hazard

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › H · ¶3
text: head restraints – specially designed air bag or padded devices on the backs of front seats helping to reduce whiplash injuries in a side or rear impact collision

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › H · ¶4
text: highway hypnosis – drowsy or trance-like condition caused by concentration on the road ahead and monotony of driving

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › H · ¶5
text: hydroplaning – occurs when a tire patch loses contact with the road by rising up on top of water

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › H · ¶6
text: highway – the width between the boundary lines of a publicly maintained way any part of which is open to the public for vehicular travel

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › I · ¶1
text: ignition interlock device – a special mechanical control device installed on a motor vehicle’s dashboard. A driver must exhale into the device to start the vehicle. The court-ordered installation of an interlock ignition device must be performed by a DPS-certified service center

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › I · ¶2
text: implied-consent law – anyone who receives a driver license automatically consents to be tested for blood-alcohol content and other drugs if stopped for suspicion of alcohol or drug usage while driving

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › I · ¶3
text: intoxilyzer – the breath-test instrument machine commonly used for determining blood-alcohol content

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › L · ¶1
text: lane change – lateral maneuver moving the vehicle from one lane to another using proper space management procedures

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › L · ¶2
text: lane signal – a signal, usually overhead, indicating if a lane can or cannot be used at a specific time

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › L · ¶3
text: liability insurance – provides compensation for damages which the insured is legally obligated to pay; covers others when you are at fault

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › L · ¶4
text: light truck – a truck with a manufacturer’s rated carrying capacity of not more than 2,000 lbs., including a pick up truck, panel delivery truck, and carry-all truck

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › L · ¶5
text: limited use lanes – traffic flow lanes posted and designed to accommodate special vehicles or carpools

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › M · ¶1
text: median – area of ground separating traffic moving in opposite directions

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › M · ¶2
text: merging area – stretch of road at the end of an acceleration lane on an expressway where vehicles join the flow of traffic

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › M · ¶3
text: minimum speed limit – speed limit to keep traffic moving safely by not allowing drivers to drive slower than a certain speed

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › M · ¶4
text: moped – a motor-driven cycle that cannot attain a speed in one mile of more than 30 mph and the engine:

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › M · item 1
text: Cannot produce more than two-brake horsepower; and

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › M · item 2
text: If an internal combustion engine, has a piston displacement of 50 cubic centimeters or less and connects to a power drive system that does not require the operator to shift gears. Two-wheeled vehicle that can be driven with either a motor or pedal.

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › M · ¶5
text: motorcycle – a motor vehicle, other than a tractor, equipped with a rider’s saddle and designed to have when propelled not more than three wheels on the ground

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › N · ¶1
text: night blindness – not being able to see well at night

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › N · ¶2
text: no-fault insurance – covers an insured’s losses and expenses associated with a collision regardless of fault

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › O · ¶1
text: odometer – the device on the instrument panel indicating the total number of miles the vehicle has been driven

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › O · ¶2
text: over driving headlights – driving at a speed making your stopping distance longer than the distance lighted by your headlights; low beams are limited to 45 mph and high beams are limited to 65 mph for stopping purposes

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › O · ¶3
text: oversteer – when the rear tire patches lose varying degrees of traction and the front tire patches have more traction causing a spinning effect (yaw) around the vehicle’s center of gravity. The vehicle has a tendency to spin to the left or right even though the driver is not turning the steering wheel

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › O · ¶4
text: overtake – to pass the vehicle ahead

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › O · ¶5
text: over-the-counter medicine – drug that can be obtained legally without a doctor’s prescription

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › P · ¶1
text: parallel parking – the vehicle lines up parallel or going the same direction as the curb. When parallel parking, the vehicle must be 6 to 18 inches from the curb

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › P · ¶2
text: passive restraint device – a restraint device, such as an airbag or an automatic safety belt, that works without the passenger or driver initiating the device

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › P · ¶3
text: pedestrian – a person on foot

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › P · ¶4
text: pedestrian signal – a signal used at traffic intersections that indicates when a person should walk or wait

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › P · ¶5
text: peer pressure – mental and social influence of others of a similar age on decision-making skills

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › P · ¶6
text: perception distance – the distance your vehicle travels during perception time

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › P · ¶7
text: perception time – the length of time it takes for the driver to make a risk-reduction decision

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › P · ¶8
text: peripheral vision – the area a person can see that is around the central field of vision

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › P · ¶9
text: perpendicular parking – the vehicle is parked at a right angle to a curb or parking stripe using visual reference points for entering and leaving

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › P · ¶10
text: prescription medicine – drug that can be purchased legally only when ordered by a doctor

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › P · ¶11
text: preventive maintenance – routine care and attention to your vehicle

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › P · ¶12
text: property-damage insurance – protects the driver who is at fault against claims for damages to another person’s property, up to specified limits

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › P · ¶13
text: protected left turn – left turn made on a left-turn, green arrow, or delayed green light while oncoming traffic is stopped

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › P · ¶14
text: protective gear – the items a motorcyclist wears to protect head, eyes, and body

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › R · ¶1
text: race – the use of one or more vehicles in an attempt to:

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › R · item 1
text: Out gain or outdistance another vehicle or prevent another vehicle from passing;

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › R · item 2
text: Arrive at a given destination ahead of another vehicle(s); or

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › R · item 3
text: Test the physical stamina or endurance of an operator over a long-distance driving route

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › R · ¶2
text: reaction distance – the distance a vehicle travels from the point the driver perceives the need to act and the point where the driver takes action through braking, steering, or acceleration. Distance your vehicle travels until the driver perceives the need to change speed or position

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › R · ¶3
text: reaction time – the time the vehicle travels from the point the driver perceives the need to act and the point where the driver takes the action through braking, steering, or acceleration. Length of time it takes the driver to execute a reduced-risk action, after a response is perceived by the driver

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › R · ¶4
text: reduced visibility – the inability of a driver to see clearly

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › R · ¶5
text: reference point – a part of the outside or inside of a vehicle, as viewed from the driver’s seat, that relates to some part of the road which allows the driver to estimate position on the road. The road positions (points of reference) of the vehicle assist the driver in determining when to start turning, vehicle limitations, or where the vehicle is actually located

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › R · ¶6
text: regulatory sign – a sign controlling traffic

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › R · ¶7
text: restraint device – any part of a vehicle holding an occupant in the seat during a collision

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › R · ¶8
text: restricted interlock license – authorizes an individual to operate a motor vehicle equipped with an ignition interlock device

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › R · ¶9
text: revocation – the termination of a driver license or privilege for an indefinite period of time. May be restored when all requirements for the revocation have been satisfied

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › R · ¶10
text: right of way – privilege of having immediate use of a certain part of a road

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › R · ¶11
text: right turn on red – turning right when the red signal is on, after stopping behind the intersection guides, unless specifically prohibited to turn

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › R · ¶12
text: roadway marking – markings and lane delineators (reflectors) providing you with warning or direction

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › R · ¶13
text: rocking a vehicle – repeating the sequence of driving forward a little then back a little to move your vehicle out of deep snow, mud, or sand

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › R · ¶14
text: rumble strips – sections of rough pavement intended to alert drivers of approaching roadway construction, tollbooth plaza, or other traffic conditions

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › S · ¶1
text: safety belt – a lap belt and any shoulder straps included as original equipment on or added to a vehicle

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › S · ¶2
text: safety chains – backup link used in case a trailer hitch fails

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › S · ¶3
text: school zone – portion of a street or highway near a school subject to special speed limits

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › S · ¶4
text: shared left-turn lane – the lane on a busy street helping drivers make safe mid-block left turns into business areas from a center lane

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › S · ¶5
text: skid – occurs when tire patches lose part or all of their traction on the roadway surface due to abrupt suspension balance or roadway surfaces conditions

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › S · ¶6
text: skid mark – a mark on the road surface from a tire sliding due to a loss of traction from braking or abrupt steering

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › S · ¶7
text: slow-moving vehicle – the vehicle is unable to travel at highway speed

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › S · ¶8
text: speed smear – occurs when objects in your peripheral vision become blurred and distorted as your speed increases

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › S · ¶9
text: staggered stop – stopping when the white line visually disappears under the hood line. This allows extra space for left-turning vehicles

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › S · ¶10
text: standard reference point – point which allows for vehicle placement on a road typical for most drivers

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › S · ¶11
text: stimulant – drug that speeds up the central nervous system

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › S · ¶12
text: stopping position – stopping behind a vehicle in a position allowing the driver enough space to steer around the vehicle to avoid a stalled, turning, or backing vehicle

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › S · ¶13
text: suspension – the temporary withdrawal of a driver license or privilege for a definite period of time

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › T · ¶1
text: tailgate – to follow another vehicle too closely

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › T · ¶2
text: total stopping distance – the distance your vehicle travels while you make a stop

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › T · ¶3
text: traction – friction or gripping power between the tire patches and the road surface

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › T · ¶4
text: traffic circle – the intersections that form when several roads meet at a circle

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › T · ¶5
text: traffic control devices – any signal, sign, or pavement marking used to control the movement of traffic

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › T · ¶6
text: traffic signal – any signal used to control the movement of traffic

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › T · ¶7
text: tunnel vision – the ability to see in a narrow field of vision of 140 degrees or less with little effective peripheral vision

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › T · ¶8
text: turn – vehicle maneuver to change direction to the left or right

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › T · ¶9
text: turnabout – the maneuvers for turning into or out of a road/driveway using reference points for positioning

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › U · ¶1
text: uncontrolled intersection – an intersection that has no signs or signals to regulate traffic including railroad crossings that do not have flashing red lights or crossing gates

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › U · ¶2
text: under-insured motorist insurance – covers costs exceeding the amount the other person’s insurance company will pay as a result of a collision caused by another’s fault

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › U · ¶3
text: uninsured motorist insurance – covers costs up to a certain amount if you are struck by another vehicle whose driver has no insurance

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › U · ¶4
text: unprotected left turn – left turn made at a signal-controlled intersection without a special left turn light

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › U · ¶5
text: urban district – the territory adjacent to and including a highway, if the territory is improved with structures used for business, industry, or dwelling houses and are located at intervals of less than 100 feet for a distance of at least one-quarter mile on either side of the highway

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › V · ¶1
text: vehicle – a device, in, upon, or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway, excepting devices used exclusively upon stationary rails or tracks

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › V · ¶2
text: vehicle malfunctions – failures of the vehicle to perform as designed, such as tire, steering, suspension, acceleration, fuel, etc.

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › V · ¶3
text: vehicle maintenance – the scheduled or unscheduled upkeep or repair of a vehicle

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › V · ¶4
text: vehicle maneuvers – moving forward, moving backward, turning, lateral maneuvers, and turnabouts

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › V · ¶5
text: visibility – the ability to see

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › W · ¶1
text: warning sign – a sign alerting you to possible hazards and road conditions

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › W · ¶2
text: warning light – an instrument panel light warning of a system malfunction and usually stays on while the system is malfunctioning

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › Y · ¶1
text: yield – to allow another vehicle or roadway user to proceed first

locator: Appendix A: Glossary of Terms › Z · ¶1
text: zero tolerance law – it is illegal for individuals who are under 21 years of age to drive with any measurable amount of alcohol in their blood

locator: Appendix B: Driver License Offices › Intro · ¶1
text: DPS offers appointments for in-person DL/ID services at more than 220 driver license offices (DLO) statewide. We have offices ranging from one person, part-time offices to mega centers that offer up to 25 service counters, provide more flexible hours and employ more License and Permit Specialists to serve customers.

locator: Appendix B: Driver License Offices › Intro · ¶2
text: We encourage customers to utilize alternative service options such as online, telephone, or mail-in renewals when eligible. The department is working to make more service options available online to reduce the number of required DLO visits. We are also expanding third party education and testing options to provide more flexibility to customers who are getting a license for the first time.

locator: Appendix B: Driver License Offices › Intro · ¶3
text: All in person DL/ID services are provided by scheduled appointment.

locator: Appendix B: Driver License Offices › Intro · ¶4
text: Visit the DPS website at https://www.dps.texas.gov/DriverLicense/appointments.htm to find an office near you and schedule your appointment. Appointments may be booked up to six months in advance. Select the option to schedule a driver license appointment and follow the instructions to make your appointment. If you are unable to keep your appointment, please cancel it so other customers may be served promptly.

locator: Appendix B: Driver License Offices › Intro · ¶5
text: Visit the DPS website at https://www.dps.texas.gov/DriverLicense/ for the latest information about driver license offices and services.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Who May Drive a Motor Vehicle in Texas? · ¶1
text: Individuals who meet the following criteria may drive a motor vehicle in Texas.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Who May Drive a Motor Vehicle in Texas? · ¶2
text: Residents:

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Who May Drive a Motor Vehicle in Texas? · item 1
text: Texas residents who have a valid Texas driver license

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Who May Drive a Motor Vehicle in Texas? · item 2
text: New residents who are exchanging a valid out-of-state license have 90 days to establish residency in Texas in order to secure a Texas driver license.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Who May Drive a Motor Vehicle in Texas? · item 3
text: Any person, while driving or operating any road machine, farm tractor, or implement of husbandry temporarily operated or moved on a highway is exempt from having a Texas license, unless the vehicle is a commercial motor vehicle

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Who May Drive a Motor Vehicle in Texas? · ¶3
text: Nonresidents:

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Who May Drive a Motor Vehicle in Texas? · item 4
text: Any nonresident who is at least 16 years of age and possesses a valid driver license issued in the nonresident’s home state or Canadian province. Nonresidents at least 16 years of age who meet these criteria may drive a vehicle permitted to be operated with a Class C or Class M driver license in Texas

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Who May Drive a Motor Vehicle in Texas? · item 5
text: Nonresidents who are at least 18 years of age may drive any vehicle in Texas if they are legally licensed to drive such a vehicle in their home state or country, and the home state or country grants like recognition (reciprocity) to citizens of Texas

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Who May Drive a Motor Vehicle in Texas? · ¶4
text: Military:

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Who May Drive a Motor Vehicle in Texas? · item 6
text: The driver of an official U.S. or state military service motor vehicle may drive a vehicle without a valid Texas driver license, unless the vehicle is a commercial motor vehicle

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Who May Drive a Motor Vehicle in Texas? · item 7
text: A nonresident on active duty in the U.S. armed forces, the member’s spouse, or dependent child who has a valid license issued by his/her home state

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Who May Drive a Motor Vehicle in Texas? · item 8
text: Any person on active military duty who holds a valid driver license issued by the U.S. armed forces in a foreign country may drive a motor vehicle in Texas for 90 days from the date of their return to the U.S.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Who May Drive a Motor Vehicle in Texas? · item 9
text: Unless a license is suspended, cancelled, revoked or denied, a Texas driver license held by any person who enters or who is in the U.S. armed forces will remain valid as long as the:

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Who May Drive a Motor Vehicle in Texas? · item 10
text: Service continues; and

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Who May Drive a Motor Vehicle in Texas? · item 11
text: Person remains absent from Texas and the absence does not exceed 90 days from the date the licensee is honorably separated from service or returns to Texas

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Who May Drive a Motor Vehicle in Texas? · ¶5
text: Special Note: You may not receive a Texas driver license until all valid driver licenses and IDs issued are surrendered.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Learner License (Instruction Permit) · ¶1
text: A learner license, also known as an instruction permit, allows a student driver to legally practice driving when accompanied by a licensed driver. The licensed driver must be at least 21 years of age with at least one year of driving experience, must occupy the seat beside the driver, and cannot be intoxicated, asleep, or engaging in any activity that prevents observation and response to the actions of the driver. A learner license will indicate “Learner License” on the front of the card and expire on the minor’s 18th birthday. A person applying for a learner license must:

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Learner License (Instruction Permit) · item 1
text: Be at least 15 but no more than 18 years of age

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Learner License (Instruction Permit) · item 2
text: Complete the classroom portion of a driver education course, vision exam, and knowledge exam

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Learner License (Instruction Permit) · item 3
text: Meet all other requirements for a first time driver license (original) applicant

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Learner License (Instruction Permit) · row 1
text: 15 with driver education | $15 for license + $1 fee = $16 | For applicants less than 18 years of age, the license expires on their 18th birthday

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Learner License (Instruction Permit) · row 2
text: * A $1 administrative fee is included in most transactions. However, if you are completing multiple transactions at the same time, either in-person, telephone or online, then you will only be charged the $1 administrative fee once. A $1 administrative fee is not charged for transactions made through the mail.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Learner License (Instruction Permit) · ¶2
text: Applicants 18 years of age and older who wish to legally practice driving are issued a Class C license with the same restrictions as a learner license. The license is generally valid for eight years and costs $32 plus a $1 administrative fee.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Verification of Enrollment and Attendance (VOE) Form · ¶1
text: If you are under 18 years of age and applying for your first Texas driver license, learner license, or provisional license, you must provide evidence that you:

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Verification of Enrollment and Attendance (VOE) Form · item 1
text: Have obtained a high school diploma or its equivalent; or

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Verification of Enrollment and Attendance (VOE) Form · item 2
text: Are a student enrolled in a public, private, or home school and attended school for at least 80 days in the fall or spring semester preceding the date of application; or

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Verification of Enrollment and Attendance (VOE) Form · item 3
text: Have been enrolled for at least 45 days and are enrolled at the time of application in a program to prepare individuals to pass the high school equivalency exam.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Verification of Enrollment and Attendance (VOE) Form · ¶2
text: This information is included on the Verification of Enrollment and Attendance (VOE) form issued by your school. Ask your school officials to complete and sign the VOE form. The VOE may not be dated more than 30 days before the date of application for a license during the school year or more than 90 days during the summer. The VOE must be presented to the license and permit specialist (LPS) when applying for an original or first time license.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Hardship License · ¶1
text: A hardship license (previously known as Minor Restricted Driver License or MRDL) may be issued to a minor who establishes the necessity to drive and may have restrictions based on the qualifying hardship.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Hardship License · ¶2
text: An application for a hardship license (DL-77) must be executed by an authorized adult on behalf of the minor. Both the adult and the minor must sign the form and present it in person at the driver license office. Only a parent, guardian, or person having custody of a minor may apply on behalf of a minor. If the minor does not have a parent, guardian, or custodian, then an employer or county judge may apply on behalf of the minor.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Hardship License · ¶3
text: A person applying for a hardship license must:

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Hardship License · item 1
text: Be at least 15 years of age but not more than 18

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Hardship License · item 2
text: Complete and pass a driver education course (a driver education course includes both the classroom and behind the wheel phase), vision, knowledge, and driving exams

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Hardship License · item 3
text: Meet all other requirements for a first-time driver license (original) applicant.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Hardship License · ¶4
text: For more information, please visit our website, https://www.dps.texas.gov/DriverLicense/teenDriver.htm .

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Hardship License · ¶5
text: DPS may require supporting documentation or conduct an investigation to confirm the information provided on the application.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Hardship License · ¶6
text: DPS will issue a hardship license if it is determined that:

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Hardship License · item 4
text: Failure to issue the hardship license will result in an unusual economic hardship for the family of the minor applicant

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Hardship License · item 5
text: The hardship license is necessary due to an illness, disability, or death of a family member

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Hardship License · item 6
text: The hardship license is necessary because the minor applicant is enrolled in a vocational education program that requires a license for participation

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Hardship License · item 7
text: A court order requiring the issuance of the hardship license is presented

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Graduated Driver License (GDL) · ¶1
text: Teenagers and young adults have the highest crash rates of all drivers, and motor vehicle crashes are the leading cause of death for U.S. teens. Young drivers make up 6.5 percent of the driving population but are responsible for 13 percent of fatal crashes. The Graduated Driver License (GDL) program eases teens into the driving experience by phasing in driving privileges and minimizing exposure to high-risk situations.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Graduated Driver License (GDL) · ¶2
text: The GDL program applies to driver license applicants under 18 years of age and has contributed to a decrease in fatal crashes. As a part of this program, all new driver license applicants are required to pass a driving exam conducted at a driver license office or authorized testing facility.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Graduated Driver License (GDL) · ¶3
text: The GDL program consists of two phases. Phase One applies to learner licenses. Phase Two applies to provisional licenses. All drivers less than 18 years of age must meet the licensing requirements for a learner license or provisional license, but they are also subject to additional requirements, including driver education and the GDL program.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Graduated Driver License (GDL) · ¶4
text: Phase One: This phase requires applicants under 18 years of age to hold a valid learner, hardship, or combination of learner and hardship license for a minimum of six months prior to the issuance of a provisional license.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Graduated Driver License (GDL) · ¶5
text: If your license is suspended during Phase One, then the initial six-month period is extended by the number of days of the suspension because your license is invalid during the suspension period.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Graduated Driver License (GDL) · ¶6
text: A Texas learner license will be issued to new Texas residents who are at least 15 years of age, present an out-of-state instruction permit, and submit a VOE form. A Texas learner license must be held for six months from the date of issuance before the individual is eligible for Phase Two.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Graduated Driver License (GDL) · ¶7
text: Phase One requirements do not apply to Class M (motorcycle) licenses. Under the GDL program, there is no minimum time a person must hold a restricted motorcycle license before applying for a Class M license.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Graduated Driver License (GDL) · ¶8
text: Phase Two: Phase Two restricts the driving privileges of individuals until their 18th birthday following the issuance of a provisional license.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Graduated Driver License (GDL) · ¶9
text: During Phase, Two these individuals may not drive a motor vehicle:

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Graduated Driver License (GDL) · item 1
text: With more than one passenger in the vehicle under the age of 21 who is not a family member

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Graduated Driver License (GDL) · item 2
text: Between midnight and 5:00 a.m. unless the operation of the vehicle is necessary for the driver to work, to attend or participate in a school-related activity, or due to a medical emergency

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Graduated Driver License (GDL) · ¶10
text: All drivers who are under 18 years of age are restricted from using a wireless communication device, including a hands-free device, except in case of an emergency.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Provisional License · ¶1
text: A provisional license is a driver license issued to persons 16 to 18 years of age that has the Phase Two GDL driving restrictions applied. The license will be marked “PROVISIONAL” and expire on the license holder’s 18th birthday. A person applying for a provisional license must:

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Provisional License · item 1
text: Be at least 16 but not more than 18 years of age

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Provisional License · item 2
text: Complete and pass a driver education course (a driver education course includes both the classroom and behind the wheel phases), vision, and driving exams

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Provisional License · item 3
text: Have held a valid learner, hardship, or combination of learner and hardship license for at least six months

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Provisional License · item 4
text: Meet all other requirements for a renewal driver license applicant

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Out-of-State License Holders · ¶1
text: Applicants who are at least 15 but less than 18 years of age and present a valid out-of-state instruction permit will be issued a Phase One learner license. Applicants who are at least 16 but less than 18 years of age and present a valid out-of-state driver license will be issued a Phase Two provisional license with passenger and time restrictions after successful completion of the driving exam. Applicants must meet all other requirements for a first-time (original) applicant.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Types of Texas Driver Licenses › Out-of-State License Holders · ¶2
text: All licenses issued to persons less than 21 years of age will be marked “UNDER 21”.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Classes of Driver Licenses · ¶1
text: Class A, B, C, and M driver licenses are issued to individuals who are exempt from obtaining or not required to obtain a commercial driver license (CDL). Most non-commercial driver licenses issued to persons 18 years of age and older are valid for eight years and cost $32 (a $1 administrative fee will be added to in-person , telephone and online transactions). Some applicants receive licenses with shorter terms due to restrictions including, but not limited to, verification of lawful presence, sex offender registration requirements, or being 85 years of age or older.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Classes of Driver Licenses · ¶2
text: Individuals who operate any of the following vehicles are exempt from obtaining a CDL but may need a Class A or Class B non-commercial driver license because the type of vehicle driven still meets the definition of a commercial motor vehicle. For more information on commercial motor vehicles and requirements for a CDL, please visit our website, http://www.dps.texas.gov/DriverLicense/CommercialLicense.htm or see the Texas Commercial Motor Vehicle Drivers Handbook . You may download the handbook online at http://www.dps.texas.gov/internetforms/Forms/DL-7C.pdf .

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Classes of Driver Licenses · item 1
text: A fire-fighting or emergency vehicle necessary for the preservation of life or property or the execution of emergency governmental functions whether operated by an employee of a political subdivision or by a volunteer firefighter.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Classes of Driver Licenses · item 2
text: A military vehicle or a commercial motor vehicle when operated for military purposes by military personnel, members of the Reserves and National Guard on active duty, including personnel on full-time National Guard duty, personnel on part-time training, and National Guard military technicians.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Classes of Driver Licenses · item 3
text: A recreational vehicle driven for personal use.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Classes of Driver Licenses · item 4
text: A vehicle that is owned, leased, or controlled by an air carrier and is driven or operated exclusively by an employee of the air carrier only on the premises of an airport, on service roads to which the public does not have access.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Classes of Driver Licenses · item 5
text: A vehicle used exclusively to transport seed cotton modules or cotton burrs.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Classes of Driver Licenses · item 6
text: A former military vehicle as defined by Texas Transportation Code 504.402(i) that is operated intrastate and not driven by an individual for compensation or in furtherance of a commercial enterprise.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Classes of Driver Licenses · item 7
text: A covered farm vehicle as defined by 49 CFR Section 390.5 that is used to transport agricultural commodities, livestock, machinery or supplies to or from a farm or ranch, not used in for-hire motor carrier operations and if under 26,001 pounds is operated anywhere in the United States and if over 26,001 pounds is operated within 150 miles of the farm or ranch.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Classes of Driver Licenses · item 8
text: A vehicle controlled and operated by a farmer:

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Classes of Driver Licenses · item 9
text: Used to transport agricultural products, farm machinery, or farm supplies to or from a farm

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Classes of Driver Licenses · item 10
text: Not used in the operation of a common or contract motor carrier, or

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Classes of Driver Licenses · item 11
text: Used within 150 miles of the person’s farm.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Classes of Driver Licenses › Class A Driver License · ¶1
text: A Class A driver license permits a person to drive:

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Classes of Driver Licenses › Class A Driver License · item 1
text: Any vehicle or combination of vehicles described under a Class B or Class C driver license; and

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Classes of Driver Licenses › Class A Driver License · item 2
text: A vehicle or combination of vehicles with a gross combination weight rating (GCWR) of 26,001 lbs. or more, provided the gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) of the vehicle(s) towed is in excess of 10,000 lbs.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Classes of Driver Licenses › Class A Driver License · ¶2
text: A Class A driver license does not permit a person to drive a motorcycle.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Classes of Driver Licenses › Class C Driver License · item 3

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Classes of Driver Licenses › Class C Driver License · item 5

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Classes of Driver Licenses › Class C Driver License · item 7
text: Manufactured and certified to comply with federal safety requirements for a motorcycle

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Classes of Driver Licenses › Class M Driver License · ¶1
text: A Class M driver license permits a person to drive a motorcycle. Before applying for a Class M license, you must pass a state approved motorcycle operator training course. Motorcycle training course providers require drivers who are less than 18 years of age to present proof of completion of the classroom phase of a driver education course, hold a learner license (issued after completing the classroom phase of a driver education course), or hold a valid Class C license prior to enrolling in a motorcycle operator training course.

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Classes of Driver Licenses › Class M Driver License › Minimum Age · ¶1
text: Motorcycle: 16 with completion of the classroom phase of a driver education course (32 hours) and a state approved motorcycle operator training course (16 hours).

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Classes of Driver Licenses › Class M Driver License › Minimum Age · ¶2
text: Motorcycle of 250 cc or less: 15 years of age with DPS approval for a hardship driver license or completion of the classroom phase of a driver education course (32 hours) and a state approved motorcycle operator training course (16 hours).

locator: Chapter 1: Your License to Drive › Classes of Driver Licenses › Class M Driver License › Minimum Age · ¶3
text: For more information on Class M driver licenses, please visit our website, https://www.dps.texas.gov/DriverLicense/motorcycleLicense.htm

text: 18 and older | $32 for license + $1 administrative fee = $33 | Eight years
