locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Intro · ¶1
text: Most crashes in Texas result from speeding, failure to yield or stop appropriately, and driving under the influence of alcohol. If requested and available, exchange names, addresses, phone numbers, vehicle identification numbers, vehicle license plate numbers, driver license information, and insurance information with all drivers involved in the crash. Write the insurance company name and policy number exactly as it is shown on the driver’s proof-of-insurance card. If you have the name of the driver’s insurance company and the information is not listed directly on the insurance card, call the Texas Department of Insurance at (800) 252-3439 to get the company address and telephone number. Be sure to also note the location of the crash and write down the contact information if there are any witnesses.

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Intro · ¶2
text: You should always notify the appropriate law enforcement agency as soon as possible when:

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Intro · item 1
text: There is an injury or fatality

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Intro · item 2
text: The vehicles involved cannot be moved off the roadway

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Intro · item 3
text: A driver leaves the scene of the crash

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Intro · item 4
text: You suspect a driver is intoxicated.

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Intro · ¶3
text: If you are involved in a crash that is not investigated by a law enforcement officer and the crash has not resulted in injury or death of a person or damage to property of $1,000 or more, you must make a written report of the crash and file it with the Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) no later than the 10th day after the date of the crash. The written report must be on a TxDOT specified form. For a copy of this form, please visit the TxDOT website at www.txdot.gov .

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Crash Resulting in Injury to, or Death of a person · ¶1
text: If you are operating a motor vehicle involved in a crash resulting in injury to or death of a person, you must immediately stop your vehicle at the scene of the crash (or as close as possible to the scene of the crash) without obstructing traffic more than necessary. If you did not stop your vehicle at the scene, you must immediately return and remain at the scene of the crash until you have complied with the following:

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Crash Resulting in Injury to, or Death of a person · item 1
text: Provide your name and address, the registration number of the vehicle you were driving, and the name of your motor vehicle liability insurer to any person injured, or to the operator or occupant of, or person attending a vehicle involved in the collision

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Crash Resulting in Injury to, or Death of a person · item 2
text: Show your driver license (if requested and available) to any person injured, or to the operator or occupant of, or person attending a vehicle involved in the collision

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Crash Resulting in Injury to, or Death of a person · item 3
text: Provide any person injured in the crash reasonable assistance including, transporting or making arrangements for transporting the person to a physician or hospital for medical treatment, if it is apparent treatment is necessary, or if the injured person requests the transportation.

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Crash Resulting in Injury to, or Death of a person · row 1
text: 1st offense crash resulting in a death of a person | Second degree felony punishable by a fine not to exceed $10,000 and imprisonment in the Texas Department of Criminal Justice (TDCJ) for 2 to 20 years.

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Crash Resulting in Injury to, or Death of a person · row 2
text: 1st offense crash resulting in serious bodily injury | Third degree felony punishable by a fine not to exceed $10,000 and imprisonment in the Texas Department of Criminal Justice (TDCJ) for 2 to 10 years.

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Crash Resulting in Injury to, or Death of a person · row 3
text: 1st offense crash resulting in injury | Imprisonment in the Texas Department of Criminal Justice (TDCJ) for up to 5 years or confinement in the county jail for up to 1 year; a fine not to exceed $5,000; or both a fine and imprisonment.

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Crash Resulting in Damage to a Vehicle · ¶1
text: If you are operating a motor vehicle involved in a crash resulting ONLY in damage to a vehicle that is driven or attended by a person, you must immediately stop your vehicle at the scene of the crash or as close as possible to the scene of the crash without obstructing traffic more than necessary. If the crash occurs on a main lane, ramp, shoulder, median, or adjacent area and each vehicle involved can be normally and safely driven, drivers must move their vehicle as soon as possible to a designated crash investigation site, if available, a location on the frontage road, the nearest suitable cross street, or other suitable location. If you did not stop your vehicle at the scene, you must immediately return and remain at the scene of the crash until you have complied with the following:

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Crash Resulting in Damage to a Vehicle · item 1
text: Provide your name and address, the registration number of the vehicle you were driving, and the name of your motor vehicle liability insurer to any person injured, or to the operator or occupant of, or person attending a vehicle involved in the collision

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Crash Resulting in Damage to a Vehicle · item 2
text: Show your driver license (if requested and available) to any operator or occupant of, or person attending a vehicle involved in the collision

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Crash Resulting in Damage to a Vehicle · row 1
text: 1st offense (Less than $200 in damages) | Class C misdemeanor and is punishable by a fine not to exceed $500.

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Crash Resulting in Damage to a Vehicle · row 2
text: 1st offense ($200 or more in damages) | Class B misdemeanor and is punishable by a fine not to exceed $2,000, confinement in jail for up to 180 days, or both.

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Crash Involving an Unattended Vehicle · ¶1
text: If you are operating a motor vehicle that collides with and damages an unattended vehicle, you must immediately stop and either:

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Crash Involving an Unattended Vehicle · item 1
text: Locate the operator or owner of the unattended vehicle and give your name and address

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Crash Involving an Unattended Vehicle · item 2
text: Securely attach a written notice in a visible way to the unattended vehicle providing:

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Crash Involving an Unattended Vehicle · item 3
text: Your name and address

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Crash Involving an Unattended Vehicle · item 4
text: A statement of the circumstances of the collision.

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Crash Involving an Unattended Vehicle · row 1
text: 1st offense (Less than $200 in damages) | Class C misdemeanor and is punishable by a fine not to exceed $500.

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Crash Involving an Unattended Vehicle · row 2
text: 1st offense ($200 or more in damages) | Class B misdemeanor and is punishable by a fine not to exceed $2,000, confinement in jail for up to 180 days, or both.

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Crash Resulting in Damages to a Fixture, Landscaping, or Structure · ¶1
text: If you are driving a motor vehicle involved in a crash resulting ONLY in damage to a fixture, landscaping, or structure legally on or adjacent to a highway, you must:

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Crash Resulting in Damages to a Fixture, Landscaping, or Structure · item 1
text: Take reasonable steps to locate the owner (or person in charge) of the property and notify him/her of the crash

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Crash Resulting in Damages to a Fixture, Landscaping, or Structure · item 2
text: Provide your name, address, and registration number of the vehicle you were driving

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Crash Resulting in Damages to a Fixture, Landscaping, or Structure · item 3
text: If requested and available, you must show your driver license to the owner or person in charge of the property

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Crash Resulting in Damages to a Fixture, Landscaping, or Structure · item 4
text: If the crash is not investigated by a law enforcement officer and the crash has not resulted in injury to or the death of a person or damage to the property of any one person to an apparent extent of $1,000 or more, you must make a written report of the crash and file it with the TxDOT no later than the 10th day after the crash.

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Crash Resulting in Damages to a Fixture, Landscaping, or Structure · row 1
text: 1st offense (Less than $200 in damages) | Class C misdemeanor and is punishable by a fine not to exceed $500.

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Crash Resulting in Damages to a Fixture, Landscaping, or Structure · row 2
text: 1st offense ($200 or more in damages) | Class B misdemeanor and is punishable by a fine not to exceed $2,000, confinement in jail for up to 180 days, or both.

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Hit-and-Run Crashes · ¶1
text: If you are involved in a hit-and-run crash, report this crash to law enforcement for investigation. The Texas Department of Insurance advises uninsured motorist coverage will pay for damages in hit-and-run crashes reported to a law enforcement agency.

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Aiding the Injured · ¶1
text: In the event you are involved in a crash that injures another person, consider the information below:

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Aiding the Injured · item 1
text: When calling a doctor or ambulance, ensure you take notice of your surroundings and state the location of the crash clearly and correctly.

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Aiding the Injured · item 2
text: Do not assume people are not injured simply because they say they are not. Send for skilled help as quickly as possible. Unskilled handling can do more harm than good.

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Aiding the Injured · item 3
text: Do not move or lift the victim(s) unless it is absolutely necessary. If a victim must be moved, get help and try not to change the position in which the victim was found.

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Aiding the Injured · item 4
text: Stop serious bleeding with thick cloth pads, as clean as possible, apply with pressure by hand or by bandaging.

locator: Chapter 11: Motor Vehicle Crashes › Aiding the Injured · item 5
text: Keep the victim(s) comfortable. If it is hot, cool the victim(s) and provide shade as much as possible. If it is cool, cover the victim with blankets or coats if necessary and if available.

locator: Chapter 12: Pedestrian Safety › Intro · ¶1
text: A driver should always pay special attention to pedestrians (persons on foot). However, there are certain safety rules pedestrians should follow.

locator: Chapter 12: Pedestrian Safety › Laws and Safety Tips for Pedestrians · item 1
text: Obey traffic control signals unless otherwise directed by a pedestrian control signal.

locator: Chapter 12: Pedestrian Safety › Laws and Safety Tips for Pedestrians · item 2
text: Do not cross the street between two intersections. It is dangerous to cross in the middle of a street.

locator: Chapter 12: Pedestrian Safety › Laws and Safety Tips for Pedestrians · item 3
text: Use sidewalks when available, and do not walk in the street.

locator: Chapter 12: Pedestrian Safety › Laws and Safety Tips for Pedestrians · item 4
text: Walk on the left side of the road if there are no sidewalks. Step off the pavement when a car approaches.

locator: Chapter 12: Pedestrian Safety › Laws and Safety Tips for Pedestrians · item 5
text: If you cross a street at any point other than within a crosswalk at an intersection, you (the pedestrian) must yield the right-of-way to all vehicles.

locator: Chapter 12: Pedestrian Safety › Laws and Safety Tips for Pedestrians · item 6
text: If you cross a street without using a pedestrian tunnel or overhead pedestrian crossing which has been provided, you (the pedestrian) must yield the right-of-way to all vehicles.

locator: Chapter 12: Pedestrian Safety › Laws and Safety Tips for Pedestrians · item 7
text: When crossing at a crosswalk, keep right if possible.

locator: Chapter 12: Pedestrian Safety › Laws and Safety Tips for Pedestrians · item 8
text: Blind, partially blind, or disabled individuals may carry a white cane while walking. Others must not display a white cane on any public street or highway.

locator: Chapter 12: Pedestrian Safety › Laws and Safety Tips for Pedestrians · item 9
text: No person may stand in the road for the purpose of soliciting a ride, contributions, or business. A person may stand in a road to solicit a charitable contribution if authorized to do so by the local authority having jurisdiction over the road.

locator: Chapter 12: Pedestrian Safety › Laws and Safety Tips for Pedestrians · item 10
text: Do not suddenly walk or run into the street in the path of a vehicle. These sudden actions may make it impossible for the vehicle operator to yield.

locator: Chapter 12: Pedestrian Safety › Laws and Safety Tips for Pedestrians · item 11
text: Wait on the curb, not in the street, until the traffic signals change to green or read “Walk.”

locator: Chapter 12: Pedestrian Safety › Laws and Safety Tips for Pedestrians · item 12
text: Always wear white or light colored clothing and/or carry a light or reflector when walking at night.

locator: Chapter 12: Pedestrian Safety › Laws and Safety Tips for Pedestrians · item 13
text: Look both ways before crossing the street and before stepping out from behind parked cars.

locator: Chapter 12: Pedestrian Safety › Laws and Safety Tips for Pedestrians · item 14
text: Be extra careful when getting off a streetcar or bus.

locator: Chapter 12: Pedestrian Safety › Laws and Safety Tips for Pedestrians · item 15
text: Get in and out of cars on the curb side of the road when possible.

locator: Chapter 12: Pedestrian Safety › Laws and Safety Tips for Pedestrians · item 16
text: Do not walk on a road when you are under the influence or consuming an alcoholic beverage. Alcohol is a contributing factor to pedestrian traffic crashes.

locator: Chapter 12: Pedestrian Safety › Laws and Safety Tips for Pedestrians · item 17
text: Pedestrians should be aware that local authorities may have ordinances that require pedestrians to comply with the directions of an official traffic control device (signals, signs, etc.) and prohibit pedestrians from crossing a road in a business district or a designated highway, except in a crosswalk.

locator: Chapter 12: Pedestrian Safety › Laws and Safety Tips for Pedestrians · image
heading: Alt text: “Sign: PUSH BUTTON FOR GREEN (pedestrian push-button sign)”
text: Sign: PUSH BUTTON FOR GREEN (pedestrian push-button sign)

locator: Chapter 12: Pedestrian Safety › Laws and Safety Tips for Motorists · item 1
text: If you see a pedestrian crossing or attempting to cross the street, slow down, use your horn if necessary, and be prepared to stop.

locator: Chapter 12: Pedestrian Safety › Laws and Safety Tips for Motorists · item 2
text: Be alert to a pedestrian guided by an assistance animal or carrying a white cane. The white cane indicates the person may be blind, partially blind, or disabled. A driver shall take the necessary pre-cautions to avoid injuring or endangering a pedestrian crossing or attempting to cross the street. The driver shall bring the vehicle to a full stop if injury or danger can only be avoided by that action.

locator: Chapter 12: Pedestrian Safety › Laws and Safety Tips for Motorists · item 3
text: Watch for individuals who are blind at bus stops, intersections, business areas, and near schools for the blind.

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Traffic Laws · ¶1
text: A bicycle is a vehicle. Any person riding a bicycle has the same rights and responsibilities that apply to a driver operating a vehicle unless these cannot, by their nature, apply to a person operating a bicycle.

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Traffic Laws · ¶2
text: Any person who operates a bicycle is subject to the same penalties for violating a traffic law as a person operating a motor vehicle. All traffic convictions will be placed on the individual’s driver record, regardless if the conviction was for an offense committed on a bicycle or in a motor vehicle.

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Traffic Laws › Do’s · item 1
text: Always obey all traffic laws, signs, and signals. Stop at all stop signs and red lights.

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Traffic Laws › Do’s · item 2
text: Always ride with the flow of traffic.

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Traffic Laws › Do’s · item 3
text: Only ride on or astride a permanent and regular seat.

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Traffic Laws › Do’s · item 4
text: When operating a bicycle on a one-way road with two or more marked traffic lanes, ride as near as possible to the left curb or edge of the road.

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Traffic Laws › Do’s · item 5
text: Individuals riding two abreast on a “laned” road must ride in a single lane and not impede the flow of traffic.

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Traffic Laws › Do’s · item 6
text: Bicyclists may ride on the shoulder of the road.

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Traffic Laws › Do’s · item 7
text: Bicyclists must signal a turn or stop by:

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Traffic Laws › Do’s · item 8
text: Using either their left arm pointing up or their right arm pointed horizontally to signal a right turn.

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Traffic Laws › Do’s · item 9
text: Using their left arm pointed horizontally to signal a left turn.

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Traffic Laws › Do’s · item 10
text: Using their left arm pointed downward to signal a stop.

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Traffic Laws › Do’s · item 11
text: A person operating a bicycle who is moving slower than the other traffic on the road shall ride as near as possible to the right curb or edge of the road unless:

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Traffic Laws › Do’s · item 12
text: The person is overtaking and passing another vehicle proceeding in the same direction

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Traffic Laws › Do’s · item 13
text: The person is preparing for a left turn at an intersection or onto a private road or driveway

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Traffic Laws › Do’s · item 14
text: There are unsafe conditions in the road such as fixed or moving objects, parked or moving vehicles, pedestrians, animals, potholes, or debris, or

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Traffic Laws › Do’s · item 15
text: The person is operating a bicycle in an outside lane that is: Less than 14 feet in width and doesn’t have a designated bicycle lane adjacent to that lane; or The lane is too narrow for a bicycle and a motor vehicle to safely travel side by side.

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Traffic Laws › Do’s · item 16
text: Less than 14 feet in width and doesn’t have a designated bicycle lane adjacent to that lane; or

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Traffic Laws › Do’s · item 17
text: The lane is too narrow for a bicycle and a motor vehicle to safely travel side by side.

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Traffic Laws › Do’s › Don’ts · item 1
text: Never carry more than the number of individuals it is designated or equipped for.

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Traffic Laws › Do’s › Don’ts · item 2
text: Never ride opposite the flow of traffic.

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Traffic Laws › Do’s › Don’ts · item 3
text: Never attach the bicycle or person to a moving streetcar or vehicle upon a road.

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Traffic Laws › Do’s › Don’ts · item 4
text: Never carry any package, bundle, or article which prevents the rider from keeping at least one hand on the handlebars.

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Shared Lane Marking · ¶1
text: The shared lane marking may be used to:

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Shared Lane Marking · image
heading: Alt text: “Illustration in the handbook section “Shared Lane Marking” (no caption in the PDF)”
text: Illustration in the handbook section “Shared Lane Marking” (no caption in the PDF)

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Shared Lane Marking · item 1
text: Assist bicyclists with lateral positioning in a shared lane with on-street parallel parking in order to reduce the chance of a bicyclist impacting the open door of a parked vehicle

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Shared Lane Marking · item 2
text: Assist bicyclists with lateral position in lanes too narrow for a motor vehicle and a bicycle to travel side by side within the same traffic lane

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Shared Lane Marking · item 3
text: Alert road users of the lateral location bicyclists are likely to occupy within the traveled way

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Shared Lane Marking · item 4
text: Encourage safe passing of bicyclists by motorists, or

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Shared Lane Marking · item 5
text: Reduce the incidence of wrong-way bicycling

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Shared Lane Marking · ¶2
text: Shared Lane Marking

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycles Must Be Properly Equipped · item 1
text: Every bicycle must be equipped with a brake, which will enable the operator to make the wheels skid on dry, level, clean pavement when applied.

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycles Must Be Properly Equipped · item 2
text: Hearing-impaired bicycle riders may display a safety flag.

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycles Must Be Properly Equipped · item 3
text: Every bicycle used at nighttime must be equipped with:

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycles Must Be Properly Equipped · item 4
text: A lamp on the front emits a white light visible from a distance of at least 500 feet in front of the bicycle, and

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycles Must Be Properly Equipped · item 5
text: A red, DPS-approved reflector on the rear visible from distances of 50 feet to 300 feet. (A red light on the rear visible from a distance of 500 feet may be used in addition to the red reflector.)

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Safety Guidelines · item 1
text: You may be required by law to wear a helmet depending on your local laws.

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Safety Guidelines · item 2
text: When riding on pedestrian facilities, reduce speed and exercise caution.

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Safety Guidelines · item 3
text: Do not weave in and out of parked cars.

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Safety Guidelines · item 4
text: Move off the street to stop, park, or make repairs to your bicycle.

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Safety Guidelines · item 5
text: Select a route according to the rider’s bicycling skill and experience.

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Safety Guidelines · item 6
text: Bicycles may be equipped with a mirror.

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Bicycle Safety Guidelines · item 7
text: Wear light colored or reflective clothing to make it easier for drivers to see you.

locator: Chapter 13: Bicycle Laws and Safety › Riding in Wet Weather · ¶1
text: Water makes certain surfaces slick. Be aware of manhole covers and painted stripes on the road. Water also obscures some hazards. Watch for potholes filled with water. In addition, the visibility of motorists is greatly decreased in wet weather.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Defensive Driving · ¶1
text: To avoid crashes, the defensive driver should:

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Defensive Driving · item 1
text: Stay alert and keep eyes moving to keep track of what is happening at all times

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Defensive Driving · item 2
text: Look for trouble spots developing all around

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Defensive Driving · item 3
text: Have a plan of action

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Defensive Driving · item 4

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Safety Belts · ¶1
text: The driver and all passengers, regardless of age, in a passenger vehicle are required to use safety belts if occupying a seat in a vehicle equipped with a safety belt. Any child under 8 years old must be secured in a federally approved child car seat if occupying a seat in a vehicle equipped with a safety belt, unless the child is more than 4’9” tall.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Safety Belts · ¶2
text: Safety belt requirements include pickups, SUVs, and trucks. Safety belts help keep you:

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Safety Belts › Penalties for Driving Without a Safety Belt · ¶1
text: A driver can receive a citation for not wearing his/her safety belt and for not having each child under the age of 17 in a safety seat or safety belt. Anyone who is at least 15 years of age can receive a citation for not wearing a safety belt. There are no exemptions to the safety belt laws. However, there are some defenses to prosecution for postal workers, individuals who deliver the newspaper, utility workers, solid waste truck workers, certain commercial farm vehicle operators, or medical reasons with a physician’s note.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › When Stopped by Law Enforcement · ¶1
text: If you are stopped by law enforcement, it is suggested you:

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › When Stopped by Law Enforcement · item 1
text: Slow down and move the vehicle safely to the right of the road.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › When Stopped by Law Enforcement · item 2
text: Park your vehicle as far to the right of the main traffic lane as possible. If available, park on the right shoulder or, if unavailable, park on a nearby well-lighted side street or parking lot away from high volume traffic.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › When Stopped by Law Enforcement · item 3
text: Place the vehicle in a parking position, set the emergency brake, turn the engine off, and activate the hazard warning lights.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › When Stopped by Law Enforcement · item 4
text: If at night, turn on the interior dome light.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › When Stopped by Law Enforcement · item 5
text: Remain in the car, lower the driver’s window if you feel safe to do so. Keep both hands clearly in sight on top of the steering wheel. Wait for the law enforcement officer to give you instructions. An officer may approach from either side of the vehicle.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › When Stopped by Law Enforcement · item 6
text: Tell the officer if you are transporting any type of weapon.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › When Stopped by Law Enforcement · item 7
text: Before reaching into your glove box or under the seat to retrieve your proof of insurance or driver’s license, inform the officer of where the items are located and follow the officer’s directions.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › When Stopped by Law Enforcement · item 8
text: If asked to exit the vehicle, check for passing vehicles to exit safely.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › When Stopped by Law Enforcement · item 9
text: Advise passengers to remain in the car unless other instructions are given by the law enforcement officer, and

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › When Stopped by Law Enforcement · item 10
text: At the conclusion of the traffic stop, give the appropriate signals and safely return to the proper lane of traffic when released by the law enforcement officer.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › When Stopped by Law Enforcement › Obligations, Responsibilities, Courtesy and Safety · ¶1
text: State law requires a driver to immediately stop when approached by an authorized emergency vehicle and you may be arrested if you do not stop immediately. If you feel the area is unsafe to stop immediately or if you have concerns the vehicle is not a real police vehicle, you can take the following steps to minimize the risk of being arrested or charges being filed against you: turn on your hazard lights and drive slowly and carefully below the posted speed limit; you may call 9-1-1 and remain on the phone with the operator while you stop and verify the officer’s identity; you may drive to a nearby well-lighted, populated place to stop. It is important to understand that law enforcement jurisdictions overlap and a local 9-1-1 call center operator may not be able to immediately determine what officer is working in that area at that time. If you stop in an unsafe location, such as on a bridge or a high traffic roadway, an officer may direct you over the public address speaker to move to a safer location. Follow the officer’s directions.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › When Stopped by Law Enforcement › Obligations, Responsibilities, Courtesy and Safety · ¶2
text: Law enforcement officers, drivers, and passengers should respond with courtesy during traffic stops and other officer/citizen interactions. Drivers and passengers should not exit the vehicle unless asked to do so. Exiting your vehicle may be perceived as aggressive behavior and a threat to the officer’s safety. Drivers and passengers inside a vehicle should not attempt to reach, dig, or search for their license or insurance documents before or while an officer is approaching. Drivers who transport handguns in their vehicles are encouraged to keep them in a separate location from license and insurance documentation.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › When Stopped by Law Enforcement › Obligations, Responsibilities, Courtesy and Safety · ¶3
text: During a traffic stop, the driver and any passengers are subjected to an investigative detention, which may only last for a reasonable amount of time. Passengers can ask the officer if they are free to leave and do so if the officer agrees. Law enforcement may ask questions during this time. You cannot be punished for refusing to answer questions; however, drivers are required by law to display a driver license when requested by an officer. If you are lawfully arrested, you are also required to give your name, residence address, and date of birth. A driver or a passenger who gives law enforcement a false or fraudulent identity or false answers may be arrested. It may be to your benefit to speak to law enforcement, such as to convey the reason you may have an emergency or for the driver to provide the officer your name, address and date of birth if you do not have your driver license with you.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › When Stopped by Law Enforcement › Obligations, Responsibilities, Courtesy and Safety · ¶4
text: Law enforcement may also ask for consent to search your vehicle or person. You may grant or deny the request to search; however, if an officer has probable cause to believe that your vehicle contains evidence of a crime, it can be searched without your consent. If an officer reasonably believes that you have a weapon, the officer can conduct a pat down search of your person and the immediate area around you, including areas of your vehicle. It is unlawful to physically resist a search, but you have the right to notify the officer that you do not consent to any search.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › When Stopped by Law Enforcement › Complaints or Concerns · ¶1
text: If you believe an officer has acted inappropriately during a traffic stop or other encounter, you should report that conduct to the officer’s superiors and follow agency guidelines for submitting complaints against officers as soon as possible. Officers will normally provide their names and badge numbers on request, when practical. Due to the overlapping of jurisdictions, drivers should make sure they identify the correct agency as well as any identifying aspects of the officer and law enforcement vehicle.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › When Stopped by Law Enforcement › Complaints or Concerns · ¶2
text: Drivers should refrain from arguing the validity of a charge during the traffic stop or detention. Signing a citation is not admitting guilt. It simply confirms your promise to pay the fine or contact the court. If you do not agree with the charge brought against you and wish to contest it, you should argue your case before a judge or request a jury trial and acquire the services of an attorney to represent you.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › When Stopped by Law Enforcement › False Identification Offense · ¶1
text: A person commits an offense if he/she gives a false or fictitious name to a law enforcement officer who has lawfully arrested or detained the person.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › When Stopped by Law Enforcement › Evading arrest or detention · ¶1
text: A person commits an offense if he intentionally flees from a person he knows is a peace officer or federal special investigator attempting to lawfully arrest or detain him/her. You will be subject to higher penalties if you use a vehicle or watercraft while evading arrest or cause injury to another person.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Road Rage · ¶1
text: Each year, road rage, also referred to as aggressive driving, causes hundreds of injuries and deaths. Aggressive driving occurs when a driver becomes angry or irritated and as a result, fails to follow the rules of the road. An aggressive driver will intentionally aggravate or attempt to aggravate other drivers and in some cases cause bodily injury, property damage, or death to others.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Road Rage › Tips to Avoid Road Rage · item 1
text: Plan your trip or schedule in advance. Allow extra time in case your vehicle breaks down or you encounter traffic congestion due to a crash, road construction, or rush-hour traffic.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Road Rage › Tips to Avoid Road Rage · item 2
text: When caught in traffic, do not get angry. Try to relax and listen to music you enjoy. Remember, traffic congestion is usually temporary and you will soon be on your way.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Road Rage › Tips to Avoid Road Rage · item 3
text: Should you need to use the horn, tap the horn; do not hold down the horn. Do not confront other drivers or make obscene gestures.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Road Rage › Tips to Avoid Road Rage · item 4
text: Do not cut into another driver’s lane of traffic. Properly signal your intentions to change lanes and change lanes when it is safe to do so. Turn your turn signal off after you complete your lane change.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Road Rage › Tips to Avoid Road Rage · item 5
text: Do not intentionally slow down, slam on your brakes, or speed up to keep someone from passing or entering your lane of travel.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Road Rage › Tips to Avoid Road Rage · item 6
text: Do not tailgate; follow at a safe distance.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Road Rage › Tips to Avoid Road Rage · item 7
text: Always remember to drive friendly and report aggressive driving to the local authorities.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Neighborhood Electronic Vehicles and Motor Assisted Scooters · ¶1
text: A neighborhood electronic vehicle is defined as a vehicle subject to Federal Motor Safety Standard 500 with a top speed of 35 mph on a paved level surface.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Neighborhood Electronic Vehicles and Motor Assisted Scooters · ¶2
text: A motor assisted scooter is defined as a self-propelled device with:

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Neighborhood Electronic Vehicles and Motor Assisted Scooters · item 1
text: At least two wheels in contact with the ground

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Neighborhood Electronic Vehicles and Motor Assisted Scooters · item 2
text: A braking system capable of stopping the device under normal operating conditions

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Neighborhood Electronic Vehicles and Motor Assisted Scooters · item 3
text: A gas or electric motor not exceeding 40 cc

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Neighborhood Electronic Vehicles and Motor Assisted Scooters · item 4
text: A deck designed to allow a person to stand or sit while operating the device, and

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Neighborhood Electronic Vehicles and Motor Assisted Scooters · item 5
text: The ability to be propelled by human power alone

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Neighborhood Electronic Vehicles and Motor Assisted Scooters · ¶3
text: Both vehicles may only be operated on a street or highway when the posted speed limit is 45 mph or less for a neighborhood electronic vehicle and 35 mph or less for a motor assisted scooter.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Neighborhood Electronic Vehicles and Motor Assisted Scooters › Electronic Personal Assistive Mobility Devices (EPAMD) · ¶1
text: EPAMD’s, such as a Segway, is defined as a two, non-tandem wheeled device designed for transporting one person that is self-balancing and propelled by an electric propulsion system with an average power of 750 watts or one horsepower.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Neighborhood Electronic Vehicles and Motor Assisted Scooters › Electronic Personal Assistive Mobility Devices (EPAMD) · ¶2
text: Special Note: Counties and municipalities may prohibit the operation of either type of vehicle on any street or highway for safety reasons.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Neighborhood Electronic Vehicles and Motor Assisted Scooters › Electronic Personal Assistive Mobility Devices (EPAMD) · ¶3
text: An EPAMD may be operated on:

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Neighborhood Electronic Vehicles and Motor Assisted Scooters › Electronic Personal Assistive Mobility Devices (EPAMD) · item 1
text: A sidewalk

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Neighborhood Electronic Vehicles and Motor Assisted Scooters › Electronic Personal Assistive Mobility Devices (EPAMD) · item 2
text: A path set aside for the exclusive operation of a bicycle

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Neighborhood Electronic Vehicles and Motor Assisted Scooters › Electronic Personal Assistive Mobility Devices (EPAMD) · item 3
text: On a residential street, road, or public highway with a maximum speed limit of 30 mph only:

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Neighborhood Electronic Vehicles and Motor Assisted Scooters › Electronic Personal Assistive Mobility Devices (EPAMD) · item 4
text: While making a direct crossing of a highway in a marked or unmarked crosswalk

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Neighborhood Electronic Vehicles and Motor Assisted Scooters › Electronic Personal Assistive Mobility Devices (EPAMD) · item 5
text: Where no sidewalk is available, or

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Neighborhood Electronic Vehicles and Motor Assisted Scooters › Electronic Personal Assistive Mobility Devices (EPAMD) · item 6
text: When so directed by a traffic control device or law enforcement officer

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Neighborhood Electronic Vehicles and Motor Assisted Scooters › Electronic Personal Assistive Mobility Devices (EPAMD) · ¶4
text: When operated on a public roadway, an EPAMD shall be ridden as close as practicable to the right-hand edge.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Transporting Cargo and Materials · ¶1
text: To prevent cargo or loose materials from falling or spilling from a car, truck, trailer, etc. onto the road and causing a crash or damage to the roads, drivers must comply with certain state requirements.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Transporting Cargo and Materials · ¶2
text: A vehicle must be equipped and maintained to prevent loose material from escaping by blowing or spilling and a vehicle bed must:

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Transporting Cargo and Materials · item 1
text: Not have a hole, crack, or other opening through which loose material can escape

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Transporting Cargo and Materials · item 2
text: Be enclosed by side panels and on the front by a panel or the vehicle cab

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Transporting Cargo and Materials · item 3
text: Be enclosed by a securely closed tailgate or panel on the rear to prevent spillage

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Transporting Cargo and Materials · item 4
text: Cover the load securely at the front and back of the load, unless completely enclosed in a compartment or the load does not blow or spill over the load carrying compartment.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Transporting Cargo and Materials · ¶3
text: No person shall load or transport any loose material on or over the public highways, such as dirt, sand, gravel, wood chips, or other material (except agricultural products in their natural state), capable of blowing or spilling from a vehicle unless:

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Transporting Cargo and Materials · item 5
text: The bed carrying the load is completely enclosed on both sides and on the front and rear by a tailgate, board or panel; and all must be so constructed as to prevent the escape of any part of the load by blowing or spilling; and

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Transporting Cargo and Materials · item 6
text: The top of the load is covered with a canvas, tarpaulin, or other covering firmly secured to the front and back to prevent the escape of the load because of blowing or spilling. This requirement does not apply to:

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Transporting Cargo and Materials · item 7
text: Any load-carrying compartment that completely encloses the load; or

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Transporting Cargo and Materials · item 8
text: The transporting of any load of loose materials not blowing or spilling over the top of the load-carrying compartment.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Transporting Cargo and Materials › Safety Chains · ¶1
text: Safety chains are required when certain types of vehicles are towing trailers in order to prevent the trailer from breaking loose and causing a serious crash. A person may not drive a passenger car or light truck while towing a trailer, semi-trailer, or house trailer on a public highway in Texas unless safety chains are attached from a trailer, semi-trailer, or house trailer to the towing vehicle. The types of safety chains and the manner of attachment must be approved by DPS. The requirements of this law do not apply to a passenger car or light truck towing a trailer or semi-trailer used for agricultural purposes or to any trailer or semi-trailer or house trailer operated in compliance with the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Transporting Cargo and Materials › Towing · ¶1
text: When one vehicle is towing another, the drawbar, chain, rope, cable, or other connection must:

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Transporting Cargo and Materials › Towing · item 1
text: Not be longer than 15 feet from one vehicle to another

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Transporting Cargo and Materials › Towing · item 2
text: Be strong enough to pull all weight drawn

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Transporting Cargo and Materials › Towing · item 3
text: Attach a white flag not less than 12 inches square

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Transporting Cargo and Materials › Towing · item 4
text: Not tow more than three vehicles attached to it by mounting the front wheels of trailing vehicles on the bed of another vehicle and leaving only the rear wheels in contact with the roadway

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Transporting Cargo and Materials › Towing · ¶2
text: This limit does not apply to trailers transporting poles, pipes, machinery, or other structures that cannot be easily dismembered.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Carbon Monoxide · ¶1
text: Beware of carbon monoxide poisoning. Cars produce carbon monoxide, which is a deadly gas. Make sure you are getting plenty of fresh air.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Carbon Monoxide › Don’t: · item 1
text: Leave the motor running in a garage

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Carbon Monoxide › Don’t: · item 2
text: Leave vents open when following closely behind another car

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Carbon Monoxide › Don’t: · item 3
text: Leave the motor running and the windows closed while the car is parked

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Carbon Monoxide › Don’t: · item 4
text: Drive with a defective muffler or exhaust system

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Carbon Monoxide › Don’t: · item 5
text: Use the heater or air conditioner in a parked car with the windows closed in an enclosed space

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Carbon Monoxide › Don’t: · ¶1
text: If you encounter a carbon monoxide poisoning victim, move them to fresh air and call 911.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Carbon Monoxide › Don’t: · ¶2
text: As a driver, you should know all the safety and operational features of the vehicle you are driving. Make sure you and your passengers are traveling in a vehicle that is safe and in good working order. Drive safely and obey all criminal and traffic laws.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Driving with Disability Program · ¶1
text: Communication Impediment with a Peace Officer is an optional restriction code offered on Texas State ID and Driver License for those wanting to alert law enforcement of a challenge with communication. Physician signed form required.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Driving with Disability Program · ¶2
text: If you want to place the code for “Communication Impediment with a Peace Officer” on your Texas ID or driver license, ask your doctor to complete form DL-101 https://www.dps.texas.gov/internetforms/Forms/DL-101.pdf and present it at the driver license office. The code will go on the back of your license, similar to other codes like organ donor or corrective lenses.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Driving with Disability Program · ¶3
text: The option for disclosure of a communication disability/impediment when registering a vehicle through the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles is also available, the communication impediment will then be privately placed in the Texas Law Enforcement Telecommunication System (TLETS) thus alerting the officer of the challenge PRIOR to approaching the vehicle in a pull-over scenario. Form VTR-216 https://www.txdmv.gov/sites/default/files/form_files/VTR-216.pdf must be completed by a licensed physician if the applicant has a physical health condition or a licensed physician, licensed psychologist, or a non-physician mental health professional if the applicant has a mental health condition. Present this form when you register your vehicle with Texas DMV.

locator: Chapter 14: Additional Safety Tips › Driving with Disability Program · ¶4
text: For more information on Driving with Disability Program please visit: Texas Driving with Disability | Office of the Texas Governor | Greg Abbott https://gov.texas.gov/organization/disabilities/texas-driving-with-disability

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Vehicle Inspection · ¶1
text: All motor vehicles registered in Texas must be inspected each year at an official motor vehicle inspection station. This includes motorcycles, mopeds, scooters, and autocycles. Evidence of financial responsibility for the vehicle being inspected must be presented at the time of the inspection.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Vehicle Inspection · ¶2
text: The Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) and the Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS) transitioned to a new vehicle inspection and registration system requiring motorists to display only the valid registration sticker on the windshield. The sticker serves as combined proof of registration and inspection.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Vehicle Inspection · ¶3
text: When a vehicle passes inspection, the inspection station will print the passing Vehicle Inspection Report (VIR) and enter the information into an electronic database. The DMV verifies the database information at the time your vehicle is registered. You should still be prepared to present the printed VIR when registering your vehicle. The VIR is only valid for 90 days from the month of inspection for registration purposes.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Required Equipment for Vehicles · ¶1
text: You must have the following equipment in proper working order for your car to be considered safe.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Required Equipment for Vehicles · row 1
text: Brakes | 1. Foot Brake - Must stop car within a distance of 25 feet at a speed of 20 mph. 2. Parking Brake - Should be adequate to stop and hold car.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Required Equipment for Vehicles · row 2
text: Lights | 1. Two Headlights (one on each side of the front) - A beam indicator showing when the high headlight beam is on. 2. Taillights - All vehicles must be equipped with two taillights. Exception: Cars manufactured before 1960 are only required to have one taillight. 3. Brake (Stop) Lights - All vehicles must have two (2) working brake lights. Exception: Cars manufactured before 1960 are only required to have one (1) brake light. Vehicles equipped with a third or high mounted stop lamp require all three to be operational. 4. License Plate Light- A white light that lights the rear license plate when the headlights (or auxiliary lamps) are lighted. 5. Parking Lights - White or amber on the front, red to the rear (may be combined with other lights). 6. Reflectors - Two red reflectors, one on each side of the car (may be combined with taillights) must be placed at a height of 15 to 60 inches and be visible up to 600 feet; visible up to 350 feet on vehicles manufactured before 1960. 7. Turn Signals - Every motor vehicle, trailer, semi-trailer, and pole-trailer must have electric turn signals (except motorcycles and certain trailers). Exception: Passenger cars and trucks less than 80 inches in width and manufactured before 1960 are not required to have electrical turn signals.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Required Equipment for Vehicles · row 3
text: Horns | Horns must be heard for a minimum distance of 200 feet.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Required Equipment for Vehicles · row 4
text: Muffler and exhaust system | All 1968 or later models must be equipped with an exhaust emission system to help reduce air pollution.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Required Equipment for Vehicles · row 5
text: Safety glass | New cars must be equipped with safety glass. Replacements of glass for any car must be with safety glass.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Required Equipment for Vehicles · row 6
text: License plates | Vehicles must have one valid plate affixed to the front and one at the rear of passenger and commercial vehicles, in the manner prescribed by law, except dealer and commercial vehicles that are only issued one license plate.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Required Equipment for Vehicles · row 7
text: Windshield wiper | Windshield wipers are necessary for safety in bad weather.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Required Equipment for Vehicles · row 8
text: Rearview mirror | A rearview mirror must be able to reflect a view of the highway for a distance of at least 200 feet to the rear of the vehicle.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Required Equipment for Vehicles · row 9
text: Slow moving vehicle emblem | Farm tractors and machinery, road construction machinery, animal-drawn vehicles and certain other motor vehicles assigned to travel at 25 mph or less must display the slow-moving vehicle emblem.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Required Equipment for Vehicles · row 10
text: Front safety belts | Front safety belts are required if safety belt anchorages were part of the original equipment of the vehicle.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Required Equipment for Vehicles · row 11
text: Tires | All vehicles are required to have tires in proper and safe condition with a minimum depth of 2/32 of an inch.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Required Equipment for Vehicles · row 12
text: Fuel cap | The fuel cap on gasoline-powered vehicles from 2 to 24 years old will be checked to determine if the fuel cap is missing or defective. Exception: Antique vehicles, circus vehicles, slow moving vehicles, motorcycles, and vehicles operated exclusively by a fuel other than gasoline and vehicles newer than 2 years or older than 24 years.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Required Equipment for Vehicles · ¶2
text: For information on commercial vehicles, please see the special requirements section in the Texas Commercial Motor Vehicle Driver Handbook .

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Equipment You Must Not Have · ¶1
text: The following equipment is considered unsafe and is not allowed on your vehicle:

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Equipment You Must Not Have · item 1
text: A red light showing from the front except on an emergency vehicle.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Equipment You Must Not Have · item 2
text: A bell, siren, or exhaust whistle except on an emergency vehicle.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Equipment You Must Not Have · item 3
text: A muffler cutout.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Equipment You Must Not Have · item 4
text: Anything extending more than three inches beyond the left side or six inches beyond the right side of the body, running board, or fenders of your car.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Equipment You Must Not Have · item 5
text: Flashing red lights on the front except on emergency vehicles, school buses, and church buses.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Equipment You Must Not Have · item 6
text: A radar interference device designed, manufactured, used, or intended to be used to interfere with, scramble, disrupt, or cause to malfunction a radar or laser device used to measure a vehicle’s speed.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Equipment You Must Not Have › Minimum Road Clearance · ¶1
text: A vehicle must not be modified or weighted in such a manner where the body is below the lowest part of the rims of the wheels.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Optional Equipment for Vehicles · ¶1
text: The following equipment is considered optional and is not required to be on your vehicle.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Optional Equipment for Vehicles · row 1
text: Spotlight | Spotlights must be turned off for a vehicle approaching from the opposite direction. If headlights fail, it may be used with the beam striking the road not more than 50 feet in front of the vehicle on which it is used.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Optional Equipment for Vehicles · row 2
text: Side cowl or fender light | Two of these types of lights are permitted; must show amber or white light without glare.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Optional Equipment for Vehicles · row 3
text: Running board courtesy lights | One running board courtesy light is permitted on each side; must show amber or white light without a glare.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Optional Equipment for Vehicles · row 4
text: Backup lights | Two backup lights are permitted separately or in combination with other lights. Do not use when vehicle is in forward motion.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Optional Equipment for Vehicles · row 5
text: Flashing lights | Widespread flashing lights may be used on any vehicle to warn of unusual traffic hazards; must show flashing amber or white to the front and flashing amber or red to the rear and must flash simultaneously.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Optional Equipment for Vehicles · row 6
text: Additional lights | Any motor vehicle may have up to three additional driving lights mounted on the front, not less than 12 inches but not more than 42 inches from the road surface.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Optional Equipment for Vehicles · row 7
text: Sunscreen or window tinting | If sunscreen or window tinting is used, it must comply with the appropriate state regulations for your vehicle make and model.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Registration of Vehicles · ¶1
text: All vehicles must be registered in the owner’s county of residency. Once the vehicle is properly registered, a registration sticker will be issued that must be displayed on the vehicle’s windshield or on the rear license plate of a motorcycle or moped.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Registration of Vehicles · item 1
text: An owner must register a newly purchased vehicle within 30 days of purchase.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Registration of Vehicles · item 2
text: Nonresident truck owners may be issued 30-day temporary registration permits for certain movements of farm products and machinery during harvesting season.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Registration of Vehicles · item 3
text: Under certain conditions, temporary registration permits and reduced registration rates for special vehicles may be obtained.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Registration of Vehicles · item 4
text: Buyers’ temporary tags are recognized for 60 days; dealers’ metal registration plates may be used on any dealer-owned vehicle except for commercial purposes (vehicle inspection is required).

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Registration of Vehicles · item 5
text: A manufacturer’s metal registration plate may be used for vehicle testing purposes only; a vehicle inspection is required. Dealers temporary cardboard tags may be used for demonstrating a vehicle for sale, or for transporting or servicing vehicles without a motor vehicle inspection. These vehicles may not be used for driver license driving exams.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Registration of Vehicles · item 6
text: Farm registered vehicles, in addition to use for farm and ranch purposes, may be used as a means of passenger transportation for members of the family to attend church or school, to visit doctors for medical treatment or supplies, or for other necessities of the home or family. Farm registered vehicles may not be used for gainful employment.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Registration of Vehicles · item 7
text: For registration applications and detailed information, consult your County Tax Assessor-Collector or the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV).

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Registration of Vehicles › Vehicles Not Required to be Registered or Inspected · ¶1
text: The following vehicles are not required to be registered, inspected, or to display a license plate when temporarily operated on highways:

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Registration of Vehicles › Vehicles Not Required to be Registered or Inspected · item 1
text: Farm tractors

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Registration of Vehicles › Vehicles Not Required to be Registered or Inspected · item 2
text: Farm trailers, farm semi-trailers, and certain fertilizer and cottonseed trailers with a gross weight of 4,000 lbs. or less

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Registration of Vehicles › Vehicles Not Required to be Registered or Inspected · item 3
text: Implements of agriculture

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Registration of Vehicles › Vehicles Not Required to be Registered or Inspected · item 4
text: Power sweepers

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Registration of Vehicles › Vehicles Not Required to be Registered or Inspected · item 5
text: Certain golf carts

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Registration of Vehicles › Vehicles Not Required to be Registered or Inspected · item 6
text: Electric bicycles

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Registration of Vehicles › Vehicles Not Required to be Registered or Inspected · item 7
text: Motorized and electric personal assistive mobility devices

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Registration of Vehicles › Vehicles Not Required to be Registered or Inspected · ¶2
text: When temporarily operated on highways, the following vehicles are not required to be registered or inspected if the owner annually secures a distinguishing $5 license plate and complies with other special conditions in the law:

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Registration of Vehicles › Vehicles Not Required to be Registered or Inspected · item 8
text: Machinery for drilling water wells and construction machinery.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Registration of Vehicles › Vehicles Not Required to be Registered or Inspected · item 9
text: Farm trailers, farm semi-trailers, cotton trailers, cottonseed trailers, and certain fertilizer trailers weighing over 4,000 lbs. but less than 34,000 lbs gross.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Registration of Vehicles › Vehicle Registration for New and Nonresidents of Texas · ¶1
text: A new Texas resident must register every vehicle he/she owns before applying for a Texas driver license.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Registration of Vehicles › Vehicle Registration for New and Nonresidents of Texas · ¶2
text: When a nonresident establishes residency in Texas or enters into gainful employment, his/her vehicle may be operated for 30 days. After 30 days, the vehicle must be registered in Texas.

locator: Chapter 2: Vehicle Inspection and Registration › Registration of Vehicles › Vehicle Registration for New and Nonresidents of Texas · ¶3
text: New residents registering a vehicle must obtain a Texas vehicle inspection report and verification of the vehicle identification number (VIN) by a state-approved vehicle inspection station prior to registration. The vehicle owner will then be provided the necessary form for processing the vehicle registration. Evidence of financial responsibility for the vehicle being registered must be presented at the time of registration. If evidence of financial responsibility is not presented, the vehicle cannot be registered. The registration receipt issued by the county tax assessor-collector for each vehicle will be acceptable proof of the registration when applying for a Texas driver license.

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › The Liability Insurance Law · ¶1
text: The Texas Motor Vehicle Safety Responsibility Act was enacted to ensure all drivers are financially responsible for the death, injury, or property damage they may cause while operating a motor vehicle. All owners and/or operators of motor vehicles in Texas must have at least the minimum amount of liability insurance.

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › The Liability Insurance Law · ¶2
text: As of January 1, 2011, the minimum amount of liability insurance is:

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › The Liability Insurance Law · item 1
text: $30,000 against injury or death of one person

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › The Liability Insurance Law · item 2
text: $60,000 against injury or death of two or more individuals

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › The Liability Insurance Law · item 3
text: $25,000 against property damage

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › The Liability Insurance Law · ¶3
text: To comply with the Texas Motor Vehicle Safety Responsibility Act , a driver, unless exempt, must maintain liability insurance or be self-insured under the provisions of the Act. Evidence of financial responsibility must be presented at the time a person applies for a driver license, registers a motor vehicle, or obtains a motor vehicle inspection report.

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › The Liability Insurance Law · ¶4
text: Every owner or operator of a motor vehicle in Texas is required to furnish evidence of financial responsibility to a law enforcement officer upon request or to another person involved in a crash.

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › Evidence of Financial Responsibility · ¶1
text: The following list includes items that will be accepted as evidence of financial responsibility.

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › Evidence of Financial Responsibility · item 1
text: A liability insurance policy in at least the minimum amounts.

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › Evidence of Financial Responsibility · item 2
text: A standard proof of liability insurance form prescribed by the Texas Department of Insurance and issued by a liability insurer that includes the:

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › Evidence of Financial Responsibility · item 3
text: Name of the insurer, insurance policy number, and policy period;

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › Evidence of Financial Responsibility · item 4
text: Name and address of each insured;

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › Evidence of Financial Responsibility · item 5
text: Policy limits or a statement the coverage of the policy complies with at least the minimum amounts of liability insurance required by this Act; and

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › Evidence of Financial Responsibility · item 6
text: The make and model of each covered vehicle.

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › Evidence of Financial Responsibility · item 7
text: An insurance binder indicating the owner and/or operator is in compliance.

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › Evidence of Financial Responsibility · item 8
text: A certificate issued by the state comptroller showing the owner of the vehicle has on deposit with the comptroller, money or securities for at least $55,000.

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › Evidence of Financial Responsibility · item 9
text: A surety bond issued by DPS showing the vehicle has a bond on file with DPS.

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › Evidence of Financial Responsibility · item 10
text: A certificate or copy of a certificate issued by the county judge of a county in which the vehicle is registered that shows the owner of the vehicle has on deposit with the county judge, cash or a cashier’s check for at least $55,000.

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › Evidence of Financial Responsibility · item 11
text: A certificate or copy of a certificate of self-insurance, issued by DPS, which shows the person has more than 25 vehicles registered in his/her name.

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › Evidence of Financial Responsibility · item 12
text: An image displayed on a wireless communication device that includes the information required in a standard insurance form.

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › Failure to Provide Evidence of Financial Responsibility · ¶1
text: If an individual fails to provide evidence of financial responsibility when required, he/she may receive a citation. The court may dismiss the charge if the individual provides evidence that a liability insurance policy was in effect when the citation was issued.

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › Failure to Provide Evidence of Financial Responsibility · ¶2
text: Upon conviction of driving a motor vehicle without sufficient evidence of financial responsibility as required, a driver is subject to penalties.

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › Failure to Provide Evidence of Financial Responsibility · row 1
text: 1st conviction | A fine of $175 to $350.

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › Failure to Provide Evidence of Financial Responsibility · row 2
text: 2nd conviction and each subsequent conviction | Suspension of driver license, a fine of $350 to $1,000, and court-impoundment of the motor vehicle driven or operated by the person at the time of the offense provided the defendant was an owner of the vehicle at the time of the offense and is an owner of the vehicle on the date of conviction. The vehicle shall be impounded for 180 days. Before the court orders the release of the vehicle, evidence of financial responsibility must be presented to the court.

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › Failure to Provide Evidence of Financial Responsibility · ¶3
text: The vehicle registration, license or driving privilege of a driver will be suspended:

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › Failure to Provide Evidence of Financial Responsibility · item 1
text: Upon conviction of a traffic violation that requires a suspension of a driver license, unless evidence of insurance is presented to DPS;

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › Failure to Provide Evidence of Financial Responsibility · item 2
text: If a judgment resulting from a crash has not been satisfied within 60 days of the judgment;

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › Failure to Provide Evidence of Financial Responsibility · item 3
text: If an installment agreement arising out of a settlement of a crash is in default;

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › Failure to Provide Evidence of Financial Responsibility · item 4
text: If, while uninsured, the individual was involved in a crash in which another person was killed, injured, or there was at least $1,000 damage to a person’s property and there exists a reasonable probability of a judgment being rendered against the driver; and

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › Failure to Provide Evidence of Financial Responsibility · item 5
text: When required to maintain evidence of financial responsibility for two years from the most recent conviction date. More specific information about compliance with the Texas Motor Vehicle Safety Responsibility Act may be found online at https://www.dps.texas.gov/section/driver-license/financial-responsibility-insurance-certificate-sr-22 . You may also write to:

locator: Chapter 3: Safety Responsibility › Failure to Provide Evidence of Financial Responsibility · ¶4
text: Mailing Address: Texas Department of Public Safety Enforcement and Compliance Service PO Box 4087 Austin, TX 78773-0320

locator: Chapter 4: Right-of-Way › Intro · ¶1
text: At times, a driver must yield to others. There are certain rules to help determine who has the right-of-way; however, if the other driver doesn’t follow these rules, give him/her the right-of-way. Remember, in every situation, right-of-way is something given, not taken. All drivers should know and understand the laws that determine who has the right-of-way.

locator: Chapter 4: Right-of-Way › Intro · row 1
text: Driver commits any traffic offense of which failure to yield the right-of-way to another vehicle is an element and causes bodily injury to another. | A fine of $500 to $2,000.

locator: Chapter 4: Right-of-Way › Intro · row 2
text: Driver causes serious bodily injury to another. | A fine of $1,000 to $4,000.

locator: Chapter 4: Right-of-Way › Right-of-Way at Intersections › Intersections Controlled by Signs and Signals · ¶1
text: When signs and signals control traffic at an intersection, you must obey them. Know the meaning of each sign and signal. See Chapter 5 for more information.

locator: Chapter 4: Right-of-Way › Right-of-Way at Intersections › Intersections Controlled by Signs and Signals · image
heading: Alt text: “Illustration in the handbook section “Intersections Controlled by Signs and Signals” (no caption in the PDF)”
text: Illustration in the handbook section “Intersections Controlled by Signs and Signals” (no caption in the PDF)

locator: Chapter 4: Right-of-Way › Right-of-Way at Intersections › Single or Two-Lane Road Intersecting a Multi-Lane Road · ¶1
text: If you are driving on a single or two lane road that intersects with a divided road or road with three (3) or more lanes, you must yield the right-of-way to vehicles traveling on the divided or three (3) or more lane road.

locator: Chapter 4: Right-of-Way › Right-of-Way at Intersections › Unpaved Road Intersecting a Paved Road · ¶1
text: If you are driving on an unpaved road that intersects with a paved road, you must yield the right-of-way to vehicles traveling on the paved road.

locator: Chapter 4: Right-of-Way › Right-of-Way at Intersections › Intersections Not Controlled by Signs, Signals, Multi-Lanes, or Pavement · ¶1
text: When approaching this type of intersection, yield the right-of-way to any vehicle that has entered or is approaching the intersection on your right. If the road to your right is clear or if approaching vehicles are far enough from the intersection to make your crossing safe, you may proceed. Since there are not any traffic-controls at this intersection, make sure there are no approaching vehicles from the left. You may legally have the right-of-way but be sure the other driver yields to you before you proceed.

locator: Chapter 4: Right-of-Way › Right-of-Way at Intersections › Intersections Not Controlled by Signs, Signals, Multi-Lanes, or Pavement · image
heading: Alt text: “Illustration in the handbook section “Intersections Not Controlled by Signs, Signals, Multi-Lanes, or Pavement” (no caption in the PDF)”
text: Illustration in the handbook section “Intersections Not Controlled by Signs, Signals, Multi-Lanes, or Pavement” (no caption in the PDF)

locator: Chapter 4: Right-of-Way › Right-of-Way at Intersections › Turning Left · ¶1
text: When turning left, always yield the right-of-way to any vehicle coming straight through from the other direction.

locator: Chapter 4: Right-of-Way › Right-of-Way at Intersections › Turning Left · image
heading: Alt text: “Illustration in the handbook section “Turning Left” (no caption in the PDF)”
text: Illustration in the handbook section “Turning Left” (no caption in the PDF)

locator: Chapter 4: Right-of-Way › Right-of-Way at Intersections › Private Roads and Driveways · ¶1
text: When entering or crossing a road, street, or highway from a private road, alley, building, or driveway, you must stop prior to the sidewalk and yield the right-of-way to all approaching vehicles and pedestrians.

locator: Chapter 4: Right-of-Way › Right-of-Way at Intersections › T-Intersection · ¶1
text: When approaching an intersection of a through street traveling from a street that ends at the intersection, you must stop and yield the right-of-way to vehicles on the through street.

locator: Chapter 4: Right-of-Way › Right-of-Way at Intersections › T-Intersection · image
heading: Alt text: “Illustration in the handbook section “T-Intersection” (no caption in the PDF)”
text: Illustration in the handbook section “T-Intersection” (no caption in the PDF)

locator: Chapter 4: Right-of-Way › Right-of-Way at Intersections › Enter or Leave Controlled-Access Highway · ¶1
text: The driver traveling on a frontage road of a controlled-access highway must yield the right-of-way to a vehicle:

locator: Chapter 4: Right-of-Way › Right-of-Way at Intersections › Enter or Leave Controlled-Access Highway · item 1
text: Entering or about to enter the frontage road from the highway; and

locator: Chapter 4: Right-of-Way › Right-of-Way at Intersections › Enter or Leave Controlled-Access Highway · item 2
text: Leaving or about to leave the frontage road to enter the highway.

locator: Chapter 4: Right-of-Way › Right-of-Way at Intersections › Enter or Leave Controlled-Access Highway · image

heading: TWO-WAY FRONTAGE ROAD · YIELD | Alt text: “TWO-WAY FRONTAGE ROAD · YIELD”
text: TWO-WAY FRONTAGE ROAD · YIELD

locator: Chapter 4: Right-of-Way › Right-of-Way at Intersections › Driving on Multiple-Lane Roads · ¶1
text: On a road divided into three or more lanes with traffic moving in the same direction, a vehicle entering a lane of traffic from the right must yield the right-of-way to a vehicle entering the same lane of traffic from the left .

locator: Chapter 4: Right-of-Way › Right-of-Way at Intersections › Driving on Multiple-Lane Roads · image
